Heritage Bridge Guidelines (Interim) - Jan 11 , 2008 24
文物桥指引(暂定)-2008 年 1 月 11 日 24
• 'The structural integrity, safety and condition of every bridge shall be determined
through the performance of at least one inspection every two years under the direction of a
professional engineer and in accordance with the Ontario Structure Inspection Manual, published by
the Ministry, as it may be amended from time to time ."
”每座桥梁的结构完整性、安全性和状况应在专业工程师的指导下，每两年至少进行
一次检查，并根据安大略省出版的《安大略省结构检查手册》确定，该手册可
能会不时修订”
MTO uses the biennial inspection information to plan for future maintenance and
rehabilitation treatments that the bridge may require throughout its life. The
preservation strategies used to ensure bridge safety and longevity, are well
documented in MTO's bridge management procedural documents and are also used
in the Ontario Bridge Management System. Whenever alteration, modification,
rehabilitation or replacement is planned for a Listed heritage bridge, the conservation
options described in Section 4 of these guidelines shall apply.
港口及航运局利用两年一次的检查资料，计划日后桥梁在使用期间可能需要进行的维
修及修复处理。用于确保桥梁安全和使用寿命的保护策略在 MTO 的桥梁管理程序文件
中有详细记录，也在安大略省桥梁管理系统中使用。无论何时计划对已列入清单的文
物桥梁进行改建、修改、修复或更换，本指南第 4 节所述的保护方案均应适用。
Ontario Regulation 104/97 Standards For Bridges under the Public Transportation
and Highway Improvement Act applies to all bridges and as a result, MTO must
ensure that listed heritage bridges are adequately maintained in between
rehabilitation cycles . Maintenance is fundamental to conservation and should be
undertaken to retain and preserve cultural heritage value . Listed bridges must not be
allowed to deteriorate to a state where future rehabilitation becomes prohibitive.
安大略省第 104/97 号条例《公共交通和公路改善法》下的桥梁标准适用于所有桥梁，
因此，市交通局必须确保所列文物桥梁在修复周期之间得到充分维护。维护是保护的
基础，应该保留和保护文化遗产的价值。不能允许列出的桥梁恶化到一个状态，在未
来的修复成为禁止。

Appendix B: Evaluation Criteria
附录 b: 评估准则
The followingscoringsystemwas developed to provide aclear and easilyunderstood system for evaluating
bridges for potential inclusion on theHeritage Bridge List. Thescoring, derived from Ontario
Regulation9/06, is divided into three mainareas: Design/ Physical Value, Contextual Value andHistoric I
Associative Value. Within these three divisions are further criteria that are individually scored. For the
purposes of these Guidelines, abridge with ascore of 60 or greater isconsidered provincially important.
开发以下评分系统是为了提供清晰易懂的评估桥梁可能被列入遗产桥梁名单的系统。评分来源于安大略省
9/06 号法规，分为三个主要领域: 设计/物理价值，上下文价值和历史 i 关联价值。在这三个部分是进一步
的标准，单独评分。为了这些指南的目的，60 分以上的缩写被认为是省级重要的。

Appendix C- Cultural Heritage Evaluation Report
附录 c-文化遗产评估报告
C1-General
C1-一般
A Cultural Heritage Evaluation Report examines a property as a whole, its relationship to its surroundings, as well
as its individual elements- engineering works, landscape and archaeological areas.
一份文化遗产评估报告审查一个财产作为一个整体，它与周围环境的关系，以及它的个别元素-工程工程，景观和考
古领域。
This report will include, but is not limited to:
这份报告将包括，但不限于:
• Historical Research, Site Analysis and Evaluation including Field Assessment,
‧历史研究、现场分析及评估，包括实地评估,
• Bridge form with scoring and evaluation,
桥梁形式与评分和评估,
•Description of Property, Statement of Cultural Heritage Value and a description of Heritage Attributes of the cultural heritage
resource (bridge, cultural heritage landscape, archaeological site, if any),
•物业说明、文化遗产价值说明及文化遗产资源(桥梁、文化遗产景观、考古遗址(如有的话)的文物属性说明;
• Images and supporting documentation.
•图片和辅助文件。
The quality of the report depends on a thorough understanding of the physical values of the property, a documentation of its
history through scholarly research,and an analysis of its social context. The author of the report relies on standard historical
techniques, such as site visits, public consultations, archival research,comparisons with similar properties and mapping.
报告的质量取决于对财产的实际价值的透彻理解，通过学术研究记录其历史，以及对其社会背景的分析。报告的作者依赖于标
准的历史技术，如实地考察，公众咨询，档案研究，与类似财产的比较和绘图。
The preparation of a Cultural Heritage Evaluation Report is the means by which a property is examined for its cultural
heritage value. The report is the main source used by MTO and MCL to determine whether a property is of cultural heritage
value. If a property is determined to be of cultural heritage value, the report serves as the foundation for the Statement of
Cultural Heritage Value and a Conservation Manual for the property. The report also functions as a background document for
property managers because it contains useful information about the history of the property and its individual assets.
文化遗产评估报告的准备是一个财产的文化遗产价值检查的手段。报告是 MTO 和 MCL 用来确定一个财产是否具有文化遗产价
值的主要来源。如果某物业被确定具有文化遗产价值，该报告将作为该物业的文化遗产价值声明和保护手册的基础。这份报告
也可以作为物业管理人员的背景文件，因为它包含了有关物业历史和个人资产的有用信息。
A Cultural Heritage Evaluation Report generally contains(but is not limited to) the following:
文化遗产评估报告一般包括(但不限于)以下内容:
1. Historical Research, Site Analysis and Evaluation
1. 历史研究、场地分析和评估
If the available identification and description of the importance and heritage attributes of the bridge and associated landscape
are inadequate for the purposes of the Cultural Heritage Evaluation Report or heritage impact assessment, or the cultural
heritage resource is newly identified, research, site survey and analysis, and evaluation are required. An explanation of the
methodology used must accompany a clear statement of the conclusions
若就文化遗产评估报告或文物影响评估而言，有关桥梁及相关景观的重要性及文物属性的现有识别及描述不足，或文化遗产资
源是新发现的，便须进行研究、实地调查及分析，以及进行评估。使用的方法的解释必须伴随着结论的清晰声明

regarding the cultural heritage value and heritage attributes of the bridge and associated landscape.
桥梁及相关景观的文化遗产价值及文物属性。
2. Description of Property, Statement of Cultural Heritage Value or Interest and description of Heritage
Attributes of the Bridge.
2. 物业描述、文化遗产价值或利益陈述及桥梁文物属性描述。
The Description of Property describes the general character of the property and identifies those aspects of the property to
which the listing applies. In addition to providing information so that the location of the property can be identified(i.e.municipal
address and neighborhood if appropriate), it should outline the principal resources that form part of the Listing(in this case, a
bridge) and identify any discernible boundaries. The Description of Property should be no longer than two or three sentences.
Property 的描述描述属性的一般特征，并标识应用清单的属性的那些方面。除了提供资料以确定物业的位置(如适用，即市政地
址及邻舍)外，它还应概述构成清单一部分的主要资源(在这种情况下是一座桥梁) ，并确定任何可辨别的边界。对财产的描述不
应该超过两到三句话。
The Statement of Cultural Heritage Value or Interest should convey why the property is important, explaining cultural
meanings, associations and connections the property holds for the community. This statement should reflect one of or more
of the evaluation criteria. The Statement should provide sufficient information to explain the significance of the property but
should be no longer that two or three paragraphs, explaining the core aspects of the property's cultural heritage value.
文化遗产价值或利益的陈述应该表达为什么财产是重要的，解释文化意义，协会和联系财产持有的社会。这份声明应该反映一
个或多个评估标准。声明应提供足够的信息，解释财产的重要性，但不应再是两三段，解释财产文化遗产价值的核心方面。
The Description of Heritage Attributes describes the key attributes or elements of the property that must be retained to
conserve its cultural heritage value or interest. Heritage attributes are those attributes(i.e. materials, forms, location and
spatial configurations) of the property, buildings and structures that contribute to the property's cultural heritage value or
interest, and which should be retained to conserve that value.
遗产属性的描述描述了为保存其文化遗产价值或利益而必须保留的财产的关键属性或要素。文物属性是指物业、建筑物及构筑
物的属性(即物料、形式、位置及空间配置) ，而这些属性对物业的文化遗产价值或利益有贡献，因此应予保留，以保存这些价
值。
For further information on this requirement, see pages 15 to 18 of MCL's Designating Heritage Properties(Ontario Heritage
Tool Kit)-http://www.culture.qov.on.ca/english/culdiv/heritage/Toolkit/DHP Eng.pdf
有关这项规定的进一步资料，请参阅管理委员会指定文物业的第 15 至 18 页(安大略省文物工具包)-http://
www.culture.qov.on.ca/chinese/culdiv/Heritage/toolkit/dhp Eng.pdf
3. Bridge form with scoring and evaluation
3. 有评分和评价的桥梁形式
In completing the bridge form, the Heritage Consultant will include a rationale for each scoring criterion. This is to make the
scoring transparent and understandable by those reviewing the report. The scoring criteria are included at Appendix B. A
template for a scoring form is included in Appendix B 1.
在完成桥梁形式，遗产顾问将包括每个评分标准的基本原理。这是为了让评分透明和可以理解的那些审查报告。评分标准包括
在附录 b 中。评分表单的模板包含在附录 b1 中。

4. 图像和辅助文件。

C2- Example of Statement of Cultural Heritage Value or Interest and Description of Heritage Attributes

1. Middle Road Bridge, City of Mississauga(adapted from the Canadian Register of Historic Places)
米西索加市中间路桥(改编自加拿大历史名胜名录)
Description of Property
财产描述
The Middle Road Bridge is located at the eastern terminus of Sherway Drive and spans the Etobicoke Creek,
which acts as a boundary between the City of Mississauga and the City of Toronto.
中间路桥位于 Sherway Drive 的东端，横跨 Etobicoke Creek，是米西索加市和多伦多市之间的边界。
Currently used as a pedestrian bridge, the Mississauga portion of the 4.3 metre wide and 26.1 metre long concrete truss
bridge is recognized for its heritage value by City of Mississauga Bylaw 1101-86.
这座 4.3 米宽、26.1 米长的混凝土桁架桥的米西索加部分目前用作行人天桥，因其具有遗产价值而得到米西索加市第 1101-86
号法律的认可。
The City of Toronto(formerly City of Etobicoke) portion of the bridge is recognized for its heritage value by(former) City of
Etobicoke Bylaw 1986-281.
多伦多市(前 Etobicoke 市)部分桥梁的遗产价值被(前) Etobicoke 市规章 1986-281 所认可。
Statement of Cultural Heritage Value or Interest The heritage value of the Middle Road Bridge lies in its architectural and
historical significance, and in its contextual value as an important community landmark.
文化遗产价值或利益陈述中间道桥的文物价值在于它的建筑和历史意义，以及它作为一个重要的社区地标的文脉价值。
Built in 1909-1910 to accommodate growing use of the Middle Road, it is the first example in Canada and second example of
a reinforced concrete truss or tied arch bridge in North America. The bridge was designed by Frank Barber of Barber and
Young, a prominent bridge and structural engineer from Toronto and constructed by O.L. Hicks of Humber Bay, who is
recognized for his unique construction method which involved the placement of ice on concrete to slow down the setting
process in order to ensure a good bond between successive pours.
它建于 1909-1910 年，为了适应日益增长的中间道路的使用，它是加拿大的第一个例子，也是北美第二个钢筋混凝土桁架或系
杆拱桥的例子。这座桥是由来自多伦多的著名桥梁和结构工程师、 Barber and Young 公司的弗兰克•巴伯(Frank Barber)设计
的，由亨伯湾(Humber Bay)的 o.l. 希克斯(o.l. Hicks)建造。希克斯以其独特的建造方法而闻名，他在混凝土上放置冰块，以减
缓凝固过程，从而确保连续浇筑之间有良好的粘合力。
Constructed on the stone abutments of a former bridge, the Middle Road Bridge is an enduring remnant of the historic Middle
Road, which was a major transportation corridor connecting the former counties of York and Peel until it was surpassed by
the Queen Elizabeth Way in the late 1930s. The bridge provided an important economic and social link for surrounding
communities. In the early 1900s, it was used by horses, carts and cattle to cross the waterway.Later, automobiles used the
bridge, although it only allowed for one lane of traffic.The bridge is now located on the edge of a quiet residential suburb.
Although used only for pedestrian traffic, it continues to provide the local community with access to a commercial area on the
Etobicoke side of the valley.
中间路大桥建于一座旧桥的石桥墩上，是历史悠久的中间路的遗迹。中间路曾是连接约克郡和皮尔郡的主要交通走廊，直到 20
世纪 30 年代后期被伊利沙伯皇后道超越。这座桥为周边社区提供了重要的经济和社会联系。在 20 世纪早期，它被马、马车和
牛用来穿越水路。后来，汽车使用桥梁，虽然它只允许一个车道的交通。这座桥现在位于一个安静的郊区住宅区的边缘。虽然
只用于行人交通，但它继续为当地社区提供进入山谷 Etobicoke 一侧商业区的通道。
Middle Road Bridge is an important landmark within the community. The
中间道桥是社区的重要地标

structure is physically prominent in its setting, and continues to be appreciated by the public. The bridge is the only remaining
feature of this portion of the popular,well-travelled highway, the Middle Road.
这座建筑物在地理位置上十分突出，并继续受到市民的欢迎。这座桥是这条广受欢迎、交通便利的高速公路——中间路——的
唯一剩下的特色。
Description of Heritage Attributes
文物属性描述
Key heritage attributes that embody the heritage value of the bridge as an early example of reinforced concrete truss or tied
arch bridge construction include its:- massive arched compression chords, slim vertical tension members and system of
counter braces - truss joints specially designed so that members will fail in the body rather than
作为钢筋混凝土桁架或系杆拱桥建造的早期例子，体现该桥文物价值的主要文物属性包括:-大型拱形压杆、细长的垂直拉杆和
反向支撑系统-特别设计的桁架节点，使构件不会在体内破坏而不是在体内破坏
at the joint
在节点处
Key heritage attributes that embody the contextual heritage value of the bridge as an enduring remnant of the historic Middle
Road and community landmark include the bridge's:
大桥作为历史悠久的中间道路和社区地标的遗迹，具有重要的文物价值，包括:
- continued cultural and economic use as a transportation link between the former Counties of Peel and York - location on the
stone abutments of a former crossing of the Etobicoke Creek - prominent setting at the eastern terminus of Sherway Drive in
view of the Queen Elizabeth Way - continued relationship to the adjacent natural lands of the Etobicoke Creek Valley
- 继续将文化和经济用途作为前 Peel 县和 York 县之间的交通枢纽-位于前 Etobicoke Creek 过境点的石墩上-位于 Sherway
Drive 东端的突出位置，以观赏伊利沙伯皇后道-继续与 Etobicoke Creek 谷毗邻的自然土地保持联系
2. West Montrose Covered Bridge, Township of Woolwich
2. 西蒙特罗斯盖桥，伍尔维奇镇
Description of Property
财产描述
The West Montrose Covered Bridge is a late 19th century covered wooden bridge that spans the Grand River in the rural
village of West Montrose. Connecting Hill Street, Covered Bridge Drive and Rivers Edge Drive, the bridge is just over 200feet
in length and covered with red-painted wood panelling and a gable roof.
西蒙特罗斯大桥是一座 19 世纪晚期的木桥，横跨西蒙特罗斯乡村的格兰德河。连接山街，有盖桥道和河边道，桥只有 200 多
英尺长，覆盖着红漆木镶板和山形屋顶。
Statement of Cultural Heritage Value or Interest
文化遗产价值或利益的陈述
The West Montrose Covered Bridge is the only remaining covered bridge in Ontario and the second oldest surviving bridge in
the Region of Waterloo. It was designed by a local contractor, John Bear, who, with his brother Benjamin,constructed the
bridge in 1881 as a replacement for an earlier open bridge at the same location. Originally, the bridge was constructed solely
of wood. Over the course of more than a century, a number of improvements have been necessary to maintain the function
and integrity of the bridge. The bridge materials today are a mix of wood, stone, asphalt, concrete and steel, representing not
only the evolution of bridge technology but also the stewardship of the township, the
西蒙特罗斯盖桥是安大略省仅存的盖桥，也是滑铁卢地区第二古老的现存桥梁。这座桥是由当地承包商约翰 · 贝尔设计的，他
和他的兄弟本杰明在 1881 年建造了这座桥，以取代之前在同一地点建造的一座开放式桥梁。最初，这座桥只是用木头建造的。
在一个多世纪的过程中，为了保持桥梁的功能和完整性，许多改进是必要的。今天的桥梁材料是木材、石材、沥青、混凝土和
钢材的混合物，不仅代表了桥梁技术的发展，也代表了该镇的管理

Heritage Bridge Guidelines (Interim)-Jan 11,20082008 年 1 月 11 日
region and the province. While the materials have been altered, however, the original form of the bridge designed by John
Bear has been largely maintained.
地区和省。虽然材料已经被改变，然而，约翰贝尔设计的桥梁的原始形式基本上得到了维护。
The'Kissing Bridge', as it was appropriately nicknamed due to the intimacy and privacy that the covered bridge offered its
travellers, is an iconic structure. It is a prominent and recognizable feature in arguably one of the most picturesque
landscapes in Ontario. It is also representative of the early history of Woolwich Township and of an earlier time in the village.
这座“亲吻桥”是一座标志性建筑，因为这座覆盖的桥为游客提供了亲密和隐私，所以得到了一个恰如其分的昵称。它是安大
略省风景最美丽的地方之一，是一个显著的和可辨认的特征。它也代表了伍尔维奇镇的早期历史和该村庄的早期时代。
Description of Heritage Attributes
文物属性描述
Attributes that contribute to the cultural heritage value of the bridge and which shou ld be retained include:
对桥梁的文化遗产价值有贡献并且应该被保留的属性包括:
-the original location of the bridge in the Village of West Montrose spann ing the Grand River -the original dimensions of the

这座桥位于横跨格兰德河的西蒙特罗斯村(Village of West Montrose) ，桥的原始位置这座桥的原始尺寸，长 208 英尺，宽 17

C3- Qualifications of a Heritage Consultant
C3-文物顾问的资格
Heritage Consultants- Built Heritage and Cultural Heritage Landscapes
文物顾问-文物建筑及文化遗产景观
It may be appropriate to employ more than one specialized heritage consultant for an undertaking impacting a bridge, as it
includes the structure itself, cultural heritage landscape, and maybe areas of archaeological potential.
对于一项影响桥梁的事业，雇用多于一名的专业遗产顾问可能是合适的，因为这项事业包括桥梁本身、文化遗产景观，以及可
能具有考古潜力的区域。
Depending on the nature of the project, a qualified heritage expert for built heritage/cultural landscapes could include a
heritage conservation architect, an architectural conservator, an architectural or landscape historian, a historic landscape
architect, or a member of another discipline with specialized training in preservation/historic materials(e.g. structural or
mechanical engineer specializing in heritage conservation).
视乎工程项目的性质，文物建筑/文化景观方面的合资格文物专家可包括文物保育建筑师、建筑修复师、建筑或景观历史学家、
历史景观建筑师，或在保育/历史材料方面受过专门训练的其他学科的成员(例如专门从事文物保育的结构或机械工程师)。
The expert should have demonstrated knowledge of the pertinent Ontario policies and procedures for cultural heritage, the
Standards and Guidelines of Conservation of Historic Places in Canada, the Ontario Heritage Bridge Guidelines, and have
demonstrated experience in fulfilling the requirements of an environmental assessment for built heritage and cultural
landscapes. This
这位专家应该表现出对安大略省有关文化遗产的政策和程序、加拿大保护历史地点的标准和准则、安大略省遗产桥准则的知识，
并表现出在满足建筑遗产和文化景观环境评估要求方面的经验。这

Appendix F- Definitions
附录 f-定义
Alter means to change in any manner and includes to restore, renovate, repair or disturb and"alteration" has a
corresponding meaning.(Ontario Heritage Act)
Alter 指以任何方式改变，包括恢复、翻新、修复或扰乱，“改变”具有相应的含义。(安大略省遗产法案)
Archaeological resources: Includes artifacts, archaeological sites and marine archaeological sites. The
identification and evaluation of such resources are based upon archaeological fieldwork undertaken in
accordance with the Ontario Heritage Act.(Provincial Policy Statement- PPS, 2005)
考古资源: 包括文物、考古遗址和海洋考古遗址。这些资源的鉴定和评估是基于根据安大略省遗产法进行的考古实
地工作。(省政策声明-PPS，2005)
Archaeological resources are often on or below ground, or form part of a cultural landscape. Their integrity can be
compromised by any land use activity, including, but not limited to, site alteration, grading, soil removal, construction,
shoreline stabilization, alteration to watercourses, extraction of aggregates and the clearing of woodlots or forested areas.
(Ontario Heritage Tool Kit, Heritage Resources in the Land Use Planning Process. MCL, 2006)
考古资源通常位于地面或地下，或者构成文化景观的一部分。任何土地使用活动，包括但不限于工地改动、分级、土壤移除、
建造、稳定海岸线、改变水道、提取集料和清理林地或林区，都可能损害其完整性。(安大略省文物工具包，土地利用规划过程
中的文物资源。MCL，2006)
Areas of archaeological potential: Areas with the likelihood to contain archaeological resources. Criteria for determining
archaeological potential are established by the Province, but municipal approaches which achieve the same objective may
also be used. Archaeological potential is confirmed through archaeological fieldwork undertaken in accordance with the
Ontario Heritage Act.(PPS, 2005)
具有考古潜力的区域: 可能含有考古资源的区域。确定考古潜力的标准由该省制定，但是达到同样目的的市政方法也可以使用。
根据安大略省遗产法案，通过考古实地工作来确认考古潜力。(PPS，2005)
Bridge: A structure that provides a roadway or walkway for the passage of vehicles,pedestrians, or cyclists across an
obstruction, gap or facility that is greater than 3metres in span.(Canadian Highway Bridge Design Code). In the context of this
guideline, this term refers to those bridge structures owned by the provincial government.
桥梁: 为车辆、行人或骑自行车者提供道路或行人通过跨度大于 3 米的障碍物、缺口或设施的建筑物。(加拿大公路桥梁设计规
范)。在本指南的上下文中，这个术语指的是省政府拥有的桥梁结构。
Built heritage resources: One or more significant buildings, structures,monuments, installations, or rema ins associated with
architectural, cultural,social, political, economic or military history and identified as being important to a community. These
resources may be identified through designation or heritage conservation easement under the Ontario Heritage Act, or listed
by local,provincial or federal jurisdictions.(PPS, 2005)
建筑遗产资源: 一个或多个与建筑、文化、社会、政治、经济或军事历史有关的重要建筑物、结构、纪念碑、装置或遗迹，并
被确定为对社区重要。这些资源可以通过安大略省遗产法案下的指定或遗产保护地役权来确定，或者由地方、省或联邦司法管
辖区列出。(PPS，2005)
Compatible development: Development that approximates or compliments the original design. The design for a new structure
is handled in such a way that it is clearly interpreted as a contemporary facility while still evoking the character of the original.
兼容性开发: 接近或赞美原始设计的开发。新结构的设计以这样一种方式处理，它被清楚地解释为一个当代的设施，同时仍然
唤起原来的性质。
Development and site alteration may be permitted on adjacent lands to protected heritage property where the proposed
development and site alteration has been evaluated and it has been demonstrated that the heritage attributes of the
protected heritage property will be conserved.
如已评估拟议的发展及地点改动，并已证明受保护的文物财产的文物属性会得到保存，则可在毗邻的土地上进行发展及地点改
动。
Mitigative measures and/or alternative development approaches may be required in order to conserve the heritage attributes
of the protected heritage property affected by the adjacent development or site alteration.(PPS, 2005)
可能需要采取缓解措施及/或其他发展方法，以保存受保护文物财产因毗邻发展或工地改动而受影响的文物特性。(PPS，2005)
Conservation: All the processes of looking after a place so as to retain its cu ltural significance.(The Burra Charter. The
Australia ICOMOS, 1999)
保护: 保护一个地方以保持其文化意义的所有过程。(伯拉宪章。澳大利亚 ICOMOS，1999)
Conservation Manual: A management document that sets out strategy to protect the cultural heritage value of a property. It
sets out what is significant about the property and what options and interventions are appropriate to retain that significance
into the future.
保护手册: 一份管理文件，阐述了保护文化遗产价值的策略。它阐述了什么是重要的财产和什么选择和干预措施是适当的，以
保留这一重要性到未来。
Conserved: The identification, protection, use and/or management of cultural heritage and archaeological resources in such a
way that their heritage values,attributes and integrity are retained. This may be addressed through a conservation plan or
heritage impact assessment.(PPS, 2005)
保存: 确定、保护、使用和/或管理文化遗产和考古资源，以保留其遗产价值、属性和完整性。这可以通过保护计划或遗产影响
评估来解决。(PPS，2005)
Cultural heritage landscape: A defined geographical area of heritage significance which has been modified by human
activities and is valued by a community. It involves a grouping(s) of individual heritage features such as structures,
spaces,archaeological sites and natural elements, which together form a significant type of heritage form, distinctive from that
of its constituent elements or parts. Examples may include, but are not limited to, heritage conservation districts designated
under the Ontario Heritage Act; and villages, parks, gardens, battlefields, mainstreets and neighbourhoods, cemeteries,
trailways and industrial complexes of cultural heritage value.(PPS, 2005)
文化遗产景观: 一个确定的地理区域的遗产意义，已经修改的人类活动和社区的价值经纬度。它涉及个别文物特色的分类，例
如建筑物、空间、考古地点和自然元素，这些特色共同构成一种重要的文物形式，与其组成元素或部分不同。例子可包括但不
限于根据《安大略遗产法》指定的文物保护区; 以及具有文化遗产价值的村庄、公园、花园、战场、主要街道和街区、墓地、
铁路和工业园区。(PPS，2005)
Cultural heritage value: A property may be determined to be of cultural heritage value if it meets the following criteria(derived
from The Ontario Heritage Act,Regulation 9/06):
文化遗产价值: 如果财产符合下列标准，就可以确定其具有文化遗产价值(源自《安大略遗产法》 ，第 9/06 条) :
• The property has design or physical value because it:
财产具有设计或物理价值，因为:
o is a rare, unique, representative or early example of a style, type,expression, material or construction method, o displays a
high degree of craftsmanship or artistic merit. or o demonstrates a high degree of technical or scientific achievement.
O 是一种罕见的、独特的、具有代表性的或早期的风格、类型、表现形式、材料或建筑方法的例子，o 展示了高度的技艺或艺
术价值。表现出高度的技术或科学成就。
• The property has historical or associative value because it:
该物业具有历史或联想价值，因为:
o has direct associations with a theme, event, belief, person, activity,organization or institution that is significant to a
community, o yields, or has the potential to yield, information that contributes to an understanding of a community or culture,
or o demonstrates or reflects the work or ideas of architect, builder,designer or theorist who is significant to a community.
O 与对社区有重要意义的主题、事件、信仰、人、活动、组织或机构有直接联系，o 产生或有可能产生有助于理解社区或文化
的信息，o 展示或反映对社区有重要意义的建筑师、建筑师、设计师或理论家的工作或想法。
Heritage Bridge Guidelines(Interim)- Jan 11, 2008
Heritage Bridge Guidelines (Interim)-Jan 11,20082008 年 1 月 11 日
• The property has contextual value because it:
•该物业具有相关价值，因为它:
a is important in defining, maintaining or supporting the character of an area, a is physically, functionally, visually
or historically linked to its surrounding, or
在界定、维持或支持一个区域的特征方面，a 是重要的，它在物理上、功能上、视觉上或历史上与其周围环境相联
系，或
a is a landmark.
A 是一个里程碑。
Similar criteria are under development for terrestrial and marine archaeological resources.
陆地和海洋考古资源也在制定类似的标准。
Listed bridge: A bridge that has been identified as having cultural heritage importance, scored greater than 60 in
the evaluation, and is worthy of conservation by inclusion on the Ontario Heritage Bridge List. Such bridges are
subject to the provisions of the Ontario Heritage Bridge Guidelines.
列入名录的桥梁: 已被确定为具有文化遗产重要性的桥梁，在评价中得分超过 60 分，并被列入安大略省遗产桥梁名
录，值得保护。这些桥梁受《安大略省遗产桥梁指南》的规定约束。
Maintenance: The continuous protective care of the fabric and the setting of a place, and is to be distinguished
from repair. Repair involves restoration or reconstruction. Maintenance is fundamental to conservation and should
be undertaken where the fabric is of cultural heritage value and its maintenance is necessary to retain that value.
(The Surra Charter, 1999)
维护: 对建筑结构和场所的设置进行持续的保护性护理，与维修区别开来。维修包括修复或重建。维修是保护的基
础，应该在具有文化遗产价值的地方进行，而维修对于保持这种价值是必要的。(The sura Charter，1999)
Reconstruction means returning a place to a known earlier state and is distinguished from restoration by the
introduction of new material into the fabric.(The Burra Charter, 1999)
重建意味着将一个地方恢复到已知的早期状态，与通过在织物中引入新材料进行修复的区别。(The Burra
Charter，1999)
Rehabilitation: In an engineering context, rehabilitation is defined as a modification, alteration or improvement to
the existing condition of a structure or bridge subsystem that is designed to correct deficiencies for a particular
design life and live load level.(Canadian Highway Bridge Design Code).
康复: 在工程环境中，康复被定义为对结构或桥梁子系统的现有状况进行修改、改造或改进，以纠正特定设计寿命
和活荷载水平的不足。(加拿大公路桥梁设计规范)。
As described in the Standards and Guidelines for the Conservation of Historic Places in Canada, Parks Canada
Rehabilitation means the action or process of making possible a continuing or compatible contemporary use for a
cultural heritage property, or of an individual component, through repair, alterations and/or additions, while
protecting its cultural heritage value.
如《加拿大历史地点保护标准和准则》所述，加拿大公园修复是指通过维修、改建和/或增建，使文化遗产财产或个
别组成部分的当代用途得以持续或兼容的行动或过程，同时保护其文化遗产价值。
Replication: The making of an exact copy of an existing structure feature or artefact.The purpose of replication is
usually to replace a missing or decayed component in order to maintain aesthetic unity and harmony.
复制: 对现有结构特征或人工制品进行精确复制。复制的目的通常是为了替换缺失或腐朽的部件，以保持审美的统
一和和谐。
Restoration: The activity in which a structure is returned to the appearance of an earlier time by removing later
material and/ or by replacing missing elements and details. Restoration of missing elements must be accurate,
use the same materials, and be based on physical evidence or documentary evidence such as historic
photographs and drawings.
修复: 通过移除后来的材料和/或替换缺失的元素和细节，使一个结构恢复到以前的样子的活动。修复缺失的元素必
须是准确的，使用相同的材料，并基于物理证据或文件证据，如历史照片和图纸。
Heritage Bridge Guidelines(Interim)- Jan 11, 2008
Heritage Bridge Guidelines (Interim)-Jan 11,20082008 年 1 月 11 日
Preservation means maintaining the fabric of a place in its existing state and retarding deterioration.(The Burra Charter, 1999)
保存意味着保持一个地方的结构在其现有状态和延缓恶化
Sympathetic Modification: Means making new work physically and visually compatible with the heritage attributes of a bridge.
New additions, alterations,structural reinforcements, or related new construction shall not destroy historic materials that
characterize the bridge. The new work shall be differentiated from the old and shall be compatible with the massing, size,
scale, and architectural features to protect the cultural heritage value of the bridge and its environment.
同情修改: 意味着使新的工作物理上和视觉上兼容桥梁的遗产属性。新的增建、改建、结构加固或相关的新建筑不得破坏具有
桥梁特征的历史材料。新工程应与旧工程区别开来，与桥梁的体积、尺寸、规模和建筑特征相适应，以保护桥梁及其环境的文
化遗产价值。

Convention for the Protection of the Architectural Heritage of Europe*
保护欧洲建筑遗产公约 *
Granada, 3.X.1985
格拉纳达，3. x. 1985
The member States of the Council of Europe, signatory hereto,
签署本协议的欧洲委员会成员国,
Considering that the aim of the Council of Europe is to achieve a greater unity between its members
for the purpose, inter alia, of safeguarding and realising the ideals and principles which are their
common heritage;
考虑到欧洲委员会的目标是在其成员之间实现更大的团结，以便除其他外，维护和实现作为其共同遗产
的理想和原则;
Recognising that the architectural heritage constitutes an irreplaceable expression of the richness and
diversity of Europe's cultural heritage, bears inestimable witness to our past and is a common heritage
of all Europeans;
认识到建筑遗产是欧洲文化遗产丰富性和多样性的不可替代的表现，是我们过去的不可估量的见证，是
所有欧洲人的共同遗产;
Having regard to the European Cultural Convention signed in Paris on 19 December 1954and in
particular to Article 1 thereof;
考虑到 1954 年 12 月 19 日在巴黎签署的欧洲文化公约，特别是其中的第 1 条;
Having regard to the European Charter of the Architectural Heritage adopted by the Committee of
Ministers of the Council of Europe on 26 September 1975 and to Resolution (76) 28, adopted on 14
April 1976, concerning the adaptation of laws and regulations to the requirements of integrated
conservation of the architectural heritage;
考虑到欧洲委员会部长委员会 1975 年 9 月 26 日通过的《欧洲建筑遗产宪章》和 1976 年 4 月 14 日通过
的关于修改法律和规章以适应综合保护建筑遗产的要求的第(76)28 号决议;
Having regard to Recommendation 880(1979) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe
on the conservation of the European architectural heritage;
考虑到欧洲委员会议会关于保护欧洲建筑遗产的第 880(1979)号建议;
Having regard to Recommendation No. R(80) 16 of the Committee of Ministers to member States on
the specialised training of architects, town planners, civil engineers and landscape designers, and to
Recommendation No. R(81) 13 of the Committee of Ministers, adopted on 1 July 1981, on action in aid
of certain declining craft trades in the context of the craft activity;
考虑到第 No 号建议。部长委员会向成员国提交的关于建筑师、城市规划师、土木工程师和景观设计师
专门培训的第 r (80)16 号决议和第。1981 年 7 月 1 日通过的部长委员会第 r (81)13 号决议，其中涉及在
手工业活动方面援助某些衰落的手工业的行动;
Recalling the importance of handing down to future generations a system of cultural references,
improving the urban and rural environment and thereby fostering the economic,social and cultural
development of States and regions;
回顾必须向后代传承一套文化参照系统，改善城市和农村环境，从而促进各国和各区域的经济、社会和
文化发展;
Acknowledging the importance of reaching agreement on the main thrust of a common policy for the
conservation and enhancement of the architectural heritage,
承认就保护和加强建筑遗产的共同政策的主旨达成协议的重要性,
Have agreed as follows:
同意如下:

Definition of the architectural heritage
建筑遗产的定义
Article 1
第一条
For the purposes of this Convention, the expression"architectural heritage" shall be considered to
comprise the following permanent properties:
为本公约之目的，“建筑遗产”一词应视为包括下列永久性财产:
1monuments: all buildings and structures of conspicuous historical, archaeological, artistic,scientific,
social or technical interest, including their fixtures and fittings; 2groups of buildings: homogeneous
groups of urban or rural buildings conspicuous for their historical, archaeological, artistic, scientific,
social or technical interest which are sufficiently coherent to form topographically definable units;
3sites: the combined works of man and nature, being areas which are partially built upon and
sufficiently distinctive and homogeneous to be topographically definable and are of conspicuous
historical, archaeological, artistic, scientific, social or technical interest.
1 个古迹: 所有具有显著历史、考古、艺术、科学、社会或技术价值的建筑物和构筑物，包括其装置和设
备; 2 组建筑物: 均匀分布的城市或乡村建筑物，这些建筑物具有显著的历史、考古、艺术、科学、社会
或技术价值，这些建筑物具有足够的连贯性，足以形成地形界定的单位; 3 个地点: 人与自然的结合作品，
这些建筑物的部分建筑物具有足够的独特性和均匀性，可以在地形上界定，具有显著的历史、考古、艺
术、科学、社会或技术价值。
Identification of properties to be protected
需要保护的财产的识别
Article 2
第二条
For the purpose of precise identification of the monuments, groups of buildings and sites to be
protected, each Party undertakes to maintain inventories and in the event of threats to the properties
concerned, to prepare appropriate documentation at the earliest opportunity.
为了准确确定需要保护的古迹、建筑群和遗址，每一缔约方承诺保持清单，并在有关财产受到威胁时，
尽早编制适当的文件。
Statutory protection procedures
法定保障程序
Article 3
第三条
Each Party undertakes:
每一方承诺:
1to take statutory measures to protect the architectural heritage; 2within the framework of such
measures and by means specific to each State or region, to make provision for the protection of
monuments, groups of buildings and sites.
1 采取法定措施保护建筑遗产; 2 在这些措施的框架内，并通过每个国家或地区特有的手段，为保护古迹、
建筑群和遗址作出规定。
Article 4
第四条
Each Party undertakes:
每一方承诺:
1to implement appropriate supervision and authorisation procedures as required by the legal protection
of the properties in question; 2to prevent the disfigurement, dilapidation or demolition of protected
properties. To this end,each Party undertakes to introduce, if it has not already done so, legislation
which:
1 根据有关财产的法律保护要求，执行适当的监督和授权程序; 2 防止受保护财产变形、破坏或拆除。为
此目的，每一方承诺，如果它还没有这样做，立法:
arequires the submission to a competent authority of any scheme for the demolition or alteration of
monuments which are already protected, or in respect of which protection proceedings have been
instituted, as well as any scheme affecting their surroundings; brequires the submission to a competent
authority of any scheme affecting a group of buildings or a part thereof or a site which involves:
A 要求向主管当局提交任何拆除或改建已受保护的古迹的计划，或已就此提起保护程序的计划，以及任
何影响其周围环境的计划; 要求向主管当局提交任何影响到一组建筑物或其中一部分或涉及:
–demolition of buildings,
- 拆除建筑物,
__________________________________________________________________________________
_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _
–the erection of new buildings,
建造新的建筑物,
–substantial alterations which impair the character of the buildings or the site; cpermits public
authorities to require the owner of a protected property to carry out work or to carry out such work itself
if the owner fails to do so;
- 对建筑物或场地进行重大改建，损害建筑物或场地的性质; 允许公共当局要求受保护财产的所有人进行
工程或在所有人不这样做的情况下自己进行工程;
dallows compulsory purchase of a protected property.
强制购买受保护的财产。
Article 5
第五条
Each Party undertakes to prohibit the removal, in whole or in part, of any protected monument, except
where the material safeguarding of such monuments makes removal imperative. In these
circumstances the competent authority shall take the necessary precautions for its dismantling,
transfer and reinstatement at a suitable location.
各缔约方承诺禁止全部或部分拆除任何受保护的古迹，除非对这些古迹的物质保护要求必须拆除。在这
种情况下，主管当局应采取必要的预防措施，将其拆除、转移并在适当的地点恢复原状。
Ancillary measures
辅助措施
Article 6
第六条
Each Party undertakes:
每一方承诺:
1to provide financial support by the public authorities for maintaining and restoring the architectural
heritage on its territory, in accordance with the national, regional and local competence and within the
limitations of the budgets available; 2to resort, if necessary, to fiscal measures to facilitate the
conservation of this heritage; 3to encourage private initiatives for maintaining and restoring the
architectural heritage.
1 根据国家、地区和地方的权限，在现有预算的限度内，由公共当局提供财政支助，以维护和修复其领
土上的建筑遗产; 2 必要时采取财政措施，促进这一遗产的保护; 3 鼓励私人倡议维护和修复建筑遗产。
Article 7
第七条
In the surroundings of monuments, within groups of buildings and within sites, each Party undertakes
to promote measures for the general enhancement of the environment.
在古迹周围、建筑群内和场地内，每一缔约方承诺促进全面改善环境的措施。
Article 8
第八条
With a view to limiting the risks of the physical deterioration of the architectural heritage, each Party
undertakes:
为了限制建筑遗产实际损坏的风险，各缔约方承诺:
1to support scientific research for identifying and analysing the harmful effects of pollution and for
defining ways and means to reduce or eradicate these effects; 2to take into consideration the special
problems of conservation of the architectural heritage in anti-pollution policies.
1 支持科学研究，以确定和分析污染的有害影响，并确定减少或消除这些影响的方法和手段; 2 在反污染
政策中考虑到保护建筑遗产的特殊问题。
Sanctions
制裁
Article 9
第九条
Each Party undertakes to ensure within the power available to it that infringements of the law
protecting the architectural heritage are met with a relevant and adequate response by the competent
authority. This response may in appropriate circumstances entail an obligation on the offender to
demolish a newly erected building which fails to comply with the requirements or to restore a protected
property to its former condition.
各缔约方承诺在其现有权力范围内，确保主管当局对违反保护建筑遗产的法律的行为作出相关和充分的
回应。在适当的情况下，这种反应可能意味着罪犯有义务拆除不符合要求的新建筑物或将受保护的财产
恢复原状。
__________________________________________________________________________________
_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _
Conservation policies
自然保育政策
Article 10
Article 10 第十条
Each Party undertakes to adopt integrated conservation policies which:
各缔约方承诺采取综合养护政策，其中:
1include the protection of the architectural heritage as an essential town and country planning
objective and ensure that this requirement is taken into account at all stages both in the drawing up of
development plans and in the procedures for authorising work; 2promote programmes for the
restoration and maintenance of the architectural heritage; 3make the conservation, promotion and
enhancement of the architectural heritage a major feature of cultural, environmental and planning
policies; 4facilitate whenever possible in the town and country planning process the conservation and
use of certain buildings whose intrinsic importance would not warrant protection within the meaning of
Article 3, paragraph 1, of this Convention but which are of interest from the point of view of their setting
in the urban or rural environment and of the quality of life; 5foster, as being essential to the future of
the architectural heritage, the application and development of traditional skills and materials.
1. 将保护建筑遗产列为一项重要的城乡规划目标，并确保在制订发展计划和批准工程程序的各个阶段都
考虑到这项要求; 2. 推动恢复和维护建筑遗产的方案; 3. 使保护、推广和改善建筑遗产成为文化、环境和
规划政策的一项主要内容;4 尽可能在城镇和国家规划过程中促进某些建筑物的保护和使用，这些建筑物
的内在重要性不值得本公约第 3 条第 1 款意义上的保护，但从它们在城市或农村环境中的位置以及生活
质量的角度来看是有意义的; 5 促进传统技能和材料的应用和发展，因为这对建筑遗产的未来至关重要。
Article 11
第十一条
Due regard being had to the architectural and historical character of the heritage, each Party
undertakes to foster:
在充分考虑遗产的建筑和历史特征的前提下，各方承诺:
–the use of protected properties in the light of the needs of contemporary life; –the adaptation when
appropriate of old buildings for new uses.
- 根据当代生活的需要使用受保护的财产;-在适当时改建旧建筑物作新用途。
Article 12
第十二条
While recognising the value of permitting public access to protected properties, each Party undertakes
to take such action as may be necessary to ensure that the consequences of permitting this access,
especially any structural development, do not adversely affect the architectural and historical character
of such properties and their surroundings.
在承认允许公众进入受保护财产的价值的同时，各缔约方承诺采取必要行动，确保允许这种进入的后果，
特别是任何结构性发展，不会对这种财产及其周围环境的建筑和历史特征产生不利影响。
Article 13
第十三条
In order to facilitiate the implementation of these policies, each Party undertakes to foster,within its own
political and administrative structure, effective co-operation at all levels between conservation, cultural,
environmental and planning activities.
为了促进这些政策的执行，每个缔约方承诺在其自己的政治和行政结构内促进保护、文化、环境和规划
活动之间在各级的有效合作。
Participation and associations
参与和协会
Article 14
第十四条
With a view to widening the impact of public authority measures for the identification,protection,
restoration, maintenance, management and promotion of the architectural heritage, each Party
undertakes:
为了扩大公共当局在识别、保护、修复、维护、管理和推广建筑遗产方面的措施的影响，各方承诺:
1to establish in the various stages of the decision-making process, appropriate machinery for the
supply of information, consultation and co-operation between the State, the regional and local
authorities, cultural institutions and associations, and the public;
1 在决策过程的各个阶段建立适当的机制，以便国家、区域和地方当局、文化机构和协会以及公众之间
提供信息、协商和合作;
__________________________________________________________________________________
_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _
2to foster the development of sponsorship and of non-profit-making associations working in this field.
2. 促进在这一领域开展工作的赞助和非牟利协会的发展。
Information and training
信息和培训
Article 15
第十五条
Each Party undertakes:
每一方承诺:
1to develop public awareness of the value of conserving the architectural heritage, both as an element
of cultural identity and as a source of inspiration and creativity for present and future generations; 2to
this end, to promote policies for disseminating information and fostering increased awareness,
especially by the use of modern communication and promotion techniques, aimed in particular:
1 提高公众对保护建筑遗产的价值的认识，这既是文化特性的一个要素，也是今世后代灵感和创造力的
来源; 2 为此目的，促进传播信息和提高认识的政策，特别是通过使用现代传播和促进技术，特别是:
aat awakening or increasing public interest, as from school-age, in the protection of the heritage, the
quality of the built environment and architecture; bat demonstrating the unity of the cultural heritage
and the links that exist between architecture, the arts, popular traditions and ways of life at European,
national and regional levels alike.
在保护文化遗产、建筑环境和建筑物的质素方面，唤起或增加公众的兴趣，例如从学龄开始; 展示文化
遗产的统一性，以及欧洲、国家和区域各级的建筑、艺术、流行传统和生活方式之间存在的联系。
Article 16
第十六条
Each Party undertakes to promote training in the various occupations and craft trades involved in the
conservation of the architectural heritage.
各方承诺促进各种职业和手工业的培训，参与保护建筑遗产。
European co-ordination of conservation policies
欧洲保护政策的协调
Article 17
第十七条
The Parties undertake to exchange information on their conservation policies concerning such matters
as:
缔约方承诺就下列事项交流有关其养护政策的信息:
1the methods to be adopted for the survey, protection and conservation of properties having regard to
historic developments and to any increase in the number of properties concerned; 2the ways in which
the need to protect the architectural heritage can best be reconciled with the needs of contemporary
economic, social and cultural activities; 3the possibilities afforded by new technologies for identifying
and recording the architectural heritage and combating the deterioration of materials as well as in the
fields of scientific research, restoration work and methods of managing and promoting the heritage;
4ways of promoting architectural creation as our age's contribution to the European heritage.
考虑到历史发展和有关财产数量的任何增加，对财产进行调查、保护和保存的方法; 2 保护建筑遗产的需
要如何才能最好地与当代经济、社会和文化活动的需要相协调; 3 确定和记录建筑遗产、防止材料退化的
新技术提供的可能性，以及在科学研究、修复工作和管理和促进遗产的方法等领域提供的可能性; 促进
建筑创作作为我们时代对欧洲遗产的贡献的 4 种方法。
Article 18
第十八条
The Parties undertake to afford, whenever necessary, mutual technical assistance in the form of
exchanges of experience and of experts in the conservation of the architectural heritage.
双方承诺在必要时提供建筑遗产保护方面的经验交流和专家交流形式的技术互助。
__________________________________________________________________________________
_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _
Article 19
第十九条
The Parties undertake, within the framework of the relevant national legislation, or the international
agreements, to encourage European exchanges of specialists in the conservation of the architectural
heritage, including those responsible for further training.
双方承诺在有关国家立法或国际协定的框架内，鼓励欧洲交流保护建筑遗产方面的专家，包括负责进一
步培训的专家。
Article 20
第二十条
For the purposes of this Convention, a Committee of Experts set up by the Committee of Ministers of
the Council of Europe pursuant to Article 17 of the Statute of the Council of Europe shall monitor the
application of the Convention and in particular:
为本公约的目的，欧洲委员会部长委员会根据欧洲委员会《伦敦条约》第 17 条设立的一个专家委员会应
监测本公约的适用情况，特别是:
1report periodically to the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe on the situation of
architectural heritage conservation policies in the States Parties to the Convention, on the
implementation of the principles embodied in the Convention and on its own activities; 2propose to the
Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe measures for the implementation of the Convention's
provisions, such measures being deemed to include multilateral activities, revision or amendment of
the Convention and public information about the purpose of the Convention; 3make recommendations
to the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe regarding invitations to States which are not
members of the Council of Europe to accede to this Convention.
1 定期向欧洲委员会部长委员会报告《公约》缔约国建筑遗产保护政策的情况、《公约》所载原则的执
行情况及其本身的活动; 2 向欧洲委员会部长委员会提出执行《公约》条款的措施，这些措施被认为包括
多边活动、修订或修正《公约》以及关于《公约》宗旨的公共信息; 3 就邀请非欧洲委员会成员国加入本
《公约》的问题向欧洲委员会部长委员会提出建议。
Article 21
第二十一条
The provisions of this Convention shall not prejudice the application of such specific more favourable
provisions concerning the protection of the properties described in Article 1 as are embodied in:
本公约的规定不妨碍关于保护第 1 条所述财产的更有利的具体规定的适用，这些规定体现在:
–the Convention for the Protection of World Cultural and Natural Heritage of 16 November 1972; –the
European Convention on the Protection of the Archaeological Heritage of 6 May 1969.
- 1972 年 11 月 16 日《保护世界文化和自然遗产公约》 ;-1969 年 5 月 6 日《欧洲保护考古遗产公约》。
Final clauses
最后条款
Article 22
第二十二条
1This Convention shall be open for signature by the member States of the Council of Europe. It is
subject to ratification, acceptance or approval. Instruments of ratification, acceptance or approval shall
be deposited with the Secretary General of the Council of Europe.
1 本公约开放供欧洲委员会成员国签署。有待批准、接受或批准。批准、接受或批准的文书应交存欧洲
委员会秘书长。
2This Convention shall enter into force on the first day of the month following the expiration of a period
of three months after the date on which three member States of the Council of Europe have expressed
their consent to be bound by the Convention in accordance with the provisions of the preceding
paragraph.
2 本公约应于欧洲委员会三个成员国按照前款规定表示同意受本公约约束之日起三个月期满后的下一个
月的第一天生效。
3In respect of any member State which subsequently expresses its consent to be bound by it,the
Convention shall enter into force on the first day of the month following the expiration of a period of
three months after the date of the deposit of the instrument of ratification,acceptance or approval.
3 对于随后表示同意受其约束的任何成员国，本公约应于批准书、接受书或核准书交存之日起三个月期
限届满后的下一个月的第一天生效。
__________________________________________________________________________________
_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _
Article 23
第二十三条
1After the entry into force of this Convention, the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe may
invite any State not a member of the Council and the European Economic Community to accede to this
Convention by a decision taken by the majority provided for in Article 20.d of the Statute of the Council
of Europe and by the unanimous vote of the representatives of the Contracting States entitled to sit on
the Committee.
1 本公约生效后，欧洲委员会部长委员会可以第 20 条规定的多数作出决定，邀请非欧洲委员会和欧洲经
济共同体成员的任何国家加入本公约。根据《欧洲委员会伦敦条约》 ，并经有资格担任委员会成员的缔
约国代表一致表决通过。
2In respect of any acceding State or, should it accede, the European Economic Community,the
Convention shall enter into force on the first day of the month following the expiration of a period of
three months after the date of deposit of the instrument of accession with the Secretary General of the
Council of Europe.
2 对于任何加入国或如果加入欧洲经济共同体，本公约应于向欧洲委员会秘书长交存加入书之日起三个
月期满后的下一个月第一天生效。
Article 24
第二十四条
1Any State may, at the time of signature or when depositing its instrument of ratification,acceptance,
approval or accession, specify the territory or territories to which this Convention shall apply.
1 任何国家均可在签署或交存其批准书、接受书、核准书或加入书时，指明本公约应适用的领土。
2Any State may at any later date, by a declaration addressed to the Secretary General of the Council
of Europe, extend the application of this Convention to any other territory specified in the declaration.
In respect of such territory the Convention shall enter into force on the first day of the month following
the expiration of a period of three months after the date of receipt of such declaration by the Secretary
General.
2 任何国家均可在稍后日期，通过向欧洲委员会秘书长发表声明，将本公约的适用范围扩大到声明中规
定的任何其他领土。对于这种领土，本公约应自秘书长收到这种声明之日起三个月期满后的下一个月的
第一天起生效。
3Any declaration made under the two preceding paragraphs may, in respect of any territory specified in
such declaration, be withdrawn by a notification addressed to the Secretary General. The withdrawal
shall become effective on the first day of the month following the expiration of a period of six months
after the date of receipt of such notification by the Secretary General.
3 就上述声明所指明的任何领土而言，根据上述两款作出的任何声明，可以通过发给秘书长的通知撤回。
撤回应在秘书长收到此种通知之日起六个月期满后的下一个月的第一天生效。
Article 25
第二十五条
1Any State may, at the time of signature or when depositing its instrument of ratification,acceptance,
approval or accession, declare that it reserves the right not to comply, in whole or in part, with the
provisions of Article 4, paragraphs c and d. No other reservations may be made.
1 任何国家均可在签署或交存其批准书、接受书、核准书或加入书时声明保留不全部或部分遵守第四条 c
款和 d 款规定的权利，不得作出任何其他保留。
2Any Contracting State which has made a reservation under the preceding paragraph may wholly or
partly withdraw it by means of a notification addressed to the Secretary General of the Council of
Europe. The withdrawal shall take effect on the date of receipt of such notification by the Secretary
General.
2 根据前款提出保留的任何缔约国可通过发给欧洲委员会秘书长的通知全部或部分撤回保留。撤回应自
秘书长收到该通知之日起生效。
3A Party which has made a reservation in respect of the provisions mentioned in paragraph 1above
may not claim the application of that provision by any other Party; it may, however, if its reservation is
partial or conditional, claim the application of that provision in so far as it has itself accepted it.
3 对上文第 1 款所述条款提出保留的缔约方不得要求任何其他缔约方适用该条款; 但是，如果其保留是部
分的或有条件的，只要它自己接受该条款，它就可以要求适用该条款。
Article 26
第二十六条
1Any Party may at any time denounce this Convention by means of a notification addressed to the
Secretary General of the Council of Europe.
一、任何缔约方均可随时通知欧洲委员会秘书长退出本公约。
2Such denunication shall become effective on the first day of the month following the expiration of a
period of six months after the date of receipt of such notification by the Secretary General.
2 退约应自秘书长收到此种通知之日起六个月期满后的下一个月的第一天起生效。

Article 27
第二十七条
The Secretary General of the Council of Europe shall notify the member States of the Council of
Europe, any State which has acceded to this Convention and the European Economic Community if it
has acceded, of:
欧洲委员会秘书长应将下列情况通知欧洲委员会成员国、任何已加入本公约的国家和已加入的欧洲经济
共同体:
any signature;
任何签名;
the deposit of any instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession; any date of entry into
force of this Convention in accordance with Articles 22, 23 and 24; any other act, notification or
communication relating to this Convention.
交存任何批准书、接受书、核准书或加入书; 本公约依照第 22 条、第 23 条和第 24 条生效的任何日期;
与本公约有关的任何其他行为、通知或来文。
In witness whereof the undersigned, being duly authorised thereto, have signed this Convention.
下列签字人经正式授权，已签署本公约，以昭信守。
Done at Granada, this 3rd day of October 1985, in English and French, both texts being equally
authentic, in a single copy which shall be deposited in the archives of the Council of Europe. The
Secretary General of the Council of Europe shall transmit certified copies to each member State of the
Council of Europe and to any State or to the European Economic Community invited to accede to this
Convention.
ETS 121 – Protection of the Architectural Heritage, 3.X.1985

Principles of Selection for
ListingBuildings
列表建筑物的选择原则
Introduction
引言
1. This guidance sets out the general principles that the Secretary of State applies when
decidingwhether a building is of special architectural or historic interest and should be
added to the listof buildings compiled under the Planning(Listed Buildings and
Conservation Areas) Act 1990.The Secretary of State cannot take any other factors into
account when considering hisdecision.
1.该指南规定了国务卿在决定某一建筑物是否具有特殊建筑或历史价值时所适用的一般原则，
并且应该列入根据 1990 年《规划(列入名单的建筑物和保护区)法》编制的建筑物清单。国务
卿在考虑他的决定时不能考虑任何其他因素。
Identifying and Recording the Historic Environment
确定和记录历史环境
2. In its broadest sense, the historic environment embraces all those aspects of the
country thatreflect the shaping hand of human history. Scarcely any part of England is
untouched by theinteraction between people and nature, which has taken place over
thousands of years. Someof the most obvious features of this environment are historic
buildings. England is exceptionallyrich in these- great churches, houses, and civic
buildings- but our understanding of thehistoric environment now encompasses a much
wider range of features, and in particularstresses the relationship between individual
buildings, and also the value of historic townscapeand landscape as a whole.
2.从最广泛的意义上说，历史环境包含了这个国家的所有方面，这些方面反映了人类历史的塑
造之手。几乎英格兰的任何一个地方都与人与自然的互动有关，这种互动已经持续了数千年。
这个环境最明显的特征之一就是历史建筑。英格兰拥有非常丰富的这些建筑——伟大的教堂、
房屋和市政建筑——但是我们对历史环境的理解现在包含了更广泛的特征，特别强调了个别建
筑之间的关系，以及历史城镇景观和景观作为一个整体的价值。
3. There is growing appreciation not just of the architectural set pieces, but of many
morestructures, especially industrial, agricultural and other vernacular buildings that,
althoughsometimes individually unassuming, collectively reflect some of the most
distinctive andcreative aspects of English history. More than this, our understanding
and appreciation of thehistoric environment now stretches beyond buildings to the
spaces and semi-natural featuresthat people have also moulded, and which are often
inseparable from the buildingsthemselves. For example, the pattern of roads and open
spaces and the views they createwithin historic townscapes may be as valuable as the
buildings. In the countryside, the detailedpatterns of fields and farms, of hedgerows
and walls, and of hamlets and villages, are amongthe most highly valued aspects of our
environment. England is particularly rich in the designedlandscapes of parks and
gardens, and the built and natural features they contain: the greatestof these are as
important to national, and indeed international, culture, as are our greatestbuildings.
3.越来越多的人开始欣赏这些建筑，尤其是工业建筑、农业建筑和其他本土建筑，尽管这些建
筑有时并不引人注目，但它们集体反映了英国历史上一些最独特和最具创造性的方面。不仅如
此，我们对历史环境的理解和欣赏现在已经超越了建筑，延伸到了人们塑造的空间和半自然的
特征，这些往往与建筑本身密不可分。例如，道路和开放空间的格局以及它们在历史城镇景观
中创造的景观可能和建筑一样有价值。在乡村，田地和农场、篱笆和围墙、村庄和村庄的细节
模式是我们环境中最有价值的方面。英格兰特别富有公园和花园的设计景观，以及它们所包含
的建筑和自然特征: 其中最伟大的对于国家乃至国际文化的重要性，就像我们最伟大的建筑一
样。
4. Processes of classification are necessary for the practical purposes of identifying
andprotecting individual sites and areas. This is achieved through the statutory systems
forscheduling ancient monuments, listing historic buildings and designating
conservation areas.Scheduling and listing are undertaken by the Secretary of State;
designation of conservationareas is the responsibility of local planning authorities. In
addition, English Heritage compilesregisters of parks and gardens of special historic
interest, and of historic battlefields. Onceidentified in these ways, the historic
environment may be protected through the planningsystem.
4.分类过程对于识别和保护个别地点和区域的实际目的是必要的。这是通过法定系统来安排古
迹，列出历史建筑和指定保护区。计划和列名由国务卿负责; 指定保护区是当地规划部门的责
任。此外，英国遗产局还负责编制具有特殊历史意义的公园和花园以及历史战场的登记册。一
旦通过这些方式确定，历史环境可以通过规划系统得到保护。
Listing Buildings of Special Architectural and Historic Interest
列出具有特殊建筑和历史价值的建筑
5. Section 1 of the Planning(Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990(the
Act)imposes a duty on the Secretary of State to compile or approve a list or lists of
buildings ofspecial architectural or historic interest as a guide to the planning
authorities when carrying out their planning functions. The planning system is
designed to regulate the development anduse of land in the public’s interest. The
designation of historic sites enables the planningsystem to protect them, through the
complementary systems of listed building consent andconservation area control,
coupled with controls over scheduled monument consent.
5.1990 年《规划(列入清单的建筑物和保护区)法》(该法)第 1 节规定，国务秘书有义务编制或
批准一份或多份具有特殊建筑或历史价值的建筑物清单，作为规划当局在履行其规划职能时的
指南。规划系统旨在规范公众利益范围内的土地开发和使用。指定历史遗址使规划系统能够保
护这些遗址，通过列入清单的建筑物同意书和保育区管制的补充制度，以及对在册古迹同意书
的管制。
6. The statutory criteria for listing are the special architectural or historic interest of a
building.Many buildings are interesting architecturally or historically, but, in order to be
listed, a buildingmust have “special” interest.
6.上市的法定标准是指建筑物的特殊建筑或历史价值。许多建筑在建筑或历史上都是有趣的，
但是，为了被列入名单，一个建筑必须有“特殊”的兴趣。
7. Buildings on the list are graded to reflect their relative architectural and historic
interest.Buildings of historic interest may justify a higher grading than would otherwise
be appropriate.
7.名单上的建筑被分级以反映它们相对的建筑和历史的兴趣。具有历史价值的建筑可能需要更
高的等级，而不是其他合适的等级。
•Grade I buildings are of exceptional interest;
一级建筑具有特殊的价值;
•Grade II* buildings are particularly important buildings of more than special interest;
•Grade II buildings are of special interest, warranting every effort to preserve them.
•二级 * 建筑物是特别重要的建筑物，不仅具有特殊意义; •二级建筑物具有特殊意义，因此有
必要尽一切努力予以保存。
8. In addition to the statutory criteria and the general principles contained in this
guidance,Selection Guides for different building types are published on English
Heritage’s website. TheSelection Guides provide detailed technical information about
each building type, and arelinked to the general principles contained in this guidance.
They demonstrate what featuresare considered significant and likely to make a building
of special architectural or historicinterest when assessing buildings of a particular type
from different periods, regions, or styles.It is recognised that some buildings are
unique or will fall into more than one building type.Where a building is a composite of
different types, then any relevant criteria from the SelectionGuides applies. The
general principles outlined below take precedence over the SelectionGuides, which are
published as supplementary information. The Guides are updated andrevised when
needed to reflect the growing understanding of the significance of particulartypes of
building through further research.
8.除了本指引所载的法定准则和一般原则外，英国文物局网站亦载有不同建筑物类型的选择指
引。这些选择指南提供了关于每种建筑类型的详细技术信息，并与本指南中包含的一般原则相
关联。当评估不同时期、不同地区或不同风格的特定类型的建筑物时，它们展示了哪些特征被
认为是重要的，并且有可能使建筑物具有特殊的建筑或历史价值。如果一栋建筑是不同类型的
组合，那么《选择指南》中的任何相关标准都适用。下面概述的一般原则优先于作为补充信息
发布的选择指南。指南在需要时进行更新和修订，以反映通过进一步研究对特定类型建筑的重
要性日益增长的理解。
Statutory Criteria
法定准则
9. The Secretary of State uses the following criteria when assessing whether a building
is ofspecial interest and therefore should be added to the statutory list:
9.国务卿在评估一栋建筑是否具有特殊利益，因此应该被列入法定清单时，使用了以下标准:
•Architectural Interest. To be of special architectural interest a building must be
ofimportance in its architectural design, decoration or craftsmanship; special
interest mayalso apply to nationally important examples of particular building
types and techniques(e.g. buildings displaying technological innovation or
virtuosity) and significant plan forms; •Historic Interest. To be of special historic
interest a building must illustrate importantaspects of the nation’s social,
economic, cultural, or military history and/or have closehistorical associations
with nationally important people. There should normally be somequality of
interest in the physical fabric of the building itself to justify the
statutoryprotection afforded by listing.
‧建筑兴趣。具有特殊建筑意义的建筑物必须在其建筑设计、装饰或工艺方面具有重要
性; 特殊意义也可适用于具有国家重要性的特定建筑类型和技术(例如展示技术创新或精
湛技术的建筑物)和重要的规划形式的例子; •历史意义。为了具有特殊的历史意义，一
个建筑物必须说明国家的社会、经济、文化或军事历史的重要方面，并且/或者与国家
重要人物有密切的历史联系。通常情况下，建筑物本身的物理结构应该具有某种质量的
利益，以证明清单所提供的法律保护是合理的。
10. When making a listing decision, the Secretary of State may take into account the
extent towhich the exterior contributes to the architectural or historic interest of any
group of buildings ofwhich it forms part. This is generally known as group value. The
Secretary of State will takethis into account particularly where buildings comprise an
important architectural or historicunity or a fine example of planning(e.g. squares,
terraces or model villages) or where there isa historical functional relationship between
a group of buildings. If a building is designatedbecause of its group value, protection
applies to the whole of the property, not just the exterior.
10.在作出列名决定时，国务卿可考虑外部对其所属任何建筑群的建筑或历史利益的贡献程度。
这通常被称为群体价值。国务卿将特别考虑到这一点，尤其是在建筑物构成重要的建筑或历史
统一性或规划的典范(如广场、露台或模范村庄)或一组建筑物之间存在历史功能关系的情况下。
如果一个建筑是因为它的群体价值而被指定，保护适用于整个财产，而不仅仅是外部。
11. When considering whether a building is of special architectural or historic interest
the Secretaryof State may take into account the desirability of preserving, on the
grounds of its architecturalor historic interest, any feature of the building containing a
man-made object or structure fixedto the building or forming part of the land and
comprised within the curtilage of the building.The desirability of preserving such a
feature is a factor which would increase the likelihood ofthe building being listed.
However, in the absence of any other aspects of special architecturalor historic interest,
such features will justify the listing of the building only if they are ofthemselves of
sufficient interest to render the building of special interest. The provision can beused
for a variety of features; examples could include a finely panelled sixteenth century
room,a fireplace and over-mantel that has been introduced from another building, or
an elaborateplaster ceiling. This provision cannot be used to preserve in situ anything
that is not a fixture,such as furniture or paintings.
11.在考虑建筑物是否具有特殊的建筑或历史价值时，国务卿可以考虑以建筑或历史价值为由，
保留建筑物的任何特征，这些特征包含固定在建筑物上的人造物体或结构，或构成建筑物土地
的一部分，并包含在建筑物的别墅内。保留这样一个特征的可取性是增加建筑被列入名单的可
能性的一个因素。然而，在没有任何其他具有特殊建筑或历史意义的方面的情况下，只有当这
些特征本身具有足够的意义使建筑具有特殊意义时，才有理由将该建筑列入清单。这项规定可
用于多种功能; 例如，一间镶嵌精美的十六世纪房间、一座从另一座建筑引进的壁炉和壁炉架，
或一个精致的石膏天花板。这个规定不能用来保存任何不是固定装置的东西，比如家具或绘画。
General Principles
一般原则
12. Age and rarity. The older a building is, and the fewer the surviving examples of its
kind, themore likely it is to have special interest. The following chronology is meant as
a guide toassessment; the dates are indications of likely periods of interest and are not
absolute. Therelevance of age and rarity will vary according to the particular type of
building because forsome types, dates other than those outlined below are of
significance. However, the generalprinciples used are that:
12.年龄和稀有度。一座建筑越古老，同类建筑中幸存的例子越少，它就越有可能引起人们的
特殊兴趣。下面的年表是评估的指南; 日期是可能的兴趣时期的指示，并不是绝对的。年龄和
稀有度的相关性会根据建筑的特殊类型而有所不同，因为对于某些类型，除了下面概述的日期
以外的日期是重要的。然而，使用的一般原则是:
•before 1700, all buildings that contain a significant proportion of their original fabric
arelisted;
在 1700 年之前，所有包含大量原始布料的建筑都被列入清单;
•from 1700 to 1840, most buildings are listed;
‧从 1700 年至 1840 年，大部分建筑物已列入清单;
•after 1840, because of the greatly increased number of buildings erected and the
muchlarger numbers that have survived, progressively greater selection is necessary;
•particularly careful selection is required for buildings from the period after 1945;
•buildings of less than 30 years old are normally listed only if they are of
outstandingquality and under threat.
•1840 年以后，由于建造的建筑物数量大大增加，幸存下来的建筑物数量也大大增加，因此有
必要逐步扩大选择范围; •1945 年以后的建筑物需要特别仔细的选择; •30 年以下的建筑物通常
只有在质量优良和受到威胁的情况下才列入名单。
13. Aesthetic merits. The appearance of a building – both its intrinsic architectural merit
and anygroup value – is a key consideration in judging listing proposals, but the special
interest of abuilding will not always be reflected in obvious external visual quality.
Buildings that areimportant for reasons of technological innovation, or as illustrating
particular aspects of socialor economic history, may have little external visual quality.
13.审美价值。建筑物的外观——包括其内在的建筑价值和任何群体的价值——是评判列表建
议书的一个关键考虑因素，但建筑物的特殊兴趣并不总是反映在明显的外部视觉质量上。那些
因为技术创新或者说明社会经济历史的特殊方面而具有重要意义的建筑，可能没有什么外在的
视觉质量。
14. Selectivity. Where a building qualifies for listing primarily on the strength of its
specialarchitectural interest, the fact that there are other buildings of similar quality
elsewhere is notlikely to be a major consideration. However, a building may be listed
primarily because itrepresents a particular historical type in order to ensure that
examples of such a type arepreserved. Listing in these circumstances is largely a
comparative exercise and needs to beselective where a substantial number of buildings
of a similar type and quality survive. In suchcases, the Secretary of State’s policy is to
list only the most representative or most significantexamples of the type.
14.选择性。如果一栋建筑符合上市条件主要是因为其特殊的建筑风格，那么其他地方有其他
类似质量的建筑物就不太可能成为主要考虑因素。然而，一个建筑可能被列入主要是因为它代
表了一个特定的历史类型，以确保这种类型的例子被保留下来。在这些情况下的列表主要是一
个比较练习，需要有选择性的大量类似类型和质量的建筑存活下来。在这种情况下，国务卿的
政策是只列出最具代表性或最重要的例子的类型。
15. National interest. The emphasis in these criteria is to establish consistency of
selection toensure that not only are all buildings of strong intrinsic architectural
interest included on the list,but also the most significant or distinctive regional
buildings that together make a majorcontribution to the national historic stock. For
instance, the best examples of local vernacularbuildings will normally be listed because
together they illustrate the importance of distinctivelocal and regional traditions.
Similarly, for example, some buildings will be listed because theyrepresent a nationally
important but localised industry, such as shoemaking inNorthamptonshire or cotton
production in Lancashire.
15 岁。国家利益。这些标准的重点是建立选择的一致性，以确保不仅所有具有强烈内在建筑
价值的建筑都列入清单，而且还包括最重要或最具特色的区域性建筑，这些建筑共同对国家历
史遗产作出重大贡献。例如，当地乡土建筑的最佳例子通常会被列入名单，因为他们一起说明
了独特的地方和地区传统的重要性。同样的，例如，一些建筑会被列出，因为它们代表了一个
国家重要的，但本地化的产业，如制鞋在北安普敦郡或棉花生产在兰开夏郡。
16. State of repair. The state of repair of a building is not a relevant consideration when
decidingwhether a building meets the test of special interest. The Secretary of State
will list a buildingwhich has been assessed as meeting the statutory criteria,
irrespective of its state of repair.
16.修复状态。在决定一栋建筑物是否符合特殊利益的测试时，建筑物的维修状态并不是一个
相关的考虑因素。国务卿将列出一个已被评估为符合法定标准的建筑物，而不论其维修状况如
何。

Urban Landscapes
都市景观
Register of Parks and Gardens Selection Guide
公园及园林名录选择指南
Summary
摘要
Historic England’s selection guides help to define which historic buildings
and sites are likely to meet the relevant tests for national designation. Four
guides, of which this is one, deal with the types of site included on Historic
England’s Register of Parks and Gardens of Special Historic Interest in
England which is a constituent part of the National Heritage List for England.
英格兰历史建筑的选择指南有助于确定哪些历史建筑和遗址可能符合国家指定
的相关测试。四个指南，其中之一，处理的遗址类型包括在历史英格兰的公园
和花园特别历史兴趣的英格兰登记册，这是一个组成部分的国家遗产清单的英
格兰。
Each guide falls into two halves. The first defines the types of site included in it,
before going on to give a brisk overview of how these developed through time,
with notice of the main designers and some of the key sites. The second half of
the guide sets out the particular tests a site has to meet if it is to be included on
the Register. A select bibliography gives suggestions for further reading.
每个向导分成两部分。首先定义了包含在其中的网站类型，然后在主要设计者和一
些关键网站的注意下，对这些网站是如何随着时间的推移发展起来的给出一个简要
的概述。指南的后半部分列出了一个网站如果要被列入注册表，必须要满足的特殊
测试。一个精选的参考书目提供了进一步阅读的建议。
This guide covers urban designed landscapes, including town walks,
squares, municipal parks and seaside gardens. The other three guides
treat Rural, and Institutional, landscapes, and Landscapes of
Remembrance, that is cemeteries and burial grounds.
这本指南涵盖了城市设计的景观，包括城镇步行道，广场，市政公园和
海滨花园。另外三本指南介绍了乡村、公共机构、景观和纪念景观，也
就是墓地和墓地。
