3.2 Modern industrial sites
3.2 现代工业用地
Modern industrial sites can sometimes have strong
claims to acknowledgment and may be considered
for scheduling. However, generic and standard
modern industrial structures lend themselves to
listing first and foremost, if they are designatable at
all. Innovation and historic interest may be key. For
the more extraordinary, non-standard, structures
listing will also be the more valid approach,
现代工业网站有时会强烈要求得到承认，并且可能会
被考虑安排日程。然而，一般的和标准的现代工业结
构首先适合上市，如果他们是可设计的。创新和历史
利益可能是关键。对于比较特殊的，非标准的，结构
上市也将是比较有效的方法,
and scheduling should only be considered in
exceptional cases where it is wholly appropriate.
For the most contentious modern sites, it would be
expected that a discussion on various options is
had with owners. Heritage management
agreements should be considered. Long-term
monumentalisation of whole sites is seldom
feasible, and selectivity is essential. Preservation
by record can be the most appropriate response:
securing a vivid coverage before closure is
desirable. Regeneration of ‘brown-field’ sites
covers many former industrial locations: where
只有在完全合适的特殊情况下，才应考虑时间安排。
对于最具争议的现代网站，可以预期的是，与业主
就各种选择进行讨论。应考虑文物管理协议。长期
对整个网站进行纪念性改造很少是可行的，而选择
性是必要的。通过记录进行保存可能是最适当的反
应:最好在关闭前确保生动的覆盖范围。“棕色田地”
的再生覆盖了许多以前的工业地点:

important structures remain, our designation
response is generally through selective listing.
如果重要的建筑物仍然存在，我们的指定反应通

3.3 Scheduling below-ground sites
3.3 安排地下场地
While it is legally possible to schedule industrial
workings below the surface of the earth, in
practice very few have been designated in
虽然在法律上可以将工业活动安排在地球表面以
下，但实际上很少有人被指定在年
the past. Considerable challenges arise over
their long-term management. Mining played a
fundamental part in the Industrial Revolution, but
only in carefully selected instances will below-
ground scheduling be appropriate.
过去。在其长期管理方面出现了相当大的挑战。
采矿业在工业革命中发挥了基础性作用，但只有
在经过精心挑选的情况下，地下调度才是适当的。
3.4 Mineral rights ownership and
outstanding mineral permissions
3.4 矿产权所有权和未获得的矿产许
可
A particular consideration for industrial
archaeological cases is that of mineral rights.
Generally minerals are held in private ownership
and often independently from the landowner, and
in some instances, mineral permissions to work or
rework mines and mine tips may be valid, but held
in abeyance, for considerable periods of time. In
addition, some sites may have other extant
planning permissions which remain valid. It is not
necessary for an owner of minerals to register his
rights if these are separate from the surface of the
land. In such instances, a decision to schedule
may incur valid claims for compensation if the
owner’s ability to exercise their valid permits are
revoked or made subject to additional costs or
conditions; a recommendation to schedule will,
therefore, be exceptional. Some information may
be available from the Land Registry but these
rights are registered on a voluntary basis.
工业考古案件的一个特别考虑因素是矿产权。一般
来说，矿物是私人所有，往往独立于土地所有者，
在某些情况下，矿物开采或重新开采的许可和采矿
技巧可能是有效的，但在相当长的一段时间内被搁
置。此外，一些网站可能有其他现存的规划许可，
仍然有效。如果矿物与土地表面分开，则矿物所有
者无须登记其权利。在这种情况下，如果所有人行
使其有效许可证的能力被撤销，或受到额外费用或
条件的限制，则安排时间的决定可能引起有效的赔
偿要求;因此，安排时间的建议属于例外情况。土
地注册处可提供一些资料，但这些权利是自愿登记
的。
3.5 Period
3.5 句号
Sites of all periods may be considered for
scheduling. Those which predate the Industrial
Revolution may be rare examples of a particular
industry. They are thereby likely to have
national importance and be strong candidates
for scheduling either in their own right, or as part
of a wider site such as a larger settlement which
可以考虑所有时段的地点进行日程安排。那些发
生在工业革命之前的，可能是某一特定行业的罕
见例子。因此，它们有可能具有全国性的重要意
义，并有可能成为时间安排的强有力的候选者，
无论是它们自己的权利，还是作为一个更大的场
所的一部分，例如一个
includes industrial features. However, period is
far from the only consideration, and even with
relatively early industrial sites, some are
sufficiently common that only selected examples
will be proposed for designation. Many sites, say
where ores were extracted at different times, will
be multi-period. While this can lead to complexity,
and perhaps a lesser immediate legibility, in
general such sites may have added interest and
potential where evidence of early works still
survives; where later works have obliterated the
early ones, this will not be the case.
包括工业特征。然而，周期远不是唯一的考虑因素，
即使是在相对较早的工业场所，有些场所也是相当
普遍的，只有选定的例子才会被提议指定。许多地
点，比如说在不同时期开采矿石的地点，将是多个

品已经抹杀了早期的，这将不是这样的情况。
3.6 Rarity, representativity
and selectivity
3.6 稀有性、代表性和选择性
Being a rare survival of a site-type may strengthen
the case for scheduling. This will include sites where
technological experimentation took place (see below
under Documentation). Equally, it is important that
the schedule is broadly representative of all kinds of
sites, and not just the extraordinary or unusual ones.
A range of industrial site-types of different periods
should be considered for inclusion, although the
relative significance of the particular industry in
national terms is also a factor - not every specialised
niche industry will justify a designated example of its
own.
作为一个罕见的生存站点类型可能会加强案件的调度。
这将包括进行技术实验的网站(见下文文档)。同样重
要的是，时间表要广泛代表所有类型的网站，而不仅
仅是那些特别的或不寻常的网站。应考虑列入一系列
不同时期的工业场地类型，尽管某一行业在国家方面
的相对重要性也是一个因素--并非每一个专门的特殊
行业都有理由作为自己的特定例子。
Selection also requires that the national spread of
an industry is represented, for instance so that it is
not forgotten that coal was mined in Kent and
Somerset, not just in the great coalfields
选择还要求代表一个行业在全国的传播，例如，这
样就不会忘记煤炭是在肯特郡和萨默塞特开采的，
而不仅仅是在大型煤田
of the north. Selection of sites for designation
should also aim to capture important regional
specialisms, such the steel-working sites of
Sheffield, as these will often have strong claims
to note on a national level. However, it should be
noted that our approach is not to designate every
survival within these localised clusters. We must
be selective, and designation can only be
warranted by the survival of substantial interest,
not simply by the fact of survival.
北境。选择指定地点还应着眼于抓住重要的地区
特色，例如谢菲尔德的炼钢厂，因为这些地点在
国家层面上往往有着强烈的主张。然而，应该指
出的是，我们的方法并不是指定这些局部集群中
的每一个生存者。我们必须是有选择性的，只有
基于实质性利益的生存，而不仅仅是基于生存的
事实，才能作出这样的指定。
With frequently encountered site-types or
structures, whether or not with a national
distribution, a selection of the best and most
representative examples will be sought.
对于经常遇到的场地类型或结构，无论是否
具有全国性分布，都将寻找最佳和最具代表
性的例子。

3.7 Documentation
3.7 文档
Where a site has good documentation, either
contemporary (such as historic plans or
descriptions), or recent (such as archaeological
surveys or excavations), this may enhance its
claims to national importance. However in many
industries, particularly metallurgical ones,
techniques used during the industrial revolution
were often closely-guarded secrets that were not
documented. Archaeological analysis of deposits
can play an important role in understanding these
poorly documented processes (see Potential).
This will seldom be the case when a full
documentary record survives of processes,
particularly on more modern sites, however.
如果一个遗址有良好的文献记载，无论是当代的
(如历史规划或描述)，或最近的(如考古调查或发
掘)，这可能会增强其声称的国家重要性。然而，
在许多行业，特别是冶金行业，工业革命期间使用
的技术往往是严格保密的秘密，没有记录在案。对
沉积物的考古分析可以在理解这些文献记载不详的
过程中发挥重要作用(见潜力)。然而，当一份完整
的文件记录在过程中幸存下来时，这种情况就很少
发生了，尤其是在更现代的网站上。
3.8 Historic importance
3.8 历史意义
Where a site is associated with a famous and
especially an innovative industrialist, engineer or
company, or saw new processes pioneered, this
may add to its significance. That will be
especially so where innovation has impacted on,
and can be read in, the form of the asset.
如果一个网站与一个著名的，特别是创新的实业家、
工程师或公司有关联，或者看到新的工艺流程，这
可能会增加它的重要性。特别是在创新已经影响并
可以从资产的形式中看出来的地方。
3.9 Group value
3.9 组值
Industrial sites function by taking in raw materials,
subjecting them to one or more processes to
produce a product (normally along with waste
products), with the output then transported off-site
to market or to form a raw material for another
industry. Sites where this sequence of activities or
‘process flow’ is still recognizable are often of
greater importance than sites where only part of
the industrial process can be identified. Thus a
spoil heap can provide additional group value,
complementing the survival of the site
工业场所的功能是吸收原材料，使其经过一种或多
种工艺生产产品(通常与废品一起)，然后将产品运
到场外市场或形成另一个工业的原材料。这种活动
顺序或“工艺流程”仍然可辨认的地点往往比只能辨
认出工业过程的一部分的地点更为重要。因此，废
弃堆可以提供额外的组价值，补充站点的生存能力
of the primary industrial process by showing its
by-products. That said, some industrial features
are so significant even in isolation that they may
justify designation when other elements of the
site have been lost. With some sites such as
those served by long leat or transport systems,
especially where documented on maps, it is
appropriate to only include sample lengths
通过显示其副产品，对初级工业过程进行分析。也
就是说，一些工业特征是如此重要，甚至在孤立的
情况下，当网站的其他元素丢失的时候，他们可能
会被认为是正当的。对于一些网站，比如那些有长
距离雷达或运输系统的网站，特别是在地图上有记
录的网站，只包括样本长度是合适的
of what would otherwise represent repetitive
archaeological information. Appropriate
boundaries are always drawn to ensure that
the key part of a dispersed site is identified.
代表了重复的考古信息。总是画出适当的边界，
以确保分散场地的关键部分得到识别。
Another form of group value occurs where there
are a number of different industrial concerns
clustered together, especially where there were
historical linkages. An example is the scheduled
Dark Hill ironworks and brickworks and the Titanic
steelworks at Coleford (Gloucestershire).
集团价值的另一种形式发生在许多不同的工业关注
点聚集在一起的地方，特别是在存在历史联系的地
方。一个例子是在科尔福德(格洛斯特郡)的黑山铁
厂和砖厂以及泰坦尼克号钢厂。
3.10 Survival and condition
3.10 生存和状态
In designation assessments, a high level of
alteration and reconstruction is sometimes the
basis for a decision not to designate. With
industrial structures and buildings, however,
partial rebuilding and repair is often related to the
industrial process. This may provide
archaeological evidence for technological
change that can itself be of sufficient significance
to warrant protection: alteration can thus have
在指定评估中，高水平的改建和重建有时是决定
不指定的依据。然而，对于工业结构和建筑物，
部分的重建和修复通常与工业过程有关。这可能
为技术变革提供考古学证据，而技术变革本身具
有足够的重要性，值得保护:因此，改变可能具有
a positive value. Where deterioration and loss
have affected the significance of a site, however,
judgment is needed as to whether national
importance is still present: remains of buildings,
sites and structures are eligible for scheduling,
but outright loss can undermine the claims. A
site’s condition can be a determinant too: given
that the aim of scheduling is to secure the long-
term preservation of a monument for the benefit
of future generations, where the condition of a site
is proven to be unsustainable, questions must be
asked about the appropriateness of scheduling.
正值。然而，如果损坏和损失影响到一个地点的重
要性，就需要判断国家重要性是否仍然存在:建筑
物、地点和结构的遗迹有资格列入时间表，但完全
损失可能会破坏索赔要求。一个遗址的状况也可以
是一个决定因素:鉴于时间安排的目的是确保为了
子孙后代的利益而长期保存一个遗址，如果一个遗
址的状况被证明是不可持续的，就必须询问时间安
排的适当性。
3.11 Potential
3.11 潜力
Industrial sites sometimes have the potential of
yielding historic information which can only be
gained through the use of the scientific
investigative techniques of archaeology.
Analysis of waste artefacts and process residues
can elucidate industrial techniques unrecorded
elsewhere, for instance. Potential, when
demonstrably present, can add to the case for
scheduling as the preferred designation option.
工业遗址有时具有提供历史信息的潜力，而这些
信息只有通过使用考古学的科学研究技术才能获
得。例如，对废物和工艺残留物的分析可以阐明
其他地方没有记录的工业技术。潜力，当明显存
在时，可以增加作为首选指定选项的调度的情况。

4 Select Bibliography
4 选择参考书目
As part of English Heritage’s Monuments Protection Programme, surveys of
major historic industries were undertaken in the years after 1990, and a series of
‘step reports’ compiled. The step 1 reports contain overviews of particular
industries, while the step 3 reports include a list of identified sites that are
potentially of national importance: validation of these assessments may be
needed, but as general indicators of significance their findings still hold true. For
industries treated in this selection guide MPP step 1 reports have been completed
for the following: alum, arsenic, brass, chemicals, clay, coal, copper, glass,
gunpowder, iron/steel, lead, lime, minor metals, oil, salt, stone, tin, zinc.
作为英国文物古迹保护计划的一部分，在 1990 年以后对主要历史产业进行了调查，
并编写了一系列”步骤报告”。步骤 1 的报告载有特定行业的概况，而步骤 3 的报告
载有可能对国家具有重要意义的已确定地点的清单:可能需要对这些评估进行验证，
但作为衡量重要性的一般指标，其结论仍然适用。对于在这个选择指南处理的工业
MPP 步骤 1 报告已完成如下:明矾，砷，黄铜，化学品，粘土，煤炭，铜，玻璃，
火药，铁/钢，铅，石灰，稀有金属，石油，盐，石头，锡，锌。

4.2 Regional studies
4.2 区域研究
Between 1965 and 1980 a series of regional guides
was published by David and Charles and then
Batsford, generally with titles in the format of The
Industrial Archaeology of … These remain useful as
starting points and for context.
1965 年至 1980 年间，大卫和查尔斯先后出版了一系
列地区指南，然后是巴斯福德，通常以《工业考古学》
的形式出版，这些书作为起点和背景仍然很有用。
The Association for Industrial Archaeology has
produced regional and county gazetteers in connection
with its annual conference each year for over 20 years.
Many are out of print but some are available at http://
industrial-archaeology.org/publications/sales/
20 多年来，工业考古学协会每年结合其年度会议编制
区域和县地名录。许多书已经绝版，但是有一些可以在

The Turkish Bridge of Mostar, Croatia, built
between 1556 and 1566, during the reign of
Sultan Soliman the Magnificent (1494 - 1566) who
was Ottoman Sultan from 1520 to 1566. The
bridge was destroyed by the Croats on November
9, 1993.
克罗地亚莫斯塔尔的土耳其大桥，建于 1556 年至
1566 年间，建于 1520 年至 1566 年奥斯曼苏丹统
治时期(1494-1566 年)。这座桥于 1993 年 11 月 9
日被克罗地亚人摧毁。
Rebuilt 11 years later, this bridge became the symbol
of
11 年后重建，这座桥成为了
reconciliation and human solidarity.
和解和人类团结的象征。
On July 23rd 2004 in Mostar, the reconstructed Old
Bridge was inaugurated by the chairman of Bosnia
and Herzegovina's tripartite presidency, Sulejman
Tihic, and UNESCO Director-General Koïchiro
Matsuura, representing the entire United Nations,
in the presence of about ten heads of state and
other top European political figures.
2004 年 7 月 23 日，在莫斯塔尔，重建的旧桥由波
斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那三方主席苏莱曼 · 蒂希克主席
和代表整个联合国的教科文组织总干事松浦光一郎

级政治人物出席。

SCOTLAND’S INVENTORY OF GARDENS AND
DESIGNED LANDSCAPES
苏格兰花园和景观设计清单
HISTORICARAINNEACHD
HISTORICARAINNEACHD 历史遗迹
ENVIRONMENTEACHDRAIDHEIL
环境教育
SCOTLANDALBA
苏格兰阿尔巴
Scotland’s Inventory of Gardens and Designed Landscapes
苏格兰园林和景观设计清单
Above: Estate staff, The Glen, Scottish Borders, before 1910 © Royal Commission on the Ancient and Historical Monuments of Scotland Cover: Drummond Castle, Perth and Kinross © Keith
Fergus, Scottish Viewpoint
上图: 苏格兰边区格兰庄园的工作人员，1910 年之前的皇家苏格兰古迹和历史遗迹委员会封面: 德拉蒙德城堡，珀斯-金罗斯基思-费格斯，苏格兰观点
This booklet explains what being on the inventory means and how we assess gardens and designed landscapes
for designation.
这本小册子解释了什么是在清单意味着，我们如何评估花园
和设计景观指定。
Scotland’s historic environment has been shaped by people for over 10,000
years.Past generations have left their mark on our towns and cities, and the
countryside around us. The sense of place and the strong cultural identity
that our historic environment provides are rooted in our communities and
promote a positive image of Scotland across the world.
苏格兰的历史环境已经被人类塑造了一万多年。过去的几代人在我们的城镇和城
市以及我们周围的乡村留下了他们的印记。我们的历史环境所提供的地方感和强
烈的文化认同感植根于我们的社区，并在世界范围内提升了苏格兰的正面形象。
Measures to protect our built environment first became law in the United
Kingdom in 1882. The inventory of gardens and designed landscapes was
begun in 1987and there are now over 300 sites on the inventory. This
number changes regularly as sites are added or reviewed.
保护建筑环境的措施于 1882 年在英国首次成为法律。花园和设计景观的清单开
始于 1987 年，现在有超过 300 个地点在清单上。这个数字随着地点的增加或审
查而定期变化。
The inventory recognises grounds intentionally laid out for artistic effect
which are of national importance.We believe that they are among
Scotland’s greatest assets.
这份清单确认了有意为艺术效果设计的具有国家重要性的场地。我们相信，这些
场地是苏格兰最大的资产之一。
Inventory sites chart Scotland’s history.They help to make Scotland a great
place to live, work and visit. The historic character of our environment is
important to our quality of life and it helps us to understand who we are.
库存网站记录了苏格兰的历史。它们使苏格兰成为一个适合居住、工作和旅游的
好地方。我们环境的历史特征对我们的生活质量很重要，它帮助我们了解我们是
谁。
Inventory sites range from country estate landscapes, botanic garden
collections,and urban parks to cemeteries. This varied and exceptional
heritage is a testament to the vision and skills of our predecessors.
目录网站的范围从乡村庄园景观，植物园收藏，城市公园到墓地。这些丰富多彩
的特殊遗产证明了我们前人的远见卓识和技能。
Adding these sites to the inventory helps us to recognise their
achievements and pass them on to future generations.
将这些网站添加到目录中，有助于我们认识到它们的成就，并将它们传递给后代。
Today’s owners of inventory sites have an important part to play in
managing our heritage. They can help to make sure that future
generations will be able to enjoy these areas of national importance.
今天的库存网站的所有者在管理我们的遗产方面扮演着重要的角色。他们可以帮
助确保后代能够享受这些国家重要的领域。
Above: Aerial view of the King’s Knot, Stirling © Historic Environment Scotland
上图: 苏格兰斯特林国王结的鸟瞰图
What is the inventory?
目录是什么？
Above: Dunrobin Castle and gardens, Highland © Historic Environment Scotland(Aerial Photography Collection)
上图: 敦罗宾城堡和花园，苏格兰高地历史环境(航拍摄影集)
The inventory is a list of Scotland’s most important gardens and designed landscapes.
这份清单列出了苏格兰最重要的花园和设计风景。
Gardens and designed landscapes are grounds intentionally laid out for
artistic effect.
园林和景观设计是为了达到艺术效果而特意布置的场地。
We maintain the inventory under the terms of the Ancient Monuments and
Archaeological Areas Act 1979,legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1979/46.
我们根据 1979 年《古代遗迹和考古地区法案》(legislation.gov.
uk/ukpga/1979/46)的条款保留了目录。
The purpose of the inventory is to identify sites of national importance and
provide information about them.When a garden and designed landscape is
included on the inventory it becomes a material consideration in the
planning process. This means that it has to be taken into account when
deciding planning applications.
清单的目的是查明具有国家重要性的场址，并提供有关这些场址的信息。当一个
花园和设计的景观包括在清单中，它成为一个物质考虑在规划过程中。这意味着
在决定规划应用时必须考虑到它。
To be added to the inventory, a site must be of national importance
and(see page 7). The most common type of site on the inventory is the
country estate landscape, developed for both pleasure and productive
purposes.
要加入清单，一个网站必须具有国家重要性和(见第 7 页)。目录中最常见的场地
类型是乡村地产景观，开发用于娱乐和生产目的。
Well-known examples include Hopetoun House in West Lothian, Culzean
Castle in South Ayrshire, and Haddo House in Aberdeenshire. However, the
inventory also recognises the significance of many other types of designed
landscape throughout Scotland. Sites on the inventory range in size from
one hectare to well over 1000 hectares and date from the medieval period
up until the 20th century.
著名的例子包括西洛锡安的 Hopetoun House，南埃尔郡的 Culzean Castle 和
阿伯丁郡的 Haddo House。然而，清单也承认了许多其他类型的景观设计在整
个苏格兰的重要性。清单上的遗址面积从 1 公顷到 1000 公顷不等，可以追溯到
中世纪直到 20 世纪。
They usually have a combination of different features such as built
structures,planting, open grounds, evidence of earth-moving(for example,
garden terraces), water management,archaeological remains and natural
landscape features, all of which may contribute to the value of a site.Within
the boundary of a garden and designed landscape, we may also designate
buildings as listed buildings or archaeological sites as scheduled
monuments. Scottish Natural Heritage may also recognise the scientific or
nature conservation value of sites.
它们通常具有不同的特征，例如建筑物、种植、开阔地面、移土证据(例如花园梯
田)、水质管理、考古遗迹和自然景观等，所有这些都可能有助提高遗址的价值。
在花园和设计景观的边界内，我们也可以将建筑物指定为列入清单的建筑物，或
将考古遗址指定为列入清单的古迹。苏格兰自然遗产也可以承认遗址的科学或自
然保护价值。
Above: The restored parterre garden at Pitmedden,Aberdeenshire © Historic Environment
Scotland
上图: 位于阿伯丁郡 Pitmedden 的修复花园
Assessing sites for the inventory
为库存评估场地
Above: The Necropolis, Glasgow © Historic Environment Scotland
上图: 墓地，格拉斯哥历史环境苏格兰
We assess each garden and designed landscape on its own merits.
我们评估每个花园和设计的景观各自的优点。
Our designation policy and selection guidance explains how we assess
gardens and designed landscapes for the inventory. See
historicenvironment.scot/designation-policy.
我们的指定政策和选择指南解释了我们如何评估花园和为清单设计景观。
To be included on the inventory, a garden and designed landscape must be
of national importance.
为了被列入清单，一个花园和设计景观必须具有国家重要性。
To decide if a site is of national
决定一个地点是否属于国家级
importance, we assess its:
重要性，我们评估它的:
– a rtistic interest
一种艺术兴趣
– historical interest
历史兴趣
– h orticultural interest
对园艺有兴趣
– a rchitetecural interest
- 建筑兴趣
– a rchaeological interest
考古方面的兴趣
– s cenic interest, and
利益，以及
– n ature conservation area interest.
- 自然保育区的利益。
We also assess the overall integrity.
我们还评估了整体的完整性。
The integrity of a garden and designed
一个完整的花园和设计
landscape means its wholeness and
景观意味着它的整体性
relates to the survival and condition of
与... 的生存和状况有关
features that contribute to its national
的特征，而这些特征有助于
importance. The inventory is not intended to recognise lost landscapes.
这份清单并不是为了确认失去的风景。
For each category, we measure interest on a scale ranging from
‘outstanding’ to ‘no interest’. Generally, the greater the number of
outstanding or high interests,the more likely the site is to be included on
the inventory. However, in some cases a garden and designed landscape
may be of such exceptional significance for only one area of interest that it
can also be regarded as nationally important.
对于每一个类别，我们用从“杰出”到“无兴趣”的范围来衡量兴趣。一般来说，
未完成或高兴趣的数量越多，网站被列入清单的可能性越大。然而，在某些情况
下，一个花园和设计的景观可能只对一个感兴趣的领域具有特殊的意义，它也可
以被认为是全国重要的。
Although a garden can be most widely known for its colourful flower
displays, this actually represents the most short-lived part of the
landscape.When assessing a site, we normally consider the more enduring
features.Typically, these include built structures,planting(including trees
with a lifespan of 100 years or more), open grounds,evidence of earth-
moving(for example,garden terraces), water management,archaeological
remains and natural landscape features. All of these may contribute to the
overall interest of the site.
虽然一个花园可以最广为人知的五颜六色的花展，这实际上代表了最短命的一部分景观。在评估一个地点时，我们通常会考虑更持久的特征。一般而言，这些建筑物
包括建筑物、种植(包括树木寿命达 100 年或以上)、开阔地面、移土证据(例如花园梯田)、水资源管理、考古遗迹和自然景观特色。所有这些都可能有助于整个遗址的
利益。
Above: Aberdour Castle and garden terraces, Fife © Historic Environment Scotland
上图: 阿伯杜尔城堡和花园露台，法夫历史环境苏格兰
Designation proposals and reviews
指定建议和审查
Anyone can ask us to designate a site or place, or to review an existing designation.
任何人都可以要求我们指定一个地点或地点，或者审查现有
的指定。
You can do any of these things by filling in our application form. The form is
available on our website at historicenvironment.scot/designation-
你可以通过填写我们的申请表来完成这些事情。申请表可以在我们的网站
historicenvironment.scot/designation-上找到
application or we can post you a copy.
或者我们可以寄给你一份副本。
Once we receive your form, we will acknowledge your application and
decide how best to deal with your request. In some circumstances we may
not go ahead with an application. If we decide not to go ahead, we will let
you know as soon as possible. You can find more detailed information on
how we assess sites and places, including our criteria and selection
guidance, in our designation policy at
一旦我们收到您的表格，我们将确认您的申请，并决定如何最好地处理您的要求。
在某些情况下，我们可能不会提出申请。如果我们决定不继续，我们会尽快通知
你。您可以在我们的指定政策中找到更多关于我们如何评估站点和地点的详细信
息，包括我们的标准和选择指南
historicenvironment.scot/designation-policy.
Historicenvironment.scot/指定政策。
Our assessments will normally include research and choosing which of the
heritage designations is most appropriate for the site that you’ve
proposed(see page 16 for information on all our heritage designations). We
may also visit the site.
我们的评估通常包括研究和选择哪些文物名称最适合您所提议的遗址(关于我们所
有文物名称的信息见第 16 页)。我们也可以参观这个遗址。
If we find that the site or place meets the criteria for designation, we will
publish a report on our online portal at portal.historicenvironment.scot,
giving information about our proposed decision.This is called a report of
handling and it normally includes an assessment of the site or place.
如果我们发现该网站或地点符合指定标准，我们将在我们的在线门户网站
portal.historicenvironment.scot 上发布一份报告，提供有关我们拟议决定的信
息。这就是所谓的处理报告，它通常包括对网站或地点的评估。
We normally consult those directly affected, including the owner, occupier
or tenant and the planning authority, before designating a site or
amending
a designation. We also normally welcome views from interested people or
groups through our website.
在指定用地或修订指定用地前，我们通常会谘询直接受影响的人士，包括业主、
占用人或承租人及规划当局。我们通常亦欢迎有兴趣的人士或团体透过我们的网
站提出意见。
We follow the same process for removing existing designations.
我们也遵循同样的流程来删除现有的名称。
We publish our final decision and the completed report of handling on our
online portal. See our website for more information about our service
standards and timescales for designation proposals.
我们在我们的在线门户网站上公布我们的最终决定和完成的处理报告。有关我们
的服务标准和时间表的更多信息，请参见我们的网站。
If you are the owner or occupier of all or part of the site or place, we will
make reasonable efforts to tell you if it has been designated or has had its
designation amended. The same applies to removals.
如你是该用地或地方的全部或部分的拥有人或占用人，我们会尽力告知你该用地
或地方是否已被指定或已被修改。这同样适用于拆除。
We will also tell the planning authority about these changes.
我们也会把这些变化告诉规划当局。
Left: One of the ancient Cadzow Oaks, Chatelherault,South Lanarkshire © Historic
Environment Scotland Below: Ornamental steps, Dawyck Botanic Garden,Scottish Borders ©
Historic Environment Scotland
左图: 古老的 Cadzow 橡树之一，南拉纳克郡的 Chatelherault 历史环境苏格兰下图: 装饰台阶，
Dawyck 植物园，苏格兰边区历史环境苏格兰
The inventory record
库存记录
Above: Balbirnie, Fife © Historic Environment Scotland
上图: Balbirnie，Fife Historic Environment 苏格兰
Each inventory garden and designed landscape is given a record.This consists of written information and a map
which shows the extent of the inventory boundary.
每个库存花园和设计景观给予一个记录。这包括书面信息和
显示库存边界范围的地图。
It is intended to help people understand why a garden and designed
landscape is of national importance. The record is usually accompanied by
photographs.
它旨在帮助人们理解为什么一个花园和设计的景观是国家的重要性。这份记录通
常伴随着照片。
You can search the records online on our website
portal.historicenvironment.scot.
你可以在我们的网站 portal.historicenvironment.scot 上搜索这些记录。
Inventory records are based on information gathered during the site visit
and research. Documentary evidence for a site can include historical
maps,estate records, photographs, designs and plans, and other material
including books,statistical records and magazine articles.
库存记录是基于网站访问和研究过程中收集的信息。遗址的文件证据可包括历史
地图、遗产记录、照片、设计和平面图，以及其他材料，包括书籍、统计记录和
杂志文章。
Each record includes a summary of why a site is important, information on
its location and setting, a site history,and information about different
aspects of the site, such as architectural features,parkland, woodland, or
water features.Earlier records may not be as complete as later records.
每个记录包括一个网站为什么重要的摘要，它的位置和设置的信息，网站的历史，
以及网站的不同方面的信息，如建筑特征，公园，林地，或水的特征。早期的记
录可能不如后来的记录完整。
Defining the boundary
界定边界
Each inventory garden and designed landscape has a map with a defined
boundary showing the geographical extent of the designation.
每个库存花园和设计景观都有一张地图，地图上有一个明确的边界，显示指定的
地理范围。
We use historic documents and maps,together with evidence collected
during the site visit, to help us define the
我们使用历史文献和地图，以及在实地考察期间收集的证据，来帮助我们定义
boundary, particularly in the case of
边界，特别是在
country house policies where there may be inner designed garden grounds
and parkland within a much larger agricultural estate.
乡村住宅政策，在一个规模大得多的农业区内，可能有内部设计的花园和公园。
Sometimes, features such as policy walls and gates clearly show where a
boundary can be drawn. In other circumstances, it is less clear-cut, and we
use our professional judgement to define the most logical boundary line.
有时候，政策墙和大门等特征会清楚地表明可以在哪里划定界限。在其他情况下，
它不是很明确，我们用我们的专业判断来定义最合乎逻辑的边界线。
Who currently owns the land does not affect how we define the boundary.
目前谁拥有这片土地并不影响我们如何界定边界。
Above: Detail from ‘A map of East Lothian, survey’d’ by J. Adair 1736, reproduced by
permission of the Trustees of the National Library of Scotland
上图: 细节来自“东洛锡安地图，由 j. Adair 1736 年勘测 d”，经苏格兰国家图书馆托管人许可复制
Living and working within an inventory garden and designed
landscape
生活和工作在一个库存花园和设计景观
When a garden and designed landscape is included on the inventory this does not mean that changes cannot be
made to it.
当一个花园和设计景观是包括在库存，这并不意味着不能作
出改变。
Gardens and designed landscapes are by their nature constantly
evolving.They cannot be ‘frozen in time’ and change is often necessary.
花园和设计的景观从本质上来说是不断发展的。它们不能“冻结在时间里”，改
变往往是必要的。
Being on the inventory does not mean that owners need to open their
property to the public. There are many privately owned sites on the
inventory which have no formal access arrangements. The Scottish
Outdoor Access Code has more information about access rights, at
outdooraccess-scotland.scot.
存货清单并不意味着业主需要向公众开放他们的财产。存货清单上有许多私人拥
有的网站没有正式的访问安排。苏格兰户外访问代码有更多关于访问权限的信息，
在户外访问-苏格兰。苏格兰。
Neither we nor the planning authority have to be consulted for work such
as:
无论是我们还是规划部门，都不需要为以下工作征求意见:
– d ay-to-day maintenance
日常维护
– planting
- 种植
– r emoving planting
移除种植
– r edesign which does not need planning permission, or – l andscaping
which does not need planning permission.
ー不需要规划许可的重新设计; 或ー l 不需要规划许可的绿化。
Being on the inventory does have an effect when a proposed development
needs planning permission. This type of development is set out in The
Town and Country Planning(Development Management Procedure)
(Scotland)Regulations 2013 as development which may affect a historic
garden and designed landscape.
当一个拟议的开发项目需要规划许可时，库存确实会产生影响。《2013 年城乡规
划(发展管理程序)(苏格兰)规例》把这类发展列为可能影响历史花园及设计景观的
发展。
If you want to make a change which needs planning permission, you need
to first contact your planning authority for guidance. If your plans involve a
listed building or scheduled monument,they can also advise you about any
other permission you might need.
如果你想做出需要规划许可的改变，你需要首先联系你的规划部门寻求指导。如
果你的规划涉及一个列出的建筑物或在册古迹，他们也可以建议你可能需要的任
何其他许可。
Where a development requires planning permission, the planning authority
will consult us for our view on the proposals.Our role is to provide advice
and expert knowledge.
如发展项目需要规划许可，规划监督会就有关建议谘询我们的意见。我们的角色
是提供建议和专业知识。
The planning authority grant planning permission and the decision rests
with them. They are also responsible for tree preservation orders(TPOs).
For advice on the implications of natural heritage designations, such as
Sites of Special Scientific Interest(SSSI), please contact Scottish Natural
Heritage at nature.scot.
规划当局授予规划许可，决定权在他们手中。他们还负责树木保护令(TPOs)。有
关自然遗产指定的意见，例如「具特殊科学价值地点」(SSSI) ，请联络苏格兰自
然遗产(nature.scot)。
The Forestry Commission Scotland may also consult us for our views on
woodland management issues within inventory sites, such as felling.
苏格兰林业委员会也可以征求我们对于森林管理问题的意见，例如伐木。
We are happy to provide advice and guidance on development affecting
inventory sites and you can find out more about this on our website.
我们很乐意就影响库存地点的开发提供建议和指导，你可以在我们的网站上找到更多相关信息。
Owners’ responsibilities
业主的责任
Responsibility for the routine maintenance of an inventory garden or
designed landscape lies with the owners and the occupiers.
业主和使用者有责任对库存花园或设计景观进行日常维护。
The owners of Scotland’s finest gardens and designed landscapes face
many challenges, ranging from climate change and managing the site as a
whole to dealing with specific problems such invasive species, tree and
plant diseases,or maintaining built structures.
苏格兰最好的花园和设计景观的所有者面临着许多挑战，从气候变化和管理整个
场地到处理具体问题，如入侵物种、树木和植物疾病，或维护建筑结构。
We support targeted and positive ways of managing gardens and designed
landscapes and welcome more comprehensive plans for managing the
sites now and into the future.
我们支持有针对性和积极的管理花园和设计景观的方法，并欢迎更全面的管理现
在和未来的网站计划。
We encourage owners to get professional advice on landscape
management issues and to find solutions which fit with the character of
their garden or designed landscape.
我们鼓励业主就园林管理问题征询专业意见，并寻找符合其园林或设计景观特色
的解决方案。
Below: Loch of Fyvie, Fyvie Castle, Aberdeenshire © Historic Environment Scotland Right:
View of Bayley Balfour Memorial Hut, Benmore Botanic Garaden,Argyll and Bute © Historic
Environment Scotland
下图: 阿伯丁郡费维湖，费维城堡，历史环境苏格兰右图: 贝利贝尔弗纪念小屋，本莫尔植物园，阿
盖尔和布特历史环境苏格兰贝利贝尔弗纪念小屋
Other heritage designations
其他文物名称
We are also responsible for designating other types of heritage assets, including listed buildings, scheduled
monuments and historic battlefields.
我们还负责指定其他类型的遗产资产，包括列入清单的建筑
物、纪念碑和历史战场。
We also advise the Scottish Government on designating sites as historic
marine protected areas. There is more information about these on our
website.
我们也建议苏格兰政府将这些地点指定为历史性的海洋保护区。在我们的网站上
有更多关于这些地区的信息。
Scotland has over 600 conservation areas which are designated by
planning authorities. Planning authorities must decide which parts of their
areas are of special architectural or historic interest, and they may
designate these as conservation areas. The public will normally be
consulted on any proposal to designate conservation areas or to change
their boundaries.
苏格兰有超过 600 个由规划部门指定的保护区。规划当局必须决定哪些地区具有
特殊的建筑或历史价值，他们可以指定这些地区为保护区。任何指定保育区或改
变其边界的建议，通常都会征询公众的意见。
World Heritage Sites are recorded by UNESCO(The United Nations
Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation) as places of outstanding
universal value in terms of their cultural or natural heritage
whc.unesco.org.
世界遗产被联合国教科文组织(联合国教科文组织)记录为具有突出的文化或自然
遗产普遍价值的地方。
Scotland currently has six World Heritage Sites. Information on these is
given on our website historicenvironment.scot/world-heritage-sites.
苏格兰目前有六个世界遗产地点。关于这些地点的信息可以在我们的网站
historicenvironment.scot/World-Heritage-Sites 上找到。
Searching for inventory sites,other designations and
our decisions
搜索库存网站，其他指定和我们的决定
You can search by keyword or map for all our designations on our online
portal at portal.historicenvironment.scot. You will also find information
about our designation decisions. If you are still not sure whether a site is
included on the inventory, you can email or phone us for help. Our contact
details are at the end of this booklet.
你可以通过关键字或地图在我们的门户网站 portal.historicenvironment.scot 上
搜索我们所有的设计。你也可以找到关于我们设计决定的信息。如果你仍然不确
定某个网站是否包含在清单中，你可以给我们发邮件或打电话寻求帮助。我们的
联系方式在这本小册子的最后。
You can also carry out map searches on Scotland’s Environment website,
where you can find more environmental information, including
conservation area boundaries: environment.gov.scot.
你也可以在苏格兰的环境网站上进行地图搜索，在那里你可以找到更多的环境信
息，包括自然保护区的边界: Environment.gov.scot。

Glasgow Botanic Gardens © Historic Environment Scotland

Departmental Public Body(NDPB)and a

of our roles is to manage the inventory of
gardens and designed landscapes.

(NDPB)和一个注册的苏格兰慈善机构

XI’AN DECLARATION
Xi’an DECLARATION 十一、宣言
ON THE CONSERVATION OF THE SETTING
关于环境保护问题
OF HERITAGE STRUCTURES, SITES AND AREAS
文物建筑物、地点及范围
Adopted in Xi’an, China
采用于中国西安
by the 15th General Assembly of ICOMOS
国际科学文化组织第十五届大会
on 21 October 2005
2005 年 10 月 21 日
Final version - 22.10.2005
最终版本 -22.10.2005
Preamble
序言
Meeting in the ancient city of Xi’an (China) on 17-21
st
October 2005, at the invitation of ICOMOS
China on the occasion of 15
th
General Assembly of ICOMOS and the celebrations marking the 40
th
anniversary of its longstanding endeavour to ensure the safeguard and conservation of the World’s
cultural heritage as part of its sustainable and human development;
2005 年 10 月 17 日至 21 日在中国西安古城举行会议，应 ICOMOS 中国的邀请，参加 ICOMOS 中
国第 15 届大会，并庆祝 ICOMOS 长期致力于确保保护和保存世界文化遗产作为其可持续和人类发展
的一部分的 40 周年;
Benefiting from the broad range of cases and reflections shared during the General Assembly’s
International Symposium on Monuments and Sites in their Settings – Conserving Cultural Heritage
in Changing Townscapes and Landscapes and learning from a broad range of experiences from
China and world-wide authorities, institutions and specialists in providing adequate care and
management of heritage structures, sites and areas such as historic cities, landscapes, seascapes,
cultural routes and archaeological sites in the context of accelerated change and development;
受益于大会纪念碑和遗址环境国际研讨会期间交流的广泛案例和思考——在不断变化的城镇景观和景
观中保护文化遗产，并学习中国和世界各地当局、机构和专家在加速变化和发展的背景下提供充分照
料和管理历史城市、景观、海景、文化路线和考古遗址等遗产结构、遗址和地区的广泛经验;
Taking note of the international and professional interest for the conservation of the settings of
monuments and sites as expressed in the International Charter for the Conservation and
Restoration of Monuments and Sites – the Venice Charter (1964) – and in the many texts it has
inspired, particularly through ICOMOS National and International Committees, as well as the Nara
Document on Authenticity (1994) and conclusions and recommendations of international meetings
like the Hoi An Declaration on the Conservation of Historic Districts in Asia (2003), the Declaration
on the Recovery of Bam’s Cultural Heritage (2004), and the Seoul Declaration on Tourism in Asia’s
Historic Towns and Areas (2005);
注意到《保护和修复古迹和遗址国际宪章》(1964 年)所表明的国际和专业人士对保护古迹和遗址环境
的兴趣，特别是通过国际古迹协商组织国家和国际委员会，以及关于真实性的奈良文件(1994 年)和国
际会议的结论和建议，如《亚洲历史街区保护海安宣言》(2003 年)、《恢复巴姆文化遗产宣言》
(2004 年)和《亚洲历史城镇和地区旅游问题首尔宣言》(2005 年) ;
Noting the references to the concept of setting in UNESCO conventions and recommendations like
the Recommendation concerning the Safeguarding of Beauty and Character of Landscapes and
Sites (1962), the Recommendation concerning the Preservation of Cultural Property Endangered by
Public or Private Works (1968), the Recommendation concerning the Safeguarding and
Contemporary Role of Historic Areas (1976), the Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible
Cultural Heritage, (2003) and more specifically the World Heritage Convention (1972) and its
Operational Guidelines, where setting is listed as an attribute of authenticity and as needing
protection through the establishment of buffer zones, and the ongoing opportunity this brings for
international and interdisciplinary co-operation between ICOMOS, UNESCO and other partners and
for developments on topics like authenticity or the conservation of historic urban landscapes
expressed in the Vienna Memorandum (2005).
注意到提及教科文组织各项公约和建议中确定的概念，如《关于保护景观和遗址的美丽和特征的建议》
(1962 年)、《关于保护因公共或私人工程而濒危的文化财产的建议》(1968 年)、《关于保护历史地
区及其当代作用的建议》(1976 年)、《保护非物质文化遗产公约》 ,(2003 年) ，更具体地说，是《世
界遗产公约》(1972 年)及其《业务准则》 ，其中将环境设置列为真实性的一个属性，需要通过建立
缓冲区加以保护，这为国际化学品卫生组织、教科文组织和其他伙伴之间的国际和跨学科合作以及在
《维也纳备忘录》(2005 年)所述的真实性或历史城市景观保护等专题方面的发展带来了持续的机会。
- 1 -
-1 -
Stressing the need to address adequately the rapid or incremental transformation of cities,
landscapes and heritage routes which result from changes in lifestyles, agriculture, development,
tourism or large-scale disasters of natural or human origin, and to recognise, protect and sustain
adequately the meaningful presence of heritage structures, sites and areas in their settings as a
way to reduce the threat these transformation processes constitute against the cultural heritage in
the full richness of its authenticity, meaning, values, integrity and diversity,
强调需要适当处理因生活方式、农业、发展、旅游业或自然或人为原因的大规模灾害而导致的城市、
景观和遗产路线的迅速或渐进变化问题，并充分认识、保护和维持遗产结构、遗址和地区在其环境中
的有意义存在，以此减少这些变化过程在文化遗产的真实性、含义、价值观、完整性和多样性方面对
其构成的威胁,
Participants of the 15
th
General Assembly of ICOMOS adopt the following Declaration of principles
and recommendations, addressing it to intergovernmental and non-governmental organisations,
national and local authorities and all institutions and specialists able to contribute through legislation,
policies, planning processes and management to better protect and conserve the world’s heritage
structures, sites and areas in their settings.
奥斯陆协议组织第十五届大会与会者通过了以下原则和建议宣言，提交给政府间组织和非政府组织、
国家和地方当局以及所有能够通过立法、政策、规划进程和管理作出贡献的机构和专家，以便更好地
保护和养护世界遗产结构、遗址和地区。
Acknowledge the contribution of setting to the significance of heritage monuments, sites
and areas
承认环境对文物古迹、遗址和地区的重要性的贡献
1. The setting of a heritage structure, site or area is defined as the immediate and
extended environment that is part of, or contributes to, its significance and
distinctive character.
文物建筑物、遗址或地区的环境定义为直接和延伸的环境，是其重要性和独特性的一部分，或
有助于其独特性。
Beyond the physical and visual aspects, the setting includes interaction with the natural
environment; past or present social or spiritual practices, customs, traditional knowledge,
use or activities and other forms of intangible cultural heritage aspects that created and
form the space as well as the current and dynamic cultural, social and economic context.
除了物质和视觉方面之外，环境还包括与自然环境的互动; 过去或现在的社会或精神习俗、
习俗、传统知识、使用或活动以及其他形式的非物质文化遗产方面，这些方面创造和形成
了空间以及当前和动态的文化、社会和经济环境。
2. Heritage structures, sites or areas of various scales, including individual
buildings or designed spaces, historic cities or urban landscapes, landscapes,
seascapes, cultural routes and archaeological sites, derive their significance and
distinctive character from their perceived social and spiritual, historic, artistic,
aesthetic, natural, scientific, or other cultural values. They also derive their
significance and distinctive character from their meaningful relationships with
their physical, visual, spiritual and other cultural context and settings.
各种规模的文物建筑物、遗址或地区，包括个别建筑物或设计空间、历史城市或城市景观、景
观、海景、文化路线和考古遗址，其重要性和独特性源自其感知到的社会和精神、历史、
艺术、美学、自然、科学或其他文化价值。它们的重要性和独特性也来源于它们与物质、
视觉、精神和其他文化背景和环境之间有意义的关系。
These relationships can be the result of a conscious and planned creative act, spiritual
belief, historical events, use or a cumulative and organic process over time through
cultural traditions.
这些关系可以是有意识和有计划的创造行为、精神信仰、历史事件、使用或随着时间的推
移通过文化传统的累积和有机过程的结果。
Understand, document and interpret the settings in diverse contexts
理解、记录和解释不同上下文中的设置
3. Understanding, documenting and interpreting the setting is essential to defining
and appreciating the heritage significance of any structure, site or area.
理解、记录和解释环境对于定义和欣赏任何建筑、地点或区域的遗产意义都是至关重要的。
The definition of setting requires an understanding of the history, evolution and
character of the surrounds of the heritage resource. Defining the setting is a process of
considering multiple factors to include the character of the arrival experience and the
heritage resource itself.
环境的定义要求对遗产资源的历史、演变和周围环境的特征有所了解。定义环境是一个考
虑多种因素的过程，包括抵达体验的特点和遗产资源本身。
4. Understanding the setting in an inclusive way requires a multi-disciplinary
approach and the use of diverse information sources.
以包容性的方式理解环境需要一个多学科的方法和使用不同的信息来源。
Sources include formal records and archives, artistic and scientific descriptions, oral
history and traditional knowledge, the perspectives of local and associated communities
as well as the analysis of views and vistas.
资料来源包括正式记录和档案、艺术和科学描述、口述历史和传统知识、当地社区和相关
社区的观点以及对观点和前景的分析。
- 2 -
- 2 -
Cultural traditions, rituals, spiritual practices and concepts as well as history, topography,
natural environment values, use and other factors contribute to create the full range of a
setting’s tangible and intangible values and dimensions. The definition of settings should
carefully articulate the character and values of the setting and its relationship to the
heritage resource.
文化传统、仪式、精神实践和观念，以及历史、地形、自然环境价值观、使用和其他因素
有助于创造一个环境的有形和无形的价值和维度的全面范围。环境的定义应该仔细阐述环
境的特征和价值，以及它与遗产资源的关系。
Develop planning tools and practices to conserve and manage settings
开发保护和管理环境的规划工具和实践
5. The implementation of effective planning and legislative tools, policies, strategies
and practices to sustainably manage settings requires consistency and continuity
in application, whilst reflecting the local or cultural contexts in which they
function.
为可持续地管理环境而实施有效的规划和立法工具、政策、战略和做法，需要在应用方面保持
一致性和连续性，同时反映其发挥作用的当地或文化背景。
Tools to manage settings include specific legislative measures, professional training,
development of comprehensive conservation and management plans or systems, and
use of adequate heritage impact assessment methods.
管理环境的工具包括具体的立法措施、专业培训、制定全面的养护和管理计划或制度，以
及使用适当的遗产影响评估方法。
6. Legislation, regulation and guidelines for the protection, conservation and
management of heritage structures, sites and areas should provide for the
establishment of a protection or buffer zone around them that reflects and
conserves the significance and distinctive character of their setting.
有关保护、保存和管理文物建筑物、遗址和地区的立法、规例和指引应规定在其周围设立一个
保护区或缓冲区，以反映和保存其环境的重要性和独特性。
7. Planning instruments should include provisions to effectively control the impact
of incremental or rapid change on settings.
规划工具应包括有效控制渐进或快速变化对环境的影响的条款。
Significant skylines, sight lines and adequate distance between any new public or
private development and heritage structures, sites and areas are key aspects to assess
in the prevention of inappropriate visual and spatial encroachments or land use in
significant settings.
重要的天际线、视线以及任何新的公共或私人发展和文物建筑物、地点和区域之间的适当
距离，是评估在重要环境中防止不适当的视觉和空间侵犯或土地使用的关键方面。
8. Heritage impact assessments should be required for all new development
impacting on the significance of heritage structures, sites and areas and on their
settings.
所有影响文物结构、地点和区域及其环境的重要性的新发展项目，都需要进行文物影响评估。
Development within the setting of heritage structures, sites and areas should positively
interpret and contribute to its significance and distinctive character.
在文物建筑、遗址和地区的背景下进行发展，应积极诠释和促进其重要性和独特性。
Monitor and manage change affecting settings
监控和管理影响环境的变化
9. The rate of change and the individual and cumulative impacts of change and
transformation on the settings of heritage structures, sites and areas is an
ongoing process which must be monitored and managed.
变化的速度以及变化和转变对遗产结构、遗址和地区环境的个别和累积影响是一个持续的过程，
必须加以监测和管理。
Incremental as well as rapid transformation of the urban or rural landscapes, the ways of
life, the economies or the natural environment can substantially or irretrievably affect the
authentic contribution that the setting makes to the significance of a heritage structure,
site or area.
城市或乡村景观、生活方式、经济或自然环境的渐进和迅速转变，可能会对环境对遗产结
构、遗址或地区的重要性所作的真正贡献产生重大或不可挽回的影响。
10. Change to the setting of heritage structures, sites and areas should be managed
to retain cultural significance and distinctive character.
文物建筑物、遗址和地区的环境改变时，应注意保留其文化意义和特色。
Managing change to the setting of heritage structures, sites and areas need not
necessarily prevent or obstruct change.
管理文物结构、遗址和地区的环境变化不一定要防止或阻碍变化。
- 3 -
-3 -
11. Monitoring should define approaches and actions to appreciate and measure as
well as prevent or remedy decay, loss of significance or trivialisation and propose
improvement in conservation, management and interpretation practices.
监测应确定方法和行动，以了解和衡量以及防止或补救腐烂、重要性丧失或琐碎化，并提出改
进养护、管理和解释做法的建议。
Qualitative and quantifiable indicators should be developed to assess the contribution of
the setting to the significance of a heritage structure, site or area.
应制订定性和量化指标，以评估环境对文物结构、遗址或地区重要性的贡献。
Indicators for monitoring should cover physical aspects such as intrusion on views,
skylines or open spaces, air pollution, sound pollution, as well as economic, social and
cultural dimensions.
监测指标应包括物理方面，例如对视野、天际线或开放空间的侵犯、空气污染、声音污染
以及经济、社会和文化方面。
Work with local, interdisciplinary and international communities for co-operation and
awareness in conserving and managing settings
与当地、跨学科和国际社区合作，促进在保护和管理环境方面的合作和意识
12. Co-operation and engagement with associated and local communities is essential
as part of developing sustainable strategies for the conservation and
management of settings.
与相关社区和当地社区的合作和参与是制定可持续发展战略的一部分，以保护和管理环境。
Inter-disciplinary engagement should be encouraged as standard practice in conserving
and managing settings. Relevant cultural heritage fields include architecture, urban and
regional planning, landscape planning, engineering, anthropology, history, archaeology,
ethnology, curation and archives.
应鼓励跨学科参与，将其作为养护和管理环境的标准做法。相关的文化遗产领域包括建筑、
城市和区域规划、景观规划、工程学、人类学、历史、考古学、民族学、策划和档案。
Co-operation with institutions and specialists in the field of natural heritage should also
be encouraged as an integral part of good practice for the identification, protection,
presentation and interpretation of heritage structures, sites or areas in their setting.
还应鼓励与自然遗产领域的机构和专家合作，作为在其环境中确定、保护、陈述和解释遗
产结构、遗址或地区的良好做法的一个组成部分。
13. Professional training, interpretation, community education and public awareness
should be encouraged to support such co-operation and sharing of knowledge as
well as to promote conservation goals, improve the efficiency of the protection
tools, management plans and other instruments.
应鼓励专业培训、口译、社区教育和提高公众认识，以支持这种合作和知识共享，并促进保护
目标，提高保护工具、管理计划和其他文书的效率。
The experience, knowledge and tools developed through the conservation of individual
heritage structures, sites and areas should be extended to complement the
management of their setting.
通过保护个别文物建筑物、遗址和地区而发展出来的经验、知识和工具，应加以扩展，以
配合对其环境的管理。
Economic resources should be allocated to the research, assessment and strategic
planning of the conservation and management of setting of heritage structures, sites and
areas.
应拨出经济资源，研究、评估和策略性规划文物建筑物、遗址和地区的保育和管理。
Awareness of the significance of the setting in its various dimensions is the shared
responsibility of professionals, institutions, associated and local communities, who
should take into account the tangible and intangible dimensions of settings when making
decisions.
认识到环境的各个方面的重要性是专业人员、机构、联系社区和地方社区的共同责任，他
们在作出决定时应考虑到环境的有形和无形方面。
Adopted in Xi’an (China) on the 21
st
October, 2005.
2005 年 10 月 21 日在西安(中国)通过。
