Tentative Lists as a planning and evaluation tool
暂定名单作为规划和评估工具
70. Tentative Lists are a useful and important planning tool for States
Parties, the World Heritage Committee, the Secretariat, and the Advisory
Bodies, as they provide an indication of future nominations.
暂定名单是缔约国、世界遗产委员会、秘书处和咨询机构的一个有用和重
要的规划工具，因为它们提供了未来提名的指示。
71. Tentative Lists should be established selectively and on the basis of
evidence that supports potential Outstanding Universal Value. States Parties are
encouraged to consult the analyses of both the World Heritage List and
Tentative Lists prepared at the request of the Committee by ICOMOS and
IUCN to identify the gaps in the World Heritage List. These analyses could
enable States Parties to compare themes, regions, geo-cultural groupings and
bio-geographic provinces for prospective World Heritage properties. States
Parties are encouraged to seek as early as possible upstream advice from the
Advisory Bodies during the development of their Tentative Lists as appropriate.
暂定名单应有选择性地建立，并基于支持潜在的突出普遍价值的证据。鼓
励缔约国参考应委员会要求由国际化学品卫生组织和自然保护联盟
编写的世界遗产名单和暂定名单的分析，以查明世界遗产名单中的
差距。这些分析可以
使缔约国能够比较主
题，地区，地理文化
群体和生物地理省份
的未来世界遗产属性。
鼓励缔约国在制定暂
定名单期间尽早征求
咨询机构的上游意见。

73. States Parties are encouraged to harmonize their Tentative Lists at regional and
thematic levels. Harmonization of Tentative Lists is the process whereby States Parties,
with the assistance of the Advisory Bodies, collectively assess their respective Tentative
List to review gaps and identify common themes. The harmonization has considerable
potential to generate fruitful dialogue between States Parties and different cultural
communities, promoting respect for common heritage and cultural diversity and can
result in improved Tentative Lists, new nominations from States Parties and cooperation
amongst groups of States Parties in the preparation of nominations.
鼓励缔约国在区域和专题层面协调其暂定清单。协调暂定名单是缔约国在咨询机
构的协助下集体评估各自暂定名单以审查差距和确定共同主题的过程。
这种协调具有相当大的潜力，可以在缔约国和不同文化群体之间开展富
有成果的对话，促进对共同遗产和文化多样性的尊重，并可以改进暂定
名单、缔约国提出新的提名以及缔约国集团在编写提名方面开展合作。
Assistance and Capacity Building for States Parties in the preparation of
Tentative Lists
协助缔约国编制暂定名单和进行能力建设
74. To implement the Global Strategy, cooperative efforts in capacity
building and training for diverse groups of beneficiaries may be necessary to
assist States Parties in acquiring and/or consolidating expertise in the
preparation, updating and harmonization of their Tentative List and the
preparation of nominations.
为了执行《全球战略》 ，可能需要在能力建设和培训不同受益群体方面
开展合作努力，以协助缔约国在编制、更新和统一暂定名单以及编
制提名方面获得和/或巩固专门知识。
75. International Assistance may be requested by States Parties for the purpose
of preparing, updating and harmonizing Tentative Lists (see Chapter VII). This can
include use of the Upstream Process (see Paragraph 121).
缔约国可请求提供国际援助，以便编制、更新和统一暂定名单(见第七章)。这
可以包括使用上游程序(见第 121 段)。
76. The Advisory Bodies and the Secretariat will use the opportunity of
evaluation missions to hold regional training workshops to assist under-
represented States in the methods of preparation of their Tentative List and
nominations.
咨询机构和秘书处将利用评价特派团的机会举办区域培训讲习班，协助任
职人数不足的国家拟订其暂定名单和提名的方法。

Decision 24 COM VI.2.3.5(ii)

II.D Criteria for the assessment of Outstanding Universal Value
二、评估突出普遍价值的标准
77. The Committee considers a property as having Outstanding Universal
Value (see paragraphs 49-53) if the property meets one or more of the following
criteria. Nominated properties shall therefore:
如物业符合下列一项或多项标准，委员会认为该物业具有突出的普遍价值
(见第 49 至 53 段)。因此，获提名的物业须:
(i) represent a masterpiece of human creative genius;
代表人类创意天才的杰作;
(ii) exhibit an important interchange of human values, over a span of time
or within a cultural area of the world, on developments in architecture or
technology, monumental arts, town-planning or landscape design;
在建筑或科技发展、纪念碑艺术、城市规划或景观设计方面，展示人类
价值观在不同时期或世界文化区内的重要交流;
(iii) bear a
unique or at least

cultural tradition or to a
civilization which is

disappeared;
对于一种文化传

少是特殊的
见证;

technological ensemble or landscape which illustrates (a) significant stage(s) in
human history;
是展示(a)人类历史上重要阶段的一类建筑物、建筑物或科技组合或
景观的杰出例子;
(v) be an outstanding example of a traditional human settlement, land-
use, or sea-use which is representative of a culture (or cultures), or human
interaction with the environment especially when it has become vulnerable
under the impact of irreversible change;
是传统人类住区、土地使用或海洋使用的突出例子，代表一种文化
(或多种文化) ，或人类与环境的互动，特别是当环境在不可逆
转的变化影响下变得脆弱时;
(vi) be directly or tangibly associated with events or living traditions, with
ideas, or with beliefs, with artistic and literary works of outstanding universal
significance. (The Committee considers that this criterion should preferably be used
in conjunction with other criteria);
直接或有形地与具有突出普遍意义的艺术和文学作品的事件或生活传统、
思想或信仰联系在一起。(委员会认为这项准则最好与其他准则
一并使用) ;
These criteria were formerly
presented as two separate sets
of criteria - criteria (i) - (vi)
for cultural heritage and (i) -

这些准则以前是作为两套独

The 6th extraordinary session of

(Decision 6 EXT.COM 5.1)

EXT.COM 5.1 号决定)
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 29

(vii) contain superlative natural phenomena or areas of exceptional natural beauty and
aesthetic importance;
包含最高级的自然现象或具有特殊的自然美和审美重要性的区域;
(viii) be outstanding examples representing major stages of earth's history, including the record
of life, significant on-going geological processes in the development of landforms, or significant
geomorphic or physiographic features;
代表地球历史主要阶段的杰出例子，包括生命的记录、地貌发展过

是在陆地、淡水、沿海和海洋生态系统以及动植物群落的演变和发

含有最重要和最重要的自然生境，以便在原地保护生物多样性，包
括那些含有从科学或保育角度而言具有突出普遍价值的受威胁
物种的生境。
78. To be deemed of Outstanding Universal Value, a property must also meet the conditions of
integrity and/or authenticity and must have an adequate protection and management system to ensure
its safeguarding.
要被视为具有突出的普遍价值，财产还必须符合完整性和/或真实性的条
件，并必须有适当的保护和管理制度，以确保其得到保护。
II.E Authenticity and/or integrity
二、真实性和/或完整性
Authenticity
真实性
79. Properties nominated under criteria (i) to (vi) must meet the conditions of authenticity. Annex
4, which includes the Nara Document on Authenticity, provides a practical basis for examining the
authenticity of such properties and is summarized below.
根据准则(i)至(vi)提名的物业必须符合真实性的条件。附件 4，其中包括奈
良文件的真实性，为审查这些财产的真实性提供了一个实际的基础，
概述如下。
80. The ability to understand the value attributed to the heritage depends on the Decision 39 COM 11
degree to which information sources about this value may be understood as
80.理解遗产价值的能力取决于决策 39 COM 11 的程度，关于这个价值的信息来源可以理解为
credible or truthful. Knowledge and understanding of these sources of
information, in relation to original and subsequent characteristics of the
cultural heritage, and their meaning as accumulated over time, are the
requisite bases for assessing all aspects of authenticity.
可信的或真实的。了解和理解这些信息来源与文化遗产的原始和后
续特征及其随着时间的推移而积累的含义，是评估真实性的所有方
面的必要基础。
81. Judgments about value attributed to cultural heritage, as well as the credibility of related
information sources, may differ from culture to culture, and even within the same culture. The respect
due to all cultures requires that cultural heritage must be considered and judged primarily within the
cultural contexts to which it belongs.
对文化遗产价值的判断，以及相关信息来源的可信度，可能因文化而异，
甚至在同一文化中也是如此。对所有文化的尊重要求文化遗产必须
首先在它所属的文化背景下被考虑和判断。
82. Depending on the type of cultural heritage, and its cultural context, properties may be understood to
meet the conditions of authenticity if their cultural values (as recognized in the nomination criteria
proposed) are truthfully and credibly expressed through a variety of attributes including:
根据文化遗产的类型及其文化背景，如果其文化价值(如提议的提名标准所承
认的)通过各种属性如实和可信地表达，包括:
• form and design;
形式及设计;
• materials and substance;
材料和物质;
• use and function;
使用和功能;
• traditions, techniques and management systems;
传统、技术和管理系统;
• location and setting;
位置及环境;
• language, and other forms of intangible heritage;
语言及其他形式的非物质文化遗产;
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 30
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 30
• spirit and feeling; and
精神和感情; 以及
• other internal and external factors.
其他内部及外部因素。
83. Attributes such as spirit and feeling do not lend themselves easily to
practical applications of the conditions of authenticity, but nevertheless are
important indicators of character and sense of place, for example, in
communities maintaining tradition and cultural continuity.
诸如精神和情感等属性不容易用于真实性条件的实际应用，但却是性格和
地方感的重要指标，例如在保持传统和文化连续性的社区中。
84. The use of all these sources permits elaboration of the specific artistic,
historic, social, and scientific dimensions of the cultural heritage being
examined. “Information sources” are defined as all physical, written, oral, and
figurative sources, which make it possible to know the nature, specificities,
meaning, and history of the cultural heritage.
所有这些来源的使用允许详细阐述具体的艺术，历史，社会和科学方面的
文化遗产正在审查。“信息来源”的定义是所有的物理、书面、口
头和比喻的来源，使人们能够了解文化遗产的性质、特殊性、意义
和历史。
85. When the conditions of authenticity are considered in preparing a
nomination for a property, the State Party should first identify all of the
applicable significant attributes of authenticity. The statement of authenticity
should assess the degree to which authenticity is present in, or expressed by,
each of these significant attributes.
当在准备财产提名时考虑到真实性的条件时，缔约国应首先确定所有适用
的真实性的重要属性。真实性声明应该评估每个重要属性的真实性
存在或表达的程度。
86. In relation to authenticity, the reconstruction of archaeological remains
or historic buildings or districts is justifiable only in exceptional circumstances.
Reconstruction is acceptable only on the basis of complete and detailed
documentation and to no extent on conjecture.
就真实性而言，重建考古遗迹或历史建筑物或地区只有在特殊情况下才是
合理的。重建是可以接受的，只有在完整和详细的文件和在任何程
度上的推测的基础上。
Integrity
诚信
87. All properties nominated for inscription on the World Heritage List shall
satisfy the conditions of integrity.
被提名列入世界遗产名录的所有财产均应符合完整性条件。
88. Integrity is a measure of the wholeness and intactness of the natural
and/or cultural heritage and its attributes. Examining the conditions of integrity,
therefore requires assessing the extent to which the property:
完整性是衡量自然和/或文化遗产及其属性的完整性和完整性的标准。检
查完整性的条件，因此需要评估财产的程度:
a) includes all elements necessary to express its Outstanding
Universal Value;
包括所有必要的元素，以表达其突出的普遍价值;
b) is of
adequate size to ensure
the complete
representation of the
features and processes
which convey the
property’s significance;
有足够的大小，
以确保完
整的表现
特征和过
程，传达
财产的重
要性;
c) suffers
from adverse effects of
development and/or
neglect.
因发展及/或疏
忽而受到
不良影响。
This should be
presented in a
statement of
integrity.
这应该在一份
完整的声明中
提出。
89. For properties
nominated under criteria
(i) to (vi), the physical
fabric of the property
and/or its significant

good condition, and the
impact of deterioration

该物业的物理

个重要的比例的元素必须传达的总体价值传达的财产应包括。文化景
观、历史城镇或其他生活资产中存在的关系和动态功能也应该得到维
护。

90. For all properties nominated under criteria (vii) - (x), bio-physical processes Decision 43 COM
11A and landform features should be relatively intact. However, it is recognized
90.对于根据标准(vii)-(x)提名的所有物业，生物物理过程第 43 COM 11A 号决定和地貌特征应
该相对完整。然而，它被认可了吗
that no area is totally pristine and that all natural areas are in a dynamic
state, and to some extent involve contact with people. Biological
diversity and cultural diversity can be closely linked and interdependent
and human activities, including those of traditional societies, local
communities and indigenous peoples, often occur in natural areas. These
activities may be consistent with the Outstanding Universal Value of the
area where they are ecologically sustainable.
没有一个地区是完全原始的，所有的自然地区都处于一种动态的状
态，并且在某种程度上涉及到与人的接触。生物多样性和文化多样
性可以密切联系和相互依存，人类活动，包括传统社会、地方社区
和原住民的活动，往往发生在自然地区。这些活动可能与生态可持
续发展区域的普遍价值相一致。
91. In addition, for properties nominated under criteria (vii) to (x), a corresponding condition of
integrity has been defined for each criterion.
此外，就根据准则(vii)至(x)提名的物业而言，每项准则都定义了相应的完
整性条件。
92. Properties proposed under criterion (vii) should be of Outstanding Universal Value and include
areas that are essential for maintaining the beauty of the property. For example, a property whose
scenic value depends on a waterfall, would meet the conditions of integrity if it includes adjacent
catchment and downstream areas that are integrally linked to the maintenance of the aesthetic qualities
of the property.
根据准则(vii)提出的物业应具有突出的普遍价值，并包括对保持物业的美
观至关重要的范畴。例如，景观价值取决于瀑布的物业，如果包括
邻近的集水区和下游地区，而这些地区与保持物业的美学品质有着
密不可分的联系，就符合完整性的条件。
93. Properties proposed under criterion (viii) should contain all or most of the key interrelated and
interdependent elements in their natural relationships. For example, an “ice age” area would meet the
conditions of integrity if it includes the snow field, the glacier itself and samples of cutting patterns,
deposition and colonization (e.g. striations, moraines, pioneer stages of plant succession, etc.); in the
case of volcanoes, the magmatic series should be complete and all or most of the varieties of effusive
rocks and types of eruptions be represented.
根据准则(viii)提出的属性应包含其自然关系中所有或大部分关键的相互关
联和相互依存的要素。例如，如果一个”冰河时代”地区包括雪地、
冰川本身和切割模式、沉积和殖民化的样本(如条纹、冰碛、植物
演替的先驱阶段等) ，那么它就符合完整性条件; 就火山而言，岩浆
系列应该是完整的，所有或大部分喷发岩石和喷发类型的样本都应
该包括在内。
94. Properties proposed under criterion (ix) should have sufficient size and contain the necessary
elements to demonstrate the key aspects of processes that are essential for the long term conservation of the
ecosystems and the biological diversity they contain. For example, an area of tropical rain forest would
meet the conditions of integrity if it includes a certain amount of variation in elevation above sea level,
changes in topography and soil types, patch systems and naturally regenerating patches; similarly a coral
reef should include, for example, seagrass, mangrove or other adjacent ecosystems that regulate nutrient
and sediment inputs into the reef.
根据标准(九)提出的财产应有足够的规模，并含有必要的要素，以证明对于长
期养护生态系统及其所包含的生物多样性至关重要的进程的关键方面。
例如，如果一个热带雨林区域的海拔高度、地形和土壤类型的变化、
斑块系统和自然再生斑块有一定程度的变化，那么它就符合完整性条
件; 同样，一个珊瑚礁应该包括例如海草、红树林或其他相邻的生态系
统，这些生态系统调节营养物质和沉积物输入到珊瑚礁中。
95. Properties proposed under criterion (x) should be the most important properties for the conservation of
biological diversity. Only those properties which are the most biologically diverse and/or representative are
likely to meet this criterion. The properties should contain habitats for maintaining the most diverse fauna and
flora characteristic of the bio-geographic province and ecosystems under consideration. For example, a tropical
savannah would meet the conditions of integrity if it includes a complete assemblage of co-evolved herbivores
and plants; an island ecosystem should include habitats for maintaining endemic biota; a property containing
wide ranging species should be large enough to include the most critical habitats essential to ensure the survival
of viable populations of those species; for an area containing migratory species, seasonal breeding and nesting
sites, and migratory routes, wherever they are located, should be adequately protected.
根据标准(x)提出的特性应该是保护生物多样性的最重要特性。只有那些最具生物
多样性和/或代表性的特性才可能符合这一标准。这些特性应该包含保持
生物地理区域和考虑中的生态系统的最多样化的动植物群特征的栖息地。
例如，热带草原如果包括共同进化的草食动物和植物的完整集合，就符合
完整性条件; 岛屿生态系统应包括维持地方性生物群的生境; 包含广泛物种
的财产应大到足以包括确保这些物种可生存种群存活所必需的最关键的生
境; 包含迁徙物种、季节性繁殖和筑巢地点以及迁徙路线的地区，无论它
们位于何处，都应得到充分保护。

实施《世界遗产公约》的操作指南 32
II.F Protection and management
二. f 保护和管理
96. Protection and management of World Heritage properties should ensure that
their Outstanding Universal Value, including the conditions of integrity and/or
authenticity at the time of inscription, are sustained or enhanced over time. A
regular review of the general state of conservation of properties, and thus also their
Outstanding Universal Value, shall be done within a framework of monitoring
processes for World Heritage properties, as specified within the Operational
Guidelines
3
.
世界遗产财产的保护和管理应确保其突出的普遍价值，包括登记时的完整性
和/或真实性条件，随着时间的推移得到维持或加强。应在《业务准
则》3 规定的世界遗产财产监测程序框架内，定期审查财产保护的一
般状况，从而也审查其突出的普遍价值。
97. All properties inscribed on the World Heritage List must have adequate
long-term legislative, regulatory, institutional and/or traditional protection and
management to ensure their safeguarding. This protection should include
adequately delineated boundaries. Similarly States Parties should demonstrate
adequate protection at the national, regional, municipal, and/or traditional level
for the nominated property. They should append appropriate texts to the
nomination with a clear explanation of the way this protection operates to
protect the nominated property. Information on protection and management
should also be included at the stage of the Preliminary Assessment.
列入世界遗产名录的所有财产都必须得到充分的长期立法、监管、体制和
/或传统保护和管理，以确保其得到保护。这种保护应该包括充分
划定的边界。同样，缔约国应在国家、地区、市政和/或传统层面
对提名的财产表现出足够的保护。他们应该在提名后面附上适当的
文本，清楚地解释这种保护如何保护被提名的财产。有关保护和管
理的资料亦应包括在初步评审阶段。
Legislative, regulatory and contractual protection measures
立法、规管及合约保障措施
98. Legislative and regulatory measures at national and local levels should assure
the protection of the property from social, economic and other pressures or changes that
might negatively impact the Outstanding Universal Value, including the integrity and/or
authenticity of the property. States Parties should also assure the full and effective
implementation of such measures.
国家和地方各级的立法和管制措施应确保保护财产不受社会、经济和其他压力或
可能对尚未实现的普遍价值，包括财产的完整性和(或)真实性产生不利影
响的变化的影响。缔约国也应确保这些措施的全面和有效实施。
Boundaries for effective protection
有效保护的边界
99. The delineation of boundaries is an essential requirement in the establishment
of effective protection of nominated properties. Boundaries should be drawn to
incorporate all the attributes that convey the Outstanding Universal Value and to ensure
the integrity and/or authenticity of the property.
划定边界是建立有效保护提名财产的一项基本要求。边界应该被绘制，以包含所
有的属性，传达出色的普遍价值，并确保财产的完整性和/或真实性。
100. For properties nominated under criteria (i) - (vi), boundaries should be
drawn to include all those areas and attributes which are a direct tangible
expression of the Outstanding Universal Value of the property, as well as those
areas which, in
the light of future
research
possibilities,
offer potential to
contribute to and
enhance such
understanding.
就根据准则(i)至
(vi) 提 名
的物业而
言，界线
应包括直
接有形表
达该物业
突出普遍
价值的所
有区域和
属性，以
及根据未
来的研究
可能性，
有可能促
进和加强
这种了解
的区域。

properties

boundaries should

就根据准则(vii)至(x)提名的物业而言，界线应反映生境、物种、过程或现象
的空间要求，为其列入世界遗产名录提供依据。界线应包括紧邻具有

的直接影响和指定区域以外资源使用的影响。

Buffer zones
缓冲区
103. Wherever necessary for the proper protection of the property, an adequate buffer zone should
be provided.
只要有必要，为了适当保护财产，就应该提供足够的缓冲区。
104. For the purposes of effective protection of the nominated property, a buffer zone is an area
surrounding the nominated property which has complementary legal and/or customary restrictions placed
on its use and development in order to give an added layer of protection to the property. This should
include the immediate setting of the nominated property, important views and other areas or attributes that
are functionally important as a support to the property and its protection. The area constituting the buffer
zone should be determined in each case through appropriate mechanisms. Details on the size,
characteristics and authorized uses of a buffer zone, as well as a map indicating the precise boundaries of
the property and its buffer zone, should be provided in the nomination.
为了有效保护指定财产，缓冲区是指指定财产周围的一个区域，对其使用和
开发有相互补充的法律和/或习惯限制，以便为财产增加一层保护。这
应该包括立即设置指定的财产、重要的意见和其他作为对财产及其保
护的支持在功能上重要的领域或属性。构成缓冲区的区域应该通过适
当的机制在每种情况下确定。应在提名书内提供有关缓冲区的面积、
特征和授权用途的详细资料，以及显示该物业及其缓冲区的精确界线
的地图。
105. A clear explanation of how the buffer zone protects the property should also be provided.
还应该提供一个关于缓冲区如何保护财产的清晰解释。
106. Where no buffer zone is proposed, the nomination should include a statement as to why a
buffer zone is not required.
如果没有建议设立缓冲区，提名应包括一项说明，说明为什么不需要设立
缓冲区。
107. Although buffer zones are not part of the nominated property, any modifications to or creation of
buffer zones subsequent to inscription of a property on the World Heritage List should be approved by the
World Heritage Committee using the procedure for a minor boundary modification (see paragraph 164 and
Annex 11). The creation of buffer zones subsequent to inscription is normally considered to be a minor
boundary modification
4
.
虽然缓冲区不属于提名财产的一部分，但在世界遗产名单上的财产被列入名
单之后，对缓冲区的任何修改或创建都应由世界遗产委员会采用小规
模边界修改程序予以批准(见第 164 段和附件 11)。在登记后建立缓冲
区通常被认为是一个小的边界修改 4。
Management systems
管理系统
108. Each nominated property should have an appropriate management plan or other documented
management system which must specify how the Outstanding Universal Value of a property should be
preserved, preferably through participatory means.
每一个被提名的财产都应有一个适当的管理计划或其他文件化的管理制度，
其中必须具体说明如何最好通过参与性手段保持财产的未决普遍价
值。
109. The purpose of a management system is to ensure the effective protection of the nominated
property for present and future generations.
管理制度的目的是确保为今世后代有效保护提名的财产。
4 With regards to transnational/transboundary properties, any modification will need the agreement of all States
Parties concerned.
至于跨国/跨境财产，任何修改均须得到所有相关缔约国的同意。
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 34
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 34
110. An effective management system depends on the type, characteristics and needs
of the nominated property and its cultural and natural context. Management systems
may vary according to different cultural perspectives, the resources available and other
factors. They may incorporate traditional practices, existing urban or regional planning
instruments, and other planning control mechanisms, both formal and informal. Impact
assessments for proposed interventions are essential for all World Heritage properties.
一个有效的管理系统取决于提名财产的类型、特征和需求以及它的文化和自然背
景。管理系统可能会根据不同的文化视角、可用资源和其他因素而有所不
同。它们可能包括传统的做法，现有的城市或区域规划工具，以及其他正
式和非正式的规划控制机制。建议的干预措施的影响评估对于所有的世界
遗产财产都是必不可少的。
111. In recognizing the diversity mentioned above, common elements of an
effective management system could include:
认识到上述多样性，有效管理制度的共同要素可包括:
a) a thorough shared understanding of the property, its universal,
national and local values and its socio-ecological context by all stakeholders,
including local communities and indigenous peoples;
包括地方社区和原住民在内的所有利益攸关方对财产、其普遍、国
家和地方价值观及其社会生态背景有透彻的共同理解;
b) a respect for diversity, equity, gender equality and human rights
and the use of inclusive and participatory planning and stakeholder consultation
processes;
尊重多样性、公平、性别平等和人权，利用包容性和参与性规划和
利益攸关方协商进程;
c) a cycle of planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and
feedback;
一个规划、实施、监测、评估和反馈的周期;
d) an assessment of the vulnerabilities of the property to social,
economic, environmental and other pressures and changes, including disasters
and climate change, as well as the monitoring of the impacts of trends and
proposed interventions;
评估财产面对社会、经济、环境和其他压力和变化(包括灾害和气
候变化)的脆弱性，以及监测趋势和拟议干预措施的影响;
e) the development of mechanisms for the involvement and
coordination of the various activities between different partners and

建立不同伙伴和持份者参与和协调各项活动的机制;

所需资源的分配;
g) capacity building;
能力建设;
h) an accountable, transparent description of how the management
system functions.
对管理系统如何运作的负责、透明的描述。

117. States Parties are responsible for implementing effective management
activities for a World Heritage property. States Parties should do so in close
collaboration with property managers, the agency with management authority and
other partners, local communities and indigenous peoples, rights-holders and
stakeholders in property management, by developing, when appropriate, equitable
governance arrangements, collaborative management systems and redress
mechanisms.
缔约国有责任对世界遗产财产实施有效的管理活动。缔约国应与财产管理人
员、拥有管理当局的机构和其他伙伴、地方社区和原住民、权利持有
人和财产管理方面的利益攸关方密切合作，酌情制定公平的治理安排、
合作管理制度和补救机制。
118. The Committee recommends that States Parties include disaster, climate
change and other risk preparedness as an element in their World Heritage site
management plans and training strategies.
委员会建议缔约国将灾害、气候变化和其他风险防范作为其世界遗产场址
管理计划和培训战略的一个组成部分。

alternatives, as well as both potential positive and negative impacts on the
Outstanding Universal Value of the property and to recommend mitigation
measures against degradation or other negative impacts on the cultural or
natural heritage within the property or its wider setting. This will ensure the
long-term safeguarding of the Outstanding Universal Value, and the
strengthening of heritage resilience to disasters and climate change.

III PROCESS FOR THE INSCRIPTION OF PROPERTIES ON THE WORLD HERITAGE
LIST
财产列入世界遗产名录的程序
The Process for the inscription of properties on the World Heritage List
starts with the inclusion of a site on the Tentative List (see Section II.C),
then there are two phases in the preparation of a nomination, the
Preliminary Assessment and the full nomination dossier.
将物业列入世界遗产名录的程序首先是将一个地点列入暂定名录
(见第二.c 节) ，然后是准备提名的两个阶段，即初步评估和完整的
提名档案。
III.A Preparation of Nominations
Iii. a 准备提名
120. Before States Parties begin to prepare a nomination of a site for inscription
on the World Heritage List (i.e. before submission of a Preliminary Assessment
request and completion of that Assessment), they should become familiar with the
nomination cycle (including the requirement for a completed Preliminary
Assessment), described in Paragraph 168. It is desirable to carry out initial
preparatory work to establish that a site has the potential to justify Outstanding
Universal Value, including integrity and/or authenticity, at the earliest stage,
possibly well before the development of a full nomination (including a Preliminary
Assessment) which could be expensive and time-consuming. Such preparatory work
might include the collection of available information on the site, thematic studies,
scoping studies on the potential for demonstrating Outstanding Universal Value,
including integrity and/or authenticity, or an initial comparative study of the site in
its regional or wider global context, including an analysis in the context of the Gap
Studies produced by the Advisory Bodies. This work will help to establish the
feasibility of a possible nomination and avoid the use of resources in the preparation
of nominations that may be unlikely to succeed. States Parties are encouraged to
seek upstream advice from the relevant Advisory Body(ies) as well as to contact the
World Heritage Centre at the earliest opportunity to seek information and guidance.
Before the submission of nominations, States Parties are also encouraged to avoid,
through constructive dialogue, as much as feasible, potential issues which may
concern other States Parties.
在缔约国开始拟订列入世界遗产名录的地点提名(即在提交初步评估请求和完
成该项评估之前)之前，它们应熟悉第 168 段所述的提名周期(包括完成
初步评估的要求)。可取的做法是进行初步准备工作，尽早确定一个网
站有潜力证明其杰出的普遍价值(包括完整性和/或真实性)是合理的，
可能要在制定全面提名(包括初步评估)之前很久，这可能是昂贵和耗
费时间的。这种筹备工作可包括收集网站上的现有信息、专题研究、
关于显示杰出普遍价值(包括完整性和/或真实性)的潜力的范围研究，
或对网站进行区域或更广泛的全球范围内的初步比较研究，包括在咨
询机构编写的《性别差距研究》的范围内进行分析。这项工作将有助
于确定可能的提名的可行性，并避免在准备可能不太可能成功的提名
时使用资源。鼓励缔约国寻求有关咨询机构的上游咨询意见，并尽早
与世界遗产中心联系，以寻求信息和指导。在提交提名之前，还鼓励
缔约国通过建设
性对话尽可能避
免可能涉及其他
缔约国的潜在问
题。

The Upstream Process advice provided regarding a site will not
prejudge the results of any future Preliminary Assessment.
上游程序提供的有关网站的建议不会预先判断任何未来初步评估的
结果。
Requests for the Upstream Process shall be submitted by the annual deadline of
31 March, using the official format (Annex 15 of the Operational Guidelines).
Should the number of requests exceed the capacity, then the prioritization
system as per Paragraph 61.c) will be applied.
对上游程序的请求应在每年 3 月 31 日的截止日期之前提交，使用官方格
式(操作指南附件 15)。如果请求的数量超过了容量，那么按照第 61.c 段
的优先级系统将被应用。
Preliminary Assessment
初步评估
122. The Preliminary Assessment is a mandatory desk-based process for all sites that may be
nominated to the World Heritage List and is undertaken following a request by the relevant State(s)
Party(ies). Information included in the Preliminary Assessment request should build on the
information provided in the Tentative List and also on any Upstream Process advice and/or
Preparatory Assistance and its outcome must be provided at least one year before a full nomination
dossier can be submitted by the State(s) Party(ies).
初步评估是根据有关缔约国的请求，对可能被提名列入世界遗产名录的所
有遗址进行的强制性案头工作。初步评估请求中所载的资料应以暂
定名单中提供的资料以及任何上游进程咨询意见和/或预备性援助
为基础，其结果必须至少在缔约国提交完整提名档案之前一年提供。
In particular:
特别是:
a) The Preliminary Assessment provides States Parties with an opportunity for enhanced
dialogue with the Advisory Bodies, and it will help to establish the feasibility of a potential
nomination and avoid the use of resources in the preparation of nominations that may be unlikely to
succeed.
初步评估为缔约国提供了加强与咨询机构对话的机会，将有助于
确定潜在提名的可行性，并避免在编写可能不太可能成功的提
名时使用资源。
b) The Preliminary Assessment provides guidance on the potential of a site to justify
Outstanding Universal Value, including integrity and/or authenticity, and, if information is provided, on the
requirements for protection and management. The decision to prepare a full nomination dossier, regardless
of the outcome of the Preliminary Assessment, will rest with the concerned State(s) Party(ies).
初步评估就网站是否有潜力证明其杰出的普遍价值，包括完整性和/或
真实性提供了指导，如果提供了信息，则就保护和管理的要求提
供了指导。无论初步评估的结果如何，编制完整提名档案的决定
将由有关缔约国作出。
c) States Parties shall submit their Preliminary Assessment request to the World Heritage
Centre according to the timetable set in paragraph 168, and using the standard format provided in
Annex 3. The request shall be submitted in English or French, in paper and electronic formats (Word
and/or PDF format) and in the required number of printed copies (same as for nomination dossiers): 2
identical copies for cultural and natural sites, and 3 identical copies for mixed sites and cultural
landscapes.
缔约国应按照第 168 段规定的时间表，使用附件 3 提供的标准格式，
向世界遗产中心提交初步评估请求。申请书须以英文或法文、
纸张和电子格式(Word 和/或 PDF 格式)以及所需印刷本数目
(与提名档案相同)提交: 文化和自然遗址两份相同，混合遗址
和文化景观三份相同。
d) On receipt of Preliminary Assessment requests from States Parties, the Secretariat will
acknowledge receipt, check for completeness (in compliance with Annex 3) and register them. The Secretariat
will forward, according to the timetable set in paragraph 168, complete Preliminary Assessment requests to the
relevant Advisory Body(ies) for
在收到缔约国提出的初步评估请求后，秘书处将确认收到请求，检查请
求的完整性(符合附件 3 的规定)并予以登记。秘书处会按照第 168 段
所订明的时间表，将初步评估的要求完整地送交有关的咨询组织，
以便

concerned State(s) Party(ies) to establish a point of contact and agree on
the process of exchange. States Parties are encouraged to appoint a
technical focal point to ensure that dialogue is effective throughout the
process, and to ensure that the conclusions of the Preliminary Assessment
are communicated to the relevant stakeholders.
案头审查。如有必要，咨询机构将要求缔约国提供应提交秘书处的任
何补充资料。由初步评估开始，谘询组织将与有关缔约国展开对话，

调中心，以确保在整个过程中对话有效，并确保将初步评估的结论传
达给相关利益攸关方。
e) The Preliminary Assessment will be undertaken by ICOMOS and IUCN on a joint basis
whenever relevant, and will be an independent desk review, which will include consultation with
expert reviewers. No mission to the site will be undertaken (see Annex 6). Based on available
information, the conclusions of the assessment will include an indication of whether the site may have
potential to justify Outstanding Universal Value. If so, specific guidance and advice, in the form of
recommendations, will be provided to assist the State(s) Party(ies) in the development of the
nomination dossier. The Preliminary Assessment Report by the Advisory Bodies shall be provided to
the State(s) Party(ies) via the Secretariat in one of the two working languages of the Convention.
初步评估将在适当时由国际化学品卫生组织和自然保护联盟联合

是这样，将以建议的形式提供具体的指导和意见，以协助缔约
国编制提名档案。咨询机构的初步评估报告应通过秘书处以
《公约》两种工作语文之一提交缔约国。
f) The Preliminary Assessment Report by the Advisory Bodies is relevant for up to 5 years. A new
Preliminary Assessment is required if a nomination is not submitted by 1 February on the fifth year following the
transmission of the Report to the concerned State(s) Party(ies).
谘询组织的初步评估报告适用期最长为五年。如果在向有关缔约国转交
报告后的第五年 2 月 1 日之前未能提交提名，则需要重新进行初步
评估。
g) A State Party may withdraw a Preliminary Assessment request it has submitted, at any
time. In such circumstances, any further consideration of a possible nomination will need to be subject
to a new request for a Preliminary Assessment.
缔约国可随时撤回其提交的初步评估请求。在这种情况下，任何
可能的提名的进一步考虑将需要服从于一个新的初步评估请求。
h) At each session of the World Heritage Committee, the Secretariat will provide a list of
Preliminary Assessments requests received and those undertaken, but will not indicate the guidance given
by the Advisory Bodies to the concerned State(s) Party(ies) in a completed Preliminary Assessment.
However, once a nomination is submitted, the related Preliminary Assessment Report shall be annexed to

在世界遗产委员会的每届会议上，秘书处将提供收到的初步评估请求

的初步评估中向有关缔约国提供的指导。然而，一旦提交提名，
相关的初步评估报告须附于提名之后。
i) Both Upstream Process and Preliminary Assessment imply guidance at an early stage, prior to the
preparation of a nomination, however they are different mechanisms. The Upstream Process is not mandatory.
The Preliminary Assessment is a mandatory phase possibly allowing access to the preparation of a nomination
dossier. Within an Upstream Process a visit to the site may be possible, while the Preliminary Assessment is
carried out exclusively on the basis of a desk review. The Upstream Process may provide general advice, in
relation to revision of a Tentative List, while the Preliminary Assessment is undertaken on a single site (whether
serial or not) already included on a State Party’s

Participation in the nomination process
参与提名程序
123. Effective and inclusive participation in the nomination process of local
communities, indigenous peoples, governmental, non-governmental and private
organizations and other stakeholders is essential to enable them to have a shared
responsibility with the State Party in the maintenance of the property. States Parties
are encouraged to ensure that Preliminary Assessment requests involve appropriate
stakeholders and rights-holders engagement. They are also encouraged to prepare
nominations with the widest possible participation of stakeholders and shall
demonstrate, as appropriate, that the free, prior and informed consent of indigenous
peoples has been obtained, through, inter alia, making the nominations publicly
available in appropriate languages and public consultations and hearings. Where
appropriate, States Parties are also encouraged to consult potentially concerned
States Parties, including neighbouring States Parties, to promote consensus,
collaboration and to celebrate cultural diversity.
有效和包容性地参与地方社区、原住民、政府、非政府组织和私营组织以及
其他利益攸关方的提名进程，对于使他们能够与缔约国共同承担维护
财产的责任至关重要。鼓励缔约国确保初步评估要求涉及适当的利益
相关者和权利持有者参与。还鼓励它们在尽可能广泛的利益攸关方参
与下编写提名，并应酌情通过以适当语文公布提名以及公开协商和听
证等方式，表明已经获得了原住民的自由、事先和知情同意。还鼓励
缔约国酌情与可能有关的缔约国，包括邻国缔约国进行磋商，以促进
协商一致、合作和庆祝文化多样性。

为编写提名提供预备援助

如第七章 e 所述，缔约国可要求为编写提名提供预备援助，在评价这些请
求时，将考虑到初步评估的结果。

秘书处在整个提名过程中的协助

2. Description of the nominated property
提名物业的说明

5. Protection and management
保护和管理
Protection: Section 5 shall include the list of the legislative, regulatory,
contractual, planning, institutional and/or traditional measures most
relevant to the protection of the nominated property and provide a
detailed analysis of the way in which this protection actually operates.
Legislative, regulatory, contractual planning and/or institutional texts,
or an abstract of the texts, shall also be attached in English or French.
保护 : 第 5 节应包括与保护提名财产最相关的立法、监管、合同、
规划、体制和 / 或传统措施清单，并详细分析这种保护的实际运作
方式。立法、监管、合同规划和 / 或机构文本，或文本摘要，也应
以英文或法文附呈。
Management: An appropriate management plan or other management
system is essential and shall be provided in the nomination dossier.
Assurances of the effective implementation of the management plan or
other management system are also expected. Sustainable development
principles should be integrated into the management system, for all
types of natural, cultural and mixed nominated properties, including
their buffer zones and wider setting.
管理 : 适当的管理计划或其他管理制度是必不可少的，应在提名档
案中提供。还预期有效实施管理计划或其他管理系统的保证。应将
可持续发展原则纳入管理系统，适用于所有类型的自然、文化和混
合提名财产，包括其缓冲区和更广泛的环境。
A copy of the management plan or documentation of the management
system shall be annexed to the nomination dossier. If the management
plan exists only in a language other than English or French, an English
or French detailed description of its provisions shall be annexed.
管理计划或管理系统文件的副本应附在提名档案中。如果管理计划
仅以英文或法文以外的语言存在，则应附上其条款的英文或法文详
细说明。
A detailed analysis or explanation of the management plan or a
documented management system shall be provided in Section 5.e of the
nomination dossier.
第 5 节应提供对管理计划或文件化管理系统的详细分析或解释。E
的提名档案。
A nomination dossier which does not include the above-mentioned
documents is considered incomplete unless other documents guiding the
management of the nominated property until the finalization of the
management plan are provided.
不包括上述文件的提名档案被视为不完整，除非在管理计划定稿之
前提供了指导被提名财产管理的其他文件。
6. Monitoring
监控
States Parties shall include the key indicators in place and/or proposed
to measure and assess the state of conservation of the nominated
property, the factors affecting it, conservation measures at the
nominated property, the periodicity of their examination, and the
identity of the responsible authorities.
缔约国应列入为衡量和评估提名财产的养护状况、影响这一状况的
因素、提名财产的养护措施、审查的周期以及主管当局的身份而制
定的和/或提议的关键指标。
7. Documentation
文件
All documentation necessary to substantiate the nomination dossier
shall be provided. In addition to what is indicated above, this shall
include a) images of a quality suitable for printing (digital photographs
at 300 dpi minimum, and if essential, supplementary film, video or
other audio visual material); and b) image/audiovisual inventory and
authorization form (see Annex 5, point 7.a). The main text of the
nomination dossier shall be transmitted in printed form as well as in
electronic format (Word and/or PDF format preferred).
所有必要的文件，以证实提名档案应提供。除上述规定外，还应包
括: a)适合印刷的质量图像(数码照片，最低为 300dpi，如有必要，
还应包括补充胶片、录像或其他视听材料) ; 以及 b)图像/视听库存
和授权表格(见附件 5，第 7 点)。A).提名档案的主要文本应以印刷
格式和电子格式(最好是 Word 和/或 PDF 格式)传送。

应提供负责当局的详细联系信息。

纸张及电子格式

处收到提名档案的纸张格式之前，提名档案不得视为已提交。

III.C 各类提名物业的提名规定
Nominated transboundary properties
提名的跨界财产
134. A nominated property may be located: Decision 7 EXT.COM 4A
134. 被提名的财产可能位于: 第 7 号决定 EXT.COM 4A
a) on the territory of a single State Party, or
在一个缔约国的领土上，或
b) on the territory of all concerned States Parties having adjacent borders (nominated
transboundary property).
在所有相邻边界的有关缔约国的领土上(指定的跨界财产)。
135. Wherever possible, nomination dossiers of transboundary sites should be prepared (see Annex 2B)
and submitted by States Parties jointly in conformity with Article 11.3 of the Convention. The States Parties
concerned shall establish a joint management committee or similar body to oversee the management of the
whole nominated transboundary property.
应尽可能编写跨界场址的提名档案(见附件 2b) ，并由缔约国按照《公约》第
11 条第 3 款联合提交。有关缔约国应设立一个联合管理委员会或类似
机构来监督整个提名的跨界财产的管理。
136. Extensions to an existing World Heritage property located in one State Party may be proposed to
become a transboundary property, with the consent of the State Party on the territory of which the
existing World Heritage property is located.
经现有世界遗产所在地所在缔约国同意，可提议将位于一个缔约国的现有
世界遗产财产扩大为跨界财产。

Nominated serial properties
提名系列物业
137. Nominated serial property includes two or more component parts related by clearly defined links:
Nominated 序列属性包括两个或多个通过明确定义的链接相关的组件部分:
a) Component parts should reflect cultural, social or functional links over time that provide,
where relevant, landscape, ecological, evolutionary or habitat connectivity.
组成部分应反映文化，社会或功能的联系随着时间的推移，提供，
在相关的，景观，生态，进化或栖息地连接。
b) Each component part should contribute to the Outstanding Universal Value of the nominated
property as a whole in a substantial, scientific, readily defined and discernible way, and may include, inter
alia, intangible attributes. The resulting Outstanding Universal Value should be easily understood and
communicated.
每个组成部分都应以实质性、科学性、易于界定和可辨别的方式，对
整个提名财产的突出普遍价值作出贡献，除其他外，还可包括无
形属性。由此产生的杰出的普世价值应该容易理解和沟通。
c) Consistently, and in order to avoid an excessive fragmentation of component parts, the
process of nomination of the property, including the selection of the component parts, should take fully
into account the overall manageability and coherence of the nominated property (see Paragraph 114).
为了始终如一地避免组成部分过于分散，提名财产的过程，包括选
择组成部分，应充分考虑到被提名财产的总体可管理性和一致
性(见第 114 段)。
and provided the series as a whole – and not necessarily its individual
component parts–is of Outstanding Universal Value.
并提供系列作为一个整体-不一定是其个别组成部分-是突出的普遍
价值。
138. A serial nominated property may occur: Decision 7 EXT.COM 4A
138. 一个系列提名属性可能出现: 决定 7 EXT.COM 4A
a) on the territory of a single State Party (nominated serial national property); or
在一个缔约国的领土上(指定的系列国家财产) ; 或
b) within the territory of different States Parties, which need not be contiguous and is
nominated with the consent of all States Parties concerned (nominated serial transnational property).
在不同缔约国领土内，不需要毗连，经所有有关缔约国同意提名
(提名的系列跨国财产)。
138bis. The States Parties concerned shall establish a joint management committee
or similar body to oversee the management of the whole of a nominated
serial transnational property (see Paragraph 114). Extension to an existing
World Heritage property located in one State Party may be proposed to
become a transnational property, with the consent of the State Party on the
territory of which the existing World Heritage property is located.
138 之二。有关缔约国应设立一个联合管理委员会或类似机构，监督被提名的
系列跨国财产的全部管理(见第 114 段)。经现有世界遗产所在地所在缔
约国同意，可以提议将位于一个缔约国的现有世界遗产财产扩大为跨
国财产。

III.D Registration of nomination dossiers
III.D 提名档案的登记
140. On receipt of nomination dossiers from States Parties, the Secretariat will
acknowledge receipt, check for completeness and register them. The Secretariat will
forward complete nomination dossiers to the relevant Advisory Bodies for evaluation.
The Secretariat will also make available the electronic format of the main text of the
nomination dossiers on the World Heritage Centre’s website. If necessary, the Advisory
Bodies will request additional information from the State(s) Party(ies), which will be
submitted to and registered by the World Heritage Centre. The timetable for registration
and processing of nomination dossiers is detailed in Paragraph 168.
秘书处在收到来自缔约国的提名档案后，会确认收到，核对提名档案的完整性，
并进行登记。秘书处会将完整的提名资料送交有关的咨询组织评估。秘书
处亦会在世界文化遗产中心网站提供提名资料的电子版本。如有需要，谘
询组织会要求缔约国提供更多资料，有关资料将提交世界文化遗产中心，
并由该中心登记。提名档案的注册及处理时间表详列于第 168 段。
141. The Secretariat establishes and submits at each Committee session a list
of all nomination dossiers received, including the date of reception, an
indication of their status “complete” or “incomplete”, as well as the date at
which they are considered as "complete" in conformity with paragraphs 128,
132 and Annex 5.
秘书处按照第 128 段、第 132 段和附件 5 的规定，确定并在委员会每届会
议上提交所收到的所有提名档案的清单，包括收到日期、表明其”
完整”或”不完整”的状况以及认为”完整”的日期。
142. A nomination dossier passes through a cycle between the time of its
submission and the decision by the World Heritage Committee. This cycle normally
lasts one and a half years between submission in February of Year 1 and the
decision of the Committee in June/July of Year 2.
提名档案自提交之日起至世界遗产委员会作出决定为止，经过一个循环。这
个周期通常持续一年半，从第一年 2 月提交到第二年 6 月/7 月委员会
作出决定。
III.E Evaluation of nomination dossiers by the Advisory Bodies
Iii. e 各咨询组织对提名档案的评估
143. The Advisory Bodies will evaluate whether or not properties nominated
by States Parties have Outstanding Universal Value, meet the conditions of
integrity and (when relevant) of authenticity and meet the requirements of
protection and management. The procedures and format of ICOMOS and IUCN
evaluations are described in Annex 6.
咨询机构将评估缔约国提名的财产是否具有突出的普遍价值，是否符合完
整性和(在相关情况下)真实性的条件，是否符合保护和管理的要求。
ICOMOS 和 IUCN 评估的程序和格式见附件 6。

评审文化遗产提名档案的工作将由
ICOMOS.

by IUCN.

Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 46

a) adhere to the World Heritage Convention and the relevant
Operational Guidelines and any additional policies set out by the Committee in
its decisions;
遵守《世界遗产公约》及相关的运作指引，以及委员会在其决定中

b) be objective, rigorous and scientific including in considering all
information provided to the Advisory Bodies regarding a nomination;
客观、严谨和科学，包括考虑向谘询组织提供的有关提名的所有资
料;
c) be conducted to a consistent standard of professionalism, equity
and transparency throughout the evaluation process in consultation and dialogue
with nominating States Parties;
在与提名缔约国磋商和对话的整个评估过程中，遵循一致的专业、
公平和透明标准;
d) comply to standard format, both for evaluations and presentations, to
be agreed with the Secretariat and include the names of all experts who participated
in the evaluation process, except desk reviewers who provide confidential reviews,
and, in an annex, a detailed breakdown of all costs and expenses related to the
evaluation;
遵守与秘书处商定的评价和专题介绍的标准格式，列入参与评价进程
的所有专家的姓名，但提供保密审查的案头审查员除外，并在附
件中详细列出与评价有关的所有费用和开支细目;
e) involve regional experts familiar with the subject;
让熟悉该主题的区域专家参与;
f) indicate clearly and separately whether the property has Outstanding
Universal Value, meets the conditions of integrity and/or authenticity, a
management plan/system and legislative protection;
清楚及分别注明该物业是否具有突出的普遍价值、是否符合完整性及/
或真实性的条件、管理计划/制度及法例保障;
g) evaluate each property systematically according to all relevant
criteria, including its state of conservation, relatively, that is, by comparison
with that of other properties of the same type, both inside and outside the State
Party's territory;
根据所有相关标准，包括其保护状况，系统地评价每一财产，即与
缔约国境内外同类财产的保护状况进行比较;
h) consider previous Upstream Process advice, if provided, and the

III.F Withdrawal of nominations
152. A State Party may withdraw a nomination it has submitted at any time prior
to the Committee session at which it is scheduled to be examined. The State
Party should inform the Secretariat in writing of its intention to withdraw the
nomination. If the State Party so wishes it can resubmit a nomination for the site,
which will be considered as a new nomination according to the procedures and
timetable outlined in paragraph 168.
152bis. In the case of transnational/transboundary nominations, if one or more
nominating State(s) Party(ies) inform the Secretariat in writing of its/their
intention to withdraw all the component parts or the whole area of the site
situated on its/their territory(ies), the Secretariat shall immediately notify all the
other nominating State(s) Party(ies) and the nomination process for the site in its
entirety shall be considered concluded. If the State(s) Party(ies) so wish it/they
can resubmit a nomination for the site, which will be considered as a new
nomination according to the procedures and timetable outlined in Paragraph
168.

158. If the Committee decides that a property should not be inscribed on the World Heritage List, the

different criteria not presented in the original nomination. In these cases, a new nomination shall be
submitted.

Referral of Nominations
转介提名
159. Nominations which the Committee decides to refer back to the State Party for
additional information may be resubmitted to the following Committee session for
examination. Referral means that the requested additional information is necessary to
determine the Outstanding Universal Value of the nominated property, which only
occurs at the time a property is inscribed on the World Heritage List (see Paragraph
154). The referral procedure does not involve a mission to the site by the Advisory
Body(ies) and it shall not involve change to criteria nor substantial change of
area(s)/component(s) from those proposed in the original nomination dossier. In the
referral procedure there is no submission of a new nomination dossier and the additional
information that reactivates the referred nomination must be received by the Secretariat
by 1 February
7
of the year in which examination by the Committee is desired. The
Secretariat will immediately transmit it to the relevant Advisory Bodies for evaluation.
A referred nomination which is not presented to the Committee within three years of the
original Committee decision will be considered as a new nomination when it is
resubmitted for examination, following the procedures and timetable outlined in
paragraph 168. States Parties might seek advice from the relevant Advisory Body(ies)
and/or the World Heritage Centre to discuss how the recommendations of the
Committee might be addressed.
委员会决定退回缔约国以获得更多信息的提名可重新提交委员会下届会议审查。
转交意味着需要提供所要求的补充资料，以确定被提名财产的未决普遍价
值，这只有在财产被列入世界遗产名录时才会发生(见第 154 段)。转介程
序并不涉及谘询组织派团前往有关地点，亦不涉及改变准则或对原有提名
档案所建议的范围/组成部分作出重大改变。在转介程序中，不提交新的
提名档案，秘书处必须在需要委员会审查的年份的 2 月 7 日之前收到重新
启动所提名的补充资料。秘书处会立即转交有关的咨询组织作出评估。在
委员会最初决定后三年内未向委员会提交的提名，在按照第 168 段所述程
序和时间表重新提交审查时，将被视为新提名。缔约国不妨征求有关咨询
机构和/或世界遗产中心的意见，以讨论如何处理委员会的建议。
Deferral of Nominations
推迟提名
160. The Committee may decide to defer a nomination for more in-depth
assessment or study, or a substantial revision by the State Party. Should the State
Party decide to resubmit the deferred nomination in any subsequent year, it must be
received by the Secretariat by 1 February
8
. This resubmission shall not be subject
to Preliminary Assessment, unless the Committee decides otherwise. These
nominations will then be reevaluated (evaluated again) by the relevant Advisory
Bodies during the course of the full year and a half evaluation cycle including an
evaluation mission according to the procedures and timetable outlined in paragraph
168. States Parties are encouraged to seek advice from the relevant Advisory Body
and/or the World Heritage Centre to discuss how the recommendations of the
Committee might be addressed. Where required, the States Parties may wish to
consider inviting an Advisory mission.
委员会可决定推迟提名，以便进行更深入的评估或研究，或由缔约国进行实
质性修订。如果缔约国决定在下一年重新提交推迟的提名，秘书处必
须在 2 月 8 日之前收到提名。除非委员会另有决定，否则不得对重新
提交的申请进行初步评估。然后，这些提名将由有关咨询机构在一年
半的评价周期内重新评价(再次评价) ，包括根据第 168 段所述程序和
时间表派出评价团。鼓励缔约国征求有关咨询机构和/或世界遗产中心
的意见，讨论如何处理委员会的建议。如有需要，缔约国可考虑邀请
咨询团。

164. If a State Party wishes to request a minor modification to the boundaries
of a property already on the World Heritage List, it must be prepared in
如果缔约国希望要求对已列入世界遗产名录的财产的边界进行少量修改，

委员会必须在 2 月 1 日之前通过秘书处收到附件 11 的格式，秘书

程序。
Significant modifications to the boundaries
对边界的重大修改
165. If a State Party wishes to significantly modify the boundaries of a
property already on the World Heritage List, the State Party shall submit this
proposal as if it was a new nomination, including the requirement to be
previously included on the Tentative List (see Paragraphs 63 and 65), and
having undergone a Preliminary Assessment (see Paragraph 122). The
requirement to undergo a Preliminary Assessment shall be disregarded when the
Committee explicitly encourages in a decision a significant boundary
modification not involving modifications to the criteria. This nomination dossier
shall be presented by 1 February

III.K Financing of evaluation of nominations
三. k 提名评价的资金筹措
168bis. States Parties submitting new nomination dossiers are expected to make
voluntary contributions towards funding evaluation of nominations by
the Advisory Bodies, taking into account the average costs of
evaluations as indicated by the Secretariat in the document related to the
World Heritage Fund presented at each Committee session. The same
principle applies to the submission of Preliminary Assessment requests.
The modalities are as follows:
168 之二。提交新提名档案的缔约国应考虑到秘书处在向委员会每届会议
提交的与世界遗产基金有关的文件中指出的评价平均费用，为咨询
机构对提名的评价提供自愿捐款。同样的原则适用于提交初步评估
请求。有关模式如下:
a) The contributions shall be made to a dedicated sub-account of the
World Heritage Fund;
捐款应提供给世界遗产基金的一个专门分帐户;
b) No contributions would be expected from Least Developed
Countries or Low-Income Economies (as defined by the United Nations
Economic and Social Council's Committee for Development Policy), Lower
Middle-Income Countries as defined by the World Bank, Small Island
Developing States and States Parties in conflict or post-conflict situations;
预计最不发达国家或低收入经济体(按照联合国经济及社会理事会
发展政策委员会的定义)、世界银行定义的中低收入国家、小
岛屿发展中国家和处于冲突或冲突后局势的缔约国不会提供
捐款;
c) The contributions are expected to be made after the Preliminary
Assessment or the nomination dossier enters the evaluation cycle upon a positive
outcome of the completeness check;
预计将在初步评估或提名档案在完整性检查取得积极成果后进入评
估周期之后提供捐助;
d) This mechanism shall not impact the objective evaluation of sites
by the Advisory Bodies, nor the order of priority as defined in the Operational
Guidelines to be used when handling nominations.
这一机制不应影响咨询机构对场址的客观评价，也不应影响在处理
提名时将采用的业务准则所界定的优先次序。

Decision 43 COM 14
第 43com 11A 号决定

四、
a
Reactive Monitoring
反应性监测
Definition of Reactive Monitoring
无功监测的定义
169.
Reactive Monitoring is the reporting by the Secretariat, other sectors of
反应性监测是秘书处的报告，其他部门 Decision 39 COM 11
第 39 号决定 COM 11
UNESCO and the Advisory Bodies to the Committee on the state of
conservation of specific World Heritage properties that are under threat.
To this end, the States Parties shall submit specific reports and impact
studies each time exceptional circumstances occur or work is
undertaken which may have an impact on the Outstanding Universal
Value of the property or its state of conservation.
联合国教科文组织和世界遗产保护委员会的咨询机构。为此目的，
缔约国应在每次发生特殊情况或进行可能对财产的未决普遍价值或
其养护状况产生影响的工作时提交具体报告和影响研究。
Reactive Monitoring is also foreseen in reference to properties
inscribed, or to be inscribed, on the List of World Heritage in Danger as
set out in paragraphs 177-191. Reactive Monitoring is also foreseen in
the procedures for the eventual deletion of properties from the World
Heritage List as set out in paragraphs 192-198.
对于第 177 至 191 段所述列入或将列入《濒危世界遗产名录》的财
产，也可预见进行反应式监测。正如第 192 至 198 段所述，在最终
从世界遗产名录中删除物业的程序中，亦预计会进行「无线电监
察」。
These reports shall be submitted to the World Heritage Committee through the
Secretariat, using the standard format in Annex 13, in English or French:
这些报告须以附件 13 的标准格式，以英文或法文，透过秘书处提交世界
遗产委员会:
a) by 1 December of the year preceding the examination of the property by the Committee,
for the properties inscribed on the World Heritage List,
在委员会审查列入世界遗产名录的财产的前一年 12 月 1 日之前,
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 56
实施《世界遗产公约》的运作指引 56
b) by 1 February of the year of examination of the property by the
Committee, for the properties inscribed on the List of World Heritage in
Danger, and for specific cases of utmost urgency.
在委员会审查财产的当年 2 月 1 日之前，审查列入《濒危世界遗产
名录》的财产，并审查极为紧急的具体案件。
Objective of Reactive Monitoring
反应性监测的目标
170. When adopting the process of Reactive Monitoring, the Committee was
particularly concerned that all possible measures should be taken to prevent the
deletion of any property from the List and was ready to offer technical cooperation
as far as possible to States Parties in this connection.
在采用被动监测程序时，委员会特别关切的是，应采取一切可能的措施，防
止从清单上删除任何财产，并准备在这方面尽可能向缔约国提供技术
合作。
171. The Committee recommends that States Parties cooperate with the
Advisory Bodies which have been asked by the Committee to carry out monitoring
and reporting on its behalf on the progress of work undertaken for the preservation
of properties inscribed on the World Heritage List.
委员会建议缔约国与委员会要求的咨询机构合作，代表委员会监测和报告为
保护列入世界遗产名录的财产而开展的工作的进展情况。
Information received from States Parties and/or other sources
从缔约国和 ( 或 ) 其他来源收到的资料

to inform the Committee, through the Secretariat, of their intention to undertake or
to authorize in an area protected under the Convention major restorations or new
constructions which may affect the Outstanding Universal Value of the property.
Notice should be given as soon as possible (for instance, before drafting basic
documents for specific projects) and before making any decisions that would be
difficult to reverse, so that the Committee may assist in seeking appropriate
solutions to ensure that the Outstanding Universal Value of the property is fully
preserved.

的重大修复或新建筑。应尽快发出通知(例如，在起草具体项目的基本
文件之前) ，并在作出任何难以逆转的决定之前发出通知，以便委员
会可协助寻求适当的解决办法，确保该财产的未决普遍价值得到充分
保留。

IV.B The List of World Heritage in Danger
四、 b 濒危世界遗产名录
Guidelines for the inscription of properties on the List of World
Heritage in Danger
列入濒危世界遗产名录的财产登记准则
177. In accordance with Article 11, paragraph 4, of the Convention, the Committee may inscribe a
property on the List of World Heritage in Danger when the following requirements are met:
根据《公约》第 11 条第 4 款，委员会可在符合下列要求的情况下将财产
列入濒危世界遗产名单:
a) the property under consideration is on the World Heritage List;
有关物业已列入世界遗产名录;
b) the property is threatened by serious and specific danger;
财产受到严重具体危险的威胁;
c) major operations are necessary for the conservation of the property;
为保护该财产而需要采取的主要行动;
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 58
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 58
d) assistance under the Convention has been requested for the property; the Committee is of
the view that its assistance in certain cases may most effectively be limited to messages of its concern,
including the message sent by inscription of a property on the List of World Heritage in Danger and
that such assistance may be requested by any Committee member or the Secretariat.
委员会认为，委员会在某些情况下提供的援助可能最有效地限于委
员会关切的信息，包括将某一财产列入《濒危世界遗产名录》
所发出的信息，委员会任何成员或秘书处均可请求提供这种援
助。
Criteria for the inscription of properties on the List of World Heritage in
Danger
列入《濒危世界遗产名录》的标准
178. A World Heritage property - as defined in Articles 1 and 2 of the Convention - can be inscribed on
the List of World Heritage in Danger by the Committee when it finds that the condition of the property
corresponds to at least one of the criteria in either of the two cases described below.
如果委员会认为，在下述两种情况中的任何一种情况下，财产的状况至少符
合其中一种标准，委员会可将《公约》第 1 条和第 2 条所界定的世界
遗产财产列入《濒危世界遗产名单》。
179. In the case of cultural properties:
就文化财产而言:
a) ASCERTAINED DANGER - The property is faced with specific and proven imminent
danger, such as:
确定的危险——这些财产面临着特定的和已证实的迫在眉睫的危险 ，
例如 :

材料严重变质;

结构及/或装饰物严重恶化;

建筑或城市规划一致性严重恶化;

城乡空间或自然环境的严重恶化;
v) significant loss of historical authenticity;
历史真实性的重大损失;
vi) important loss of cultural significance.
文化意义的重大损失。
b) POTENTIAL DANGER - The property is faced with threats which could have
deleterious effects on its inherent characteristics. Such threats are, for example:
潜在的危险 - 财产面临的威胁，可能有害影响其固有的特点。这样

缺乏保育政策;

区域规划项目的威胁效应;

城市规划的威胁效应;
v) outbreak or threat of armed conflict;
武装冲突的爆发或威胁;
vi) threatening impacts of climatic, geological or other environmental factors.
气候、地质或其他环境因素的威胁性影响。

182. The Committee may wish to bear in mind the following supplementary factors when

the decision shall immediately be issued by the Committee, in accordance with Article 11.4 of the
Convention.
应将委员会的决定通知有关缔约国，委员会应根据《公约》第 11 条第 4
款立即发布关于该决定的公告。
188. The Secretariat publishes the updated List of World Heritage in Danger in printed form and is also
available at: https://whc.unesco.org/en/danger
秘书处以印刷形式出版了最新的《濒危世界遗产名录》 ，也可在
https://whc.unesco. org/en/Danger 网站查阅
189. The Committee shall allocate a specific, significant portion of the World Heritage Fund to
financing of possible assistance to World Heritage properties inscribed on the List of World Heritage
in Danger.
委员会应拨出世界遗产基金的一大部分专款，资助可能援助列入《濒危世
界遗产名录》的世界遗产财产。
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 61
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 61
Regular review of the state of conservation of properties on the List of
World Heritage in Danger
定期审查列入濒危世界遗产名录的财产的保护状况
190. The Committee shall review annually the state of conservation of properties on the List of
World Heritage in Danger. This review shall include such monitoring procedures and expert missions
as might be determined necessary by the Committee.
委员会应每年审查《濒危世界遗产名录》所列财产的保护状况。这种审查
应包括委员会可能确定的监测程序和专家任务。
191. On the basis of these regular reviews, the Committee shall decide, in consultation with the
State Party concerned, whether:
在这些定期审查的基础上，委员会应与有关缔约国协商决定:
a) additional measures are required to conserve the property;
须采取额外措施以保育该物业;
b) to delete the property from the List of World Heritage in Danger if the property is no
longer under threat;
如该物业不再受到威胁，应将该物业从世界遗产名录中删除;
c) to consider the deletion of the property from both the List of World Heritage in Danger
and the World Heritage List if the property has deteriorated to the extent that it has lost those
characteristics which determined its inscription on the World Heritage List, in accordance with the
procedure set out in paragraphs 192-198.
根据第 192 至 198 段规定的程序，如果财产已经恶化到失去了决定
将其列入世界遗产名录的那些特征，则应考虑从《濒危世界遗
产名录》和《世界遗产名录》中删除该财产。

necessary corrective measures have not been taken within the time proposed, the State Party on whose

如果列入世界遗产名录的财产严重恶化，或者未在建议的时间内采取必要

concerned, it will, as far as possible, verify the source and the contents of the information in

information received.
秘书处会要求有关的咨询组织就收到的资料提出意见。
196. The Committee will examine all the information available and will take a decision. Any such
decision shall, in accordance with Article 13 (8) of the Convention, be taken by a majority of two-
thirds of its members present and voting. The Committee shall not decide to delete any property unless
the State Party has been consulted on the question.
委员会将审查所有可用的资料，并将作出决定。根据《公约》第 13 条第 8
款，任何此种决定应以出席并参加表决的成员的三分之二多数作出。
委员会不得决定删除任何财产，除非就此问题征求了缔约国的意见。

197. The State Party shall be informed of the Committee's decision and public notice of this decision shall be

will be reflected in the next updated List that is published.
如果委员会的决定涉及对世界遗产名录的任何修改，这一修改将反映在公

taken for the application of the Convention, including the state of conservation of
the World Heritage properties located on their territories.
请缔约国通过世界遗产委员会向教科文组织大会提交报告，说明它们为适用

200. Periodic Reporting is a self-reporting process and should be led as far as
possible by the States Parties in each region. The Secretariat coordinates and
facilitates the Periodic Reporting Process at the global level. States Parties may
request expert advice from the Advisory Bodies and the Secretariat, which may
also (with agreement of the States Parties concerned) commission further expert
advice.
定期报告是一个自我报告过程，应尽可能由每个区域的缔约国领导。秘书
处在全球范围内协调和促进定期报告过程。缔约国可请咨询机构和
秘书处提供专家意见，秘书处也可(经有关缔约国同意)委托提供进
一步的专家意见。
201. Periodic Reporting serves four main purposes:
定期汇报有四个主要目的:
a) to provide an assessment of the application of the World Heritage
Convention by the State Party;
对缔约国适用《世界遗产公约》的情况进行评估;
b) to provide an assessment as to whether the Outstanding Universal
Value of the properties inscribed on the World Heritage List is being maintained
over time;
评估列入世界遗产名录的物业在一段时间内是否仍然具有突出的普
遍价值;
c) to provide up-dated information about the World Heritage
properties to record the changing circumstances and state of conservation of the
properties;
提供有关世界遗产物业的最新资料，以记录有关物业在不断变化的
情况和保育状况;
d) to provide
a mechanism for

and experiences between
States Parties concerning
the implementation of

定期报告对于更有效地长期保护所登记的财产以及加强执行《公约》的可

204. The sixth year of each cycle is a period for reflection and evaluation.

as appropriate before a new cycle is initiated. The World Heritage Committee
may also decide to use the reflection to initiate the development and publication

VI ENCOURAGING SUPPORT FOR THE WORLD HERITAGE CONVENTION
六、鼓励支持世界遗产公约
VI.A Objectives
六、目标
211. The objectives are:
目标是:
a) to enhance capacity building and research;
加强能力建设和研究;
b) to raise the general public’s awareness, understanding and
appreciation of the need to preserve cultural and natural heritage;
提高公众对保护文化和自然遗产的认识、了解和欣赏;

community; and
加强世界遗产在社区生活中的作用; 以及
d) to increase equitable, inclusive and effective participation of local
and national populations, including indigenous peoples, in the protection and
presentation of heritage.
使包括原住民在内的地方和全国人民更加公平、包容和有效地参与
遗产的保护和呈现。
VI.B Capacity building and research
能力建设和研究
212. The Committee seeks to develop capacity building within the States
Parties in conformity with its Strategic Objectives and the World Heritage
Capacity Building Strategy adopted by the Committee.
委员会根据其战略目标和委员会通过的《世界遗产能力建设战略》 ，致力
于发展缔约国内部的能力建设。
The World Heritage Capacity Building Strategy
世界遗产能力
建设战略
213. Recognizing the
high level of skills and
multidisciplinary approach
necessary for the
protection, conservation,
and presentation of the
World Heritage, the
Committee has adopted
the World Heritage
Capacity Building
Strategy. The definition of
capacity building identifies
three broad areas where
capacities reside and for
which audiences for
capacity building need
targeting: practitioners,
institutions, and
communities and
networks. The World
Heritage Capacity
Building Strategy provides
a framework of action, and
orients actors at the
international, regional, or
national levels to create
regional and national
capacity building
strategies in addition to
individual capacity
building activities. The
actions can be taken up by
the many actors who
currently provide or could
provide capacity building activities for the benefit of World Heritage. The primary goal
of the Capacity Building Strategy is to ensure that necessary skills are developed by a
wide range of actors for better implementation of the Convention. In order to avoid
overlap
委员会认识到保护、保护和介绍世界遗产所需的高水平技能和多学科综合学科研
究法，因此通过了世界遗产能力建设战略。能力建设的定义确定了能力
存在的三个广泛领域，能力建设的受众需要针对这些领域: 从业人员、机
构以及社区和网络。《世界遗产能力建设战略》提供了一个行动框架，
指导国际、区域或国家各级的行为者除了个人能力建设活动之外，还制
定区域和国家能力建设战略。这些行动可以由目前提供或者可以提供能
力建设活动的许多参与者采取，以利于世界遗产。能力建设战略的主要
目标是确保广泛的参与者发展必要的技能，以便更好地执行公约。为了
避免重叠

Heritage Convention

National capacity building strategies and regional co-operation
国家能力建设战略和区域合作
214. States Parties are encouraged to ensure that there is a gender-balanced
representation of their professionals and specialists at all levels and that they are
adequately trained. To this end, States Parties are encouraged to develop national
capacity building strategies and include regional cooperation for training as part of
their strategies. Development of such regional and national strategies can be assisted
by the Advisory Bodies and the various UNESCO Category 2 Centres related to
World Heritage, taking into consideration the World Heritage Capacity Building
Strategy.
鼓励缔约国确保各级专业人员和专家的性别比例均衡，并确保他们得到充分
的培训。为此，鼓励缔约国制定国家能力建设战略，并将培训方面的
区域合作纳入其战略。咨询机构和教科文组织与世界遗产有关的第二
类中心可以协助制定这种区域和国家战略，同时考虑到世界遗产能力
建设战略。
214bis. States Parties are encouraged to develop educational and capacity building
programmes that harness the reciprocal benefits of the Convention for
heritage and society. The programmes may be based on innovation and local
entrepreneurship, and aimed in particular at medium/small/micro scale
levels, to promote sustainable and inclusive economic benefits for local
communities and indigenous peoples and to identify and promote
opportunities for public and private investment in sustainable development
projects, including those that promote use of local materials and resources
and foster local cultural and creative industries and safeguarding intangible
heritage associated with World Heritage properties.
214 之二。鼓励缔约国制定教育和能力建设方案，利用《公约》对遗产和社会
的互惠惠。这些方案可以基于创新和地方企业家精神，特别是针对中
小型/微型规模，以促进为地方社区和原住民带来可持续和包容性的经
济利益，并确定和促进对可持续发展项目的公共和私人投资机会，包
括那些促进利用地方材料和资源、促进地方文化和创意产业以及保护
与世界遗产财产有关的非物质遗产的项目。
Research
研究
215. The Committee develops and coordinates international cooperation in the
area of research needed for the effective implementation of the Convention. States
Parties are also encouraged to make resources available to undertake research, since
knowledge and understanding are fundamental to the identification, management,
and monitoring of World Heritage properties. States Parties are encouraged to
support scientific studies and research methodologies, including traditional and
indigenous knowledge held by local communities and indigenous peoples, with all
necessary consent. Such studies and research are aimed at demonstrating the
contribution that the conservation and management of World Heritage properties,
their buffer zones
and wider setting
make to sustainable

VI.C Awareness-raising and education
六. c 提高认识和教育
Awareness-raising
提高认识
217. States Parties are encouraged to raise awareness of the need to preserve
World Heritage in their own countries. In particular, they should ensure that
World Heritage status is adequately marked and promoted on-site.
鼓励缔约国提高对在本国保护世界遗产的必要性的认识。特别是，他们应
该确保世界遗产地位得到充分的标识并在现场得到宣传。
218. The Secretariat provides assistance to States Parties in developing activities
aimed at raising public awareness of the Convention and informing the public of the
dangers threatening World Heritage. The Secretariat advises States Parties regarding
the preparation and implementation of on-site promotional and educational projects to
be funded through International Assistance. The Advisory Bodies and appropriate
State agencies may also be solicited to provide advice on such projects.
秘书处协助缔约国开展活动，旨在提高公众对《公约》的认识，并告知公众
威胁世界遗产的危险。秘书处就筹备和实施由国际援助资助的现场宣
传和教育项目，向缔约国提供意见。咨询机构和适当的国家机构也可
能被要求就这些项目提供建议。
Education
教育
219. The World Heritage Committee encourages and supports the
development of educational materials, activities and programmes.
世界遗产委员会鼓励和支持教育材料、活动和方案的发展。
International Assistance
国际援助
220. States Parties are encouraged to develop quality educational activities related to
World Heritage through a variety of learning environments tailored to each audience with,
wherever possible, the participation of schools, universities, museums and other local and
national educational authorities.
鼓励缔约国通过为每个受众量身定制的各种学习环境，开展与世界遗产有关的高
质量教育活动，并尽可能让学校、大学、博物馆和其他地方和国家教育当
局参与。
221. The Secretariat, in cooperation with the UNESCO Education Sector and
other partners, produces and publishes a World Heritage Educational Resource
Kit, “World Heritage in Young Hands”, for use in secondary schools around the
world. The Kit is adaptable for use at other educational levels.
秘书处与教科文组织教育部门和其他伙伴合作，制作并出版了一套世界遗
产教育资料，题为”青年手中的世界遗产”，供世界各地的中学使
用。这套教材适用于其他教育水平。
222. International Assistance may be requested by States Parties from the World
Heritage Fund for the purpose of developing and implementing awareness-raising and
educational activities or programmes (see Chapter VII).
缔约国可请求世界遗产基金提供国际援助，以便制定和执行提高认识和教育
活动或方案(见第七章)。

THE WORLD HERITAGE FUND AND INTERNATIONAL ASSISTANCE
世界遗产基金和国际援助
VII.A
七. a
The World Heritage Fund
世界遗产基金会
223. The World Heritage Fund is a trust fund, established by the Convention
in conformity with the provisions of the Financial Regulations of UNESCO. The
resources of the Fund consist of compulsory and voluntary contributions made by
States Parties to the Convention, and any other resources authorized by the
Fund’s regulations.
世界遗产基金是一个信托基金，根据联合国教科文组织财务条例的规定，
由公约设立。该基金的资源包括由《公约》缔约国提供的强制性和
自愿性捐款，以及基金条例授权的任何其他资源。
224. The financial regulations for the Fund are set out in document WHC/7
available at https://whc.unesco.org/en/financialregulations
基金的财务条例载于 WHC/7 号文件，可在 https://WHC.unesco.
org/en/financialregulations 查阅

Heritage Convention

执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 67
VII.B Mobilization of other technical and financial resources and
partnerships in support of the World Heritage Convention
调动其他技术和财政资源以及伙伴关系支持世界遗产公约
225. To the extent possible, the World Heritage Fund should be used to mobilize
additional funds for International Assistance from other sources.
应尽可能利用世界遗产基金从其他来源筹集更多的国际援助资金。
226. The Committee decided that contributions offered to the World Heritage
Fund for international assistance campaigns and other UNESCO projects for
any property inscribed on the World Heritage List shall be accepted and used as
International Assistance pursuant to Section V of the Convention, and in
conformity with the modalities established for carrying out the campaign or
project.
委员会决定，向世界遗产基金提供的用于国际援助运动和教科文组织其他
项目的捐款，应根据《公约》第五节的规定，并按照为开展这一运
动或项目而确定的方式，接受并用作国际援助。
227. States Parties are invited to provide support to the Convention in addition to
obligatory contributions paid to the World Heritage Fund. This voluntary support
can be provided through additional contributions to the World Heritage Fund or
direct financial and technical contributions to properties.
请缔约国除向世界遗产基金支付强制性捐款外，向《公约》提供支助。这种
自愿支持可以通过对世界遗产基金的额外捐款或对财产的直接财政和
技术捐款来提供。
228. States Parties are encouraged to participate in international fundraising
campaigns launched by UNESCO and aimed at protecting World Heritage.
鼓励缔约国参与联合国教科文组织发起的旨在保护世界遗产的国际筹款活动。
229. States Parties and others who anticipate making contributions towards these
campaigns or other UNESCO projects for World Heritage properties are
encouraged to make their contributions through the World Heritage Fund.
鼓励缔约国和其他打算为这些运动或教科文组织关于世界遗产财产的其他项
目捐款的国家通过世界遗产基金捐款。
230. States Parties are encouraged to promote the establishment of national,
public and private foundations or associations aimed at raising funds to support
World Heritage conservation efforts.
鼓励缔约国建立国家、公共和私人基金会或协会，以筹集资金支持世界遗
产保护工作。
231. The Secretariat provides support in mobilizing financial and technical
resources for World Heritage conservation and actively engages in resource
mobilization, including through developing partnerships with public and private
institutions in conformity with the decisions and the strategies adopted by the
World Heritage Committee and UNESCO regulations.
秘书处支持为保护世界遗产调动财政和技术资源，并积极参与资源调动，包
括根据世界遗产委员会通过的决定和战略以及教科文组织的条例，与
公共和私营机构建立伙伴关系。
232. The Secretariat should refer to UNESCO’s “Comprehensive Partnership
Strategy” to govern external fundraising in favour of the World Heritage
秘书处应该参考联合国教科文组织的“全面伙伴关系战略”来管理有利于

VII.C International Assistance
Vii. c 国际援助
233. The Convention provides International Assistance to States Parties for
the protection of the world cultural and natural heritage located on their
territories and inscribed, or potentially suitable for inscription on the World
Heritage List. International Assistance should be seen as supplementary to
national efforts for the conservation and management of World Heritage and
Tentative List properties when adequate resources cannot be secured at the
national level.
《公约》向缔约国提供国际援助，以保护位于其领土上并已登记或可能适
合列入世界遗产名录的世界文化和自然遗产。在国家一级无法获得
充足资源的情况下，国际援助应被视为对各国保护和管理世界遗产
和暂定名单财产的努力的补充。
234. International Assistance is primarily financed from the World Heritage
Fund, established under the World Heritage Convention. The Committee
determines the budget for International Assistance on a biennial basis.
国际援助主要由世界遗产基金提供资金，该基金是根据世界遗产公约设立
的。委员会每两年确定一次国际援助的预算。
See Articles 13 (1)(2) and
Articles 19-26 of the World
Heritage Convention
见《世界遗产公约》第
13(1)(2)条和第 19-26 条
Section IV of the World
Heritage Convention
《世界遗产公约》第
四节
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 68
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 68
235. The World Heritage Committee coordinates and allocates types of
International Assistance in response to State Party requests. These types of
International Assistance, described in the summary table set out below, in order
of priority are:
世界遗产委员会根据缔约国的请求协调和分配国际援助类型。这些类型的
国际援助，如下表所述，按优先次序排列如下:
a) Emergency assistance;
紧急援助;
b) Conservation and Management assistance (incorporating assistance
for training and research, technical cooperation and promotion and education);
保护和管理援助(包括培训和研究、技术合作、推广和教育方面的
援助) ;
c) Preparatory assistance.
预备性援助。
VII.D Principles and priorities for International Assistance
八. 四、国际援助的原则和优先事项
236. Priority is given to International Assistance for properties inscribed on
the List of World Heritage in Danger. The Committee created a specific budget
line to ensure that a significant portion of assistance from the World Heritage
Fund is allocated to properties inscribed on the List of World Heritage in
Danger.
对列入濒危世界遗产清单的财产给予国际援助是优先事项。委员会设立了
一个具体的预算项目，以确保世界遗产基金提供的大部分援助用于
列入《濒危世界遗产名录》的财产。
237. States Parties in arrears of payment of their compulsory or voluntary
contributions to the World Heritage Fund are not eligible for International
Assistance, it being understood that this provision does not apply to requests for
emergency assistance.
拖欠对世界遗产基金的强制性或自愿性捐款的缔约国没有资格获得国际援
助，但有一项了解，即这项规定不适用于紧急援助请求。
238. To support its Strategic Objectives, the Committee also allocates
International Assistance in conformity with the priorities set out in its decisions
and in the Regional Programmes it adopts as a follow-up to Periodic Reports
(see para. 210).
为了支持其战略目标，委员会还根据其决定和作为定期报告后续行动通过
的区域方案所列优先事项分配国际援助(见第 210 段)。
239. In addition to the priorities outlined in paragraphs 236-238 above, the
following considerations govern the decisions of the Committee in granting
International Assistance:
除了上文第 236 至 238 段所述的优先次序外，委员会在作出提供国际援助
的决定时，须考虑以下因素:
a) the likelihood that the assistance will have a catalytic and
multiplier effect (“seed money”) and promote financial and technical
contributions from other sources;
援助有可能产生催化和乘数效应(”种子资金”) ，并促进其他来源
的财政和技术捐助;
b) when funds available are limited and a selection has to be made,
preference is given to:
当可用资金
有限

240. A balance will be maintained in the allocation of resources between cultural
and natural heritage and between Conservation and Management and Preparatory
Assistance. This balance is reviewed and decided upon on a regular basis by the
Committee and during the second year of each biennium by the Chairperson or the
World Heritage Committee.
在文化遗产和自然遗产之间，以及在保护和管理和预备援助之间，资源的分
配将保持平衡。这一余额由委员会定期审查并决定，并在每个两年期
的第二年由主席或世界遗产委员会作出决定。
