VII.F Procedure and format
Vii. f 程序和格式
242. All States Parties submitting requests for international assistance are encouraged to consult the Secretariat
and the Advisory Bodies during the conceptualization, planning and elaboration of each request. To facilitate
鼓励所有提出国际援助请求的缔约国在每项请求的构想、规划和拟订过程中
与秘书处和咨询机构协商。促进
States Parties’ work, examples of successful international assistance
requests may be provided upon request.
缔约国的工作，成功的国际援助请求的例子可以根据请求提供。
243. The application form for International Assistance is presented in Annex 8 and the types, amounts, deadlines for
submission and the authorities responsible for approval are outlined in the summary table in Chapter VII.E.
国际援助申请表载于附件 8，提交的类型、数额、截止日期和负责核准的当局概
述于第七章 e 节的简表。
244. The request should be submitted in English or French, duly signed and transmitted by the National
Commission for UNESCO, the State Party Permanent Delegation to UNESCO and/or appropriate
governmental Department or Ministry to the following address:

VII.G Assessment of International Assistance requests
247. Provided they are complete, all requests are assessed by the Secretariat
irrespective of the amount requested. In addition, requests with a budget above
US$ 30,000 are assessed as follows:
a) By ICOMOS for requests for cultural heritage (all types of assistance)
and ICCROM (all types of assistance except Preparatory assistance);
b) By IUCN for requests for natural heritage;
c) By ICOMOS and IUCN for requests for mixed heritage (all types of
assistance) and ICCROM (all types of assistance except Preparatory
assistance).
The Secretariat processes requests for Emergency assistance within up to
10 working days.
Whenever necessary, the Secretariat may consult the Advisory Bodies,
for the assessment of requests with a budget under US$ 30,000.
ICOMOS, IUCN and ICCROM will be consulted on all requests which
specifically demand the involvement of one or more Advisory Bodies in
the respective project.

World Heritage Committee or, in observer capacity, a person designated by the
Chairperson, meets once or twice a year to examine the International Assistance
requests of more than US$ 5,000, except those for Emergency Assistance, and to
make recommendations to the Chairperson and/or the Committee.

253. The Chairperson is not authorized to approve requests submitted by
his/her own country. These will be examined by the Committee.
主席无权批准本国提出的请求，这些请求将由委员会审查。
254. All requests for Preparatory Assistance or Conservation and Management
Assistance of more than US$ 5,000 should be received by the Secretariat on or
before 31 October. Incomplete forms which do not come back duly completed by
30 November will be sent back to the States Parties for submission to a next cycle.
Complete requests are examined by a first panel held in January. Requests for
which the panel issues a positive or a negative recommendation will be submitted to
the Chairperson/Committee for decision. A second panel may be held at least eight
weeks before the Committee session for requests which were revised since the first
panel. Requests sent back for a substantial revision will be examined by the panel
depending on their date of receipt. Requests requiring only minor revision and no
further examination by the panel must come back within the year when they were
examined first; otherwise they will be sent again to a next panel. The chart detailing
the submission process is attached in Annex 8.
所有超过 5000 美元的预备援助或保护和管理援助请求应在 10 月 31 日或之前
由秘书处收到。未能在 11 月 30 日前正式填妥的不完整表格将被送回
缔约国，以便提交下一个周期。完整的申请将由一月份举行的第一个
小组审查。小组提出正面或负面建议的要求，将提交主席/委员会作出
决定。第二个小组可能在委员会会议之前至少八周举行，以处理自第
一个小组以来修订的请求。发回的要求进行实质性修订的请求将由专
家小组根据他们的收到日期进行审查。只需稍作修改且小组不再进一
步审查的请求必须在首次审查的年份内返回; 否则将再次发送给下一
个小组。详细的提交流程图见附件 8。

VII.H Contractual Arrangements
七、 h 合同安排

representative(s) for the implementation of the approved International Assistance requests in conformity
with UNESCO regulations, following the work plan and budget breakdown described in the originally
approved request.
教科文组织与有关缔约国或

VII.I Evaluation and follow-up of International Assistance

VIII
八
VIII.A Preamble
八. 序言
258. At its second session (Washington, 1978), the Committee adopted the World
Heritage Emblem which had been designed by Mr. Michel Olyff. This Emblem
symbolizes the interdependence of cultural and natural properties: the central square
is a form created by humans and the circle represents nature, the two being
intimately linked. The Emblem is round, like the world, but at the same time it is a
symbol of protection. It symbolizes the Convention, signifies the adherence of States
Parties to the Convention, and serves to identify properties inscribed in the World
Heritage List. It is associated with public knowledge about the Convention and is the
imprimatur of the Convention's credibility and prestige. Above all, it is a
representation of the universal values for which the Convention stands.
委员会第二届会议(1978 年，华盛顿)通过了米歇尔 · 奥利夫先生设计的世界遗
产徽章。这个标志象征着文化和自然属性的相互依存: 中央广场是人类
创造的形式，圆圈代表自然，两者紧密相连。徽章是圆的，像世界一
样，但同时它也是一种保护的象征。它象征着《公约》 ，标志着《公
约》缔约国的加入，并用于识别列入世界遗产名录的财产。它与公众
对《公约》的了解有关，是《公约》可信度和威望的认可。最重要的
是，它代表了《公约》所代表的普世价值。
Decision 43 COM 11A
第 43 COM 11A 号决
定
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 74
世界遗产公约实施运作指南 74

considerations of an artistic nature. However, when the emblem is used in a

UNESCO Secretariat must be strictly followed. The Emblem should always
carry the text “WORLD HERITAGE. PATRIMOINE MONDIAL”. The space
occupied by “PATRIMONIO MUNDIAL” can be used for its translation into

委员会决定，艺术家提议的徽章可以根据使用情况、技术可能性和艺术性
考虑，以任何颜色或大小使用。然而，当徽章与联合国教科文组织

形标准。会徽应该始终带有“世界遗产”的文字。世界遗产”。“
PATRIMONIO MUNDIAL”所占用的空间可用于将其翻译成使用该
徽章的国家的本国语言。
260. In order to ensure the Emblem benefits from as much visibility as possible
while preventing improper uses, the Committee at its twenty-second session (Kyoto,
1998) adopted “Guidelines and Principles for the Use of the World Heritage
Emblem” as set out in the following paragraphs. In addition, a “Table of Uses”
(Annex 14) provides complementary guidance.
为了确保世界遗产徽章尽可能提高知名度，同时防止不当使用，委员会第二
十二届会议(1998 年，京都)通过了”世界遗产徽章使用准则和原则”，
载于以下各段。此外，「使用表」(附件 14)亦提供补充指引。
261. Although there is no mention of the Emblem in the Convention, its use
has been promoted by the Committee to identify properties protected by the
Convention and inscribed on the World Heritage List since its adoption in 1978.
虽然《公约》中没有提到这一标志，但委员会一直推动使用这一标志，以
查明自 1978 年通过《公约》以来受《公约》保护并列入世界遗产
名录的财产。

262. The World Heritage Committee is responsible for determining the use of the
World Heritage Emblem and for making policy prescriptions regarding how it may
be used. Since the adoption by the UNESCO General Conference in October 2007
of the Directives concerning the Use of the Name, Acronym, Logo and Internet
Domain Names of UNESCO
13
, it is strongly encouraged to use the World Heritage
Emblem as part of a linked logo block accompanied by UNESCO’s logo, whenever
feasible. When the emblem is used in a linked logo block with the UNESCO logo,
the graphical standards of the UNESCO Secretariat must be strictly followed. The
use of the World Heritage Emblem alone remains however possible, in line with the
present Guidelines and with the Table of Uses (Annex 14).
世界遗产委员会负责确定世界遗产徽章的使用，并就如何使用世界遗产徽章
制定政策规定。自 2007 年 10 月教科文组织大会通过关于使用教科文
组织名称、首字母缩略词、徽标和因特网域名的指示以来，13 大力鼓

界遗产徽章仍然是可能的，符合目前的指南和使用表(附件 14)。
263. As requested by the Committee at its 26th session (Budapest, 2002), the
World Heritage Emblem, with and without its surrounding text, has been
notified and accepted on 21 May 2003 by the Paris Union Member states under
Article 6ter of the Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property,
adopted in 1883 and revised at Stockholm in 1967. Therefore, UNESCO has
recourse to Paris Convention Member States’ domestic systems to prevent the
use of the World Heritage Emblem where such use falsely suggests a connection
with UNESCO, the World Heritage Convention, or any other abusive use.
根据委员会第二十六届会议(2002 年，布达佩斯)的要求，巴黎联盟成员国
已于 2003 年 5 月 21 日根据 1883 年通过并于 1967 年在斯德哥尔摩
修订的《保护工业产权巴黎公约》第 6 条之三通知并接受了世界遗
产徽章及其周围文本。因此，教科文组织利用《巴黎公约》成员国
的国内制度防止使用世界遗产徽章，如果这种使用错误地表明与教
科文组织、《世界遗产公约》或任何其他滥用有关。
264. The Emblem also has fund-raising potential that can be used to enhance the
marketing value of products with which it is associated. A balance is needed between the
Emblem's use to further the aims of the Convention and optimize knowledge of the
Convention worldwide and the need to prevent its abuse for inaccurate, inappropriate,
and unauthorized commercial or other purposes.
该徽章还具有筹资潜力，可用于提高与其相关的产品的市场价值。需要在以下两
者之间取得平衡: 一方面是为了推进《公约》的目标和在全世界充分了解
《公约》而使用《公约》 ，另一方面是为了防止其被滥用于不准确、不适
当和未经授权的商业或其他目的。

VIII.C Responsibilities of States Parties
八. c 缔约国的责任
267. States Parties to the Convention should take all possible measures to prevent the use of the
Emblem in their respective countries by any group or for any purpose not explicitly recognized by the
Committee. States Parties are encouraged to make full use of national legislation including Trade
Mark Laws.
《公约》缔约国应采取一切可能措施，防止任何团体或为委员会未明确承
认的任何目的在各自国家使用该徽章。鼓励缔约国充分利用国家立
法，包括商标法。
VIII.D Increasing
proper uses of the
World Heritage
Emblem
八. d 增加世界遗产徽章的适当使用
268. Properties inscribed on the World Heritage List should be marked with the emblem jointly with the
UNESCO logo, which should, however, be placed in such a way that they do not visually impair the
property in question.
列入世界遗产名录的财产应与教科文组织的标志一起标有该标志，但标志的
放置方式不应在视觉上损害有关财产。
269. Once a property is inscribed on the World Heritage List, the State Party should place a plaque,
whenever possible, to commemorate this inscription. These plaques are designed to inform the public of the
country concerned and foreign visitors that the property visited has a particular value which has been
recognized by the international community. In other words, the property is exceptional, of interest not only
to one nation, but also to the whole world. However, these plaques have an additional function which is to
inform the general
public about the World
Heritage Convention,
or at least about the
World Heritage concept and the World Heritage List.
一旦某一财产被列入世界遗产名录，缔约国应尽可能放置一块牌匾，以纪念
这一铭文。这些牌匾旨在告知有关国家的公众和外国访客，所访问的
财产具有国际社会公认的特殊价值。换句话说，这些财产是特殊的，
不仅仅是一个国家的利益，也是整个世界的利益。然而，这些牌匾还
有一个额外的功能，那就是让公众了解世界遗产公约，或者至少了解
世界遗产的概念和世界遗产名录。
270. The Committee has adopted the following Guidelines for the production of these plaques:
委员会通过了以下指导方针来制作这些牌匾:
a) the plaque should be so placed that it can easily be seen by visitors, without disfiguring the
property;
匾额应摆放在游人容易看到的地方，而不会损坏物业;
Decision 45 COM 12
第 45 号决定 COM 12
c) the text should mention the property's Outstanding Universal Value; in this regard it
might be useful to give a short description of the property's outstanding characteristics. States Parties
may, if they wish, use the descriptions appearing in the various World Heritage publications or in the
World Heritage exhibit, and which may be obtained from the Secretariat;
案文应提及该财产的突出普遍价值; 在这方面，简要描述该财产的
突出特征可能是有益的。缔约国如果愿意，可以使用各种世界
b) the UNESCO - World Heritage linked logo should appear on the
plaque;
Production of plaques to commemorate the inscription of properties on
the World Heritage List
遗产出版物或世界遗产展览中的描述，这些描述可向秘书处索
取;
d) the text should make reference to the World Heritage Convention and particularly to the
World Heritage List and to the international recognition conferred by inscription on this List (however, it is
not necessary to mention at which session of the Committee the property was inscribed); it may be
appropriate to produce the text in several languages for properties which receive many foreign visitors.
案文应提及《世界遗产公约》 ，特别是《世界遗产名录》 ，以及列入
该名录所赋予的国际承认(然而，没有必要提及该财产是在委员
会的哪届会议上列入名录的) ; 也许应该为接待许多外国访客的财
产制作几种语文的案文。
271. The Committee proposes the following text as an example:
委员会提议以下案文为例:
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 77
实施世界遗产公约的操作指南 77
(a)徽章应用于与《公约》工作实质性相关的所有项目，包括在技术上和法律上尽可能最大限度
地利用已经批准和通过的项目，以促进《公约》。
(b)批准使用徽章的决定应与所涉产品的质量和内容密切相关，而不是与销售产品的数量或预期
的财务回报密切相关。审批的主要标准应该是与世界遗产原则和价值相关的产品的教育、科学、
文化或艺术价值。在没有教育价值或极少教育价值的产品上，如杯子、 t 恤、别针和其他旅游
纪念品，不应经常批准使用徽章。这项政策的例外情况将被考虑用于特殊活动，如委员会会议
和揭牌仪式。
(c)关于授权使用徽章的任何决定必须完全明确，并符合《世界遗产公约》明确和隐含的目标和
价值观。
(d)除非根据这些原则获得授权，否则商业实体直接在自己的材料上使用徽章以表示对世界遗产
的支持是不合法的。然而，委员会承认，任何个人、组织或公司都可以自由出版或制作他们认
为适当的关于世界遗产财产的材料，但根据世界遗产徽章正式授权这样做仍然是委员会的专属
特权，可以按照本准则和原则以及用途表的规定行使。
“(Name of property) has been inscribed upon the World Heritage List of
the Convention concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and
Natural Heritage. Inscription on this List confirms the Outstanding
Universal Value of a cultural or natural property which deserves
protection for the benefit of all humanity.”
a) The Emblem should be utilized for all projects substantially associated
with the work of the Convention, including, to the maximum extent
technically and legally possible, those already approved and adopted, in
order to promote the Convention.
b) A decision to approve use of the Emblem should be linked strongly to
the quality and content of the product with which it is to be associated,
not on the volume of products to be marketed or the financial return
expected. The main criterion for approval should be the educational,
scientific, cultural, or artistic value of the proposed product related to
World Heritage principles and values. Approval should not routinely be
granted to place the Emblem on products that have no, or extremely
little, educational value, such as cups, T-shirts, pins, and other tourist
souvenirs. Exceptions to this policy will be considered for special events,
such as meetings of the Committee and ceremonies at which plaques are
unveiled.
c) Any decision with respect to authorizing the use of the Emblem must
be completely unambiguous and in keeping with the explicit and implicit
goals and values of the World Heritage Convention.
d) Except when authorized in accordance with these principles, it is not
legitimate for commercial entities to use the Emblem directly on their
own material to show their support for World Heritage. The Committee
recognizes, however, that any individual, organization, or company is
free to publish or produce whatever they consider to be appropriate
regarding World Heritage properties, but official authorization to do so
under the World Heritage Emblem remains the exclusive prerogative of
the Committee, to be exercised as prescribed in these Guidelines and
Principles and in the Table of Uses.
”(财产名称)已被列入《保护世界文化和自然遗产公约》的世界遗
产名录。这份名录确认了文化或自然财产的重要普遍价值，值得为
全人类的利益受到保护。”
272. This text could be then followed by a brief description of the property concerned.
这段文字之后可以简要描述相关的财产。
273. Furthermore, the national authorities should encourage World Heritage properties to make a
broad use of the Emblem such as on their letterheads, brochures and staff uniforms.
此外，国家当局应鼓励世界遗产财产广泛使用徽章，例如在其信笺、小册
子和工作人员制服上使用徽章。
274. Third parties which have received the right to produce communication products related to the
World Heritage Convention and World Heritage properties must give the Emblem proper visibility.
They should avoid creating a different Emblem or logo for that particular product.
第三方已经获得了生产与世界遗产公约和世界遗产相关的传播产品的权利，
必须使徽章具有适当的知名度。他们应该避免为特定的产品创造不
同的徽章或标志。
VIII.E Principles on the use of the World Heritage Emblem
八. e 使用世界遗产徽章的原则
275. The responsible authorities are henceforth requested to use the following
principles in making decisions on the use of the Emblem:
现要求主管当局在决定使用该会徽时应遵循以下原则:
Decision 39 COM 11
第 39 号决定 COM 11
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 78
世界遗产公约实施运作指南 78
e) Use of the Emblem by other contracting parties should normally
only be authorized when the proposed use deals directly with World Heritage
properties. Such uses may be granted after approval by the national authorities
of the countries concerned.
其他缔约方使用徽章通常只有在拟议的用途直接涉及世界遗产财产
时才应获得授权。这样的使用可以在有关国家的国家当局批
准后批准。
f) In cases where no specific World Heritage properties are involved
or are not the principal focus of the proposed use, such as general seminars
and/or workshops on scientific issues or conservation techniques, use may be
granted only upon express approval in accordance with these Guidelines and
Principles and with the Table of Uses. Requests for such uses should
specifically document the manner in which the proposed use is expected to
enhance the work of the Convention.
如果不涉及具体的世界遗产财产或不是拟议用途的主要重点，例如
关于科学问题或保护技术的一般性研讨会和/或讲习班，则只
有根据本准则和原则以及使用表明确批准才能批准使用。就
这些用途提出的要求，应具体记录拟议用途预期将如何加强
《公约》的工作。
g) Permission to use the Emblem should not be granted to travel
agencies, airlines, or to any other type of business operating for predominantly
commercial purposes, except under exceptional circumstances and when
manifest benefit to the World Heritage generally or particular World Heritage
properties can be demonstrated. Requests for such use should require approval
in accordance with these Guidelines and Principles and with the Table of Uses.
Such requests should be approved by the national authorities concerned, and be
defined within the framework of specific partnership agreements with
UNESCO/World Heritage Centre.
旅行社、航空公司或主要为商业目的经营的任何其他类型的企业不
应获准使用徽章，除非在特殊情况下，并且能够证明对世界
遗产总体或特定的世界遗产财产有明显的益处。使用上述设
施的申请须根据本指引及原则及使用场地表获得批准。这些
请求应该得到有关国家当局的批准，并在与联合国教科文组
织/世界遗产中心的具体伙伴关系协议框架内定义。
The Secretariat is not to accept any advertising, travel, or other
promotional considerations from travel agencies or other, similar
companies in exchange or in lieu of financial remuneration for use
of the Emblem.
秘书处不得接受来自旅行社或其他类似公司的任何广告、旅
行或其他促销考虑，以换取或代替使用徽章的财务报酬。
h) When commercial benefits are anticipated, the Secretariat should
ensure that the World Heritage Fund receives a fair share of the revenues and
conclude a contract or other agreement that documents the nature of the
understandings that govern the project and the arrangements for provision of
income to the Fund. In all cases of commercial use, any staff time and related
costs for personnel assigned by the Secretariat or other reviewers, as
appropriate, to any initiative, beyond the nominal, must be fully covered by the
party requesting authorization to use the Emblem.
在预期商业利益时，秘书处应确保世界遗产基金获得收入的公平份
额，并缔结一项合同或其他协定，记录指导该项目的谅解的
性质和向基金提供收入的安排。在所有商业使用的情况下，
秘书处或其他审查人员酌情指派给任何倡议的人员的任何工
作时间和
相关费用
除名义上

VIII.F Authorization
procedure for the use of
the World Heritage
Emblem
八. f 使用世界遗产徽章
的授权程序
276. National
authorities may grant the
use of the Emblem to a
national entity, provided
that the project, whether
national or international,
involves only World
Heritage properties
located on the same
national territory.
National authorities’
a) A request indicating the objective of the use of the Emblem, its
duration and territorial validity, should be addressed to the Director of
the World Heritage Centre.
b) The Director of the World Heritage Centre has the authority to grant
the use of the Emblem in accordance with the Guidelines and Principles.
For cases not covered, or not sufficiently covered, by the Guidelines and
Principles and by the Table of Uses, the Director refers the matter to the
Chairperson who, in the most difficult cases, might wish to refer the
matter to the Committee for final decision. A yearly report on the
authorized uses of the Emblem will be submitted to the World Heritage
Committee.
c) Authorization to use the Emblem in major products to be widely
distributed over an undetermined period of time is conditional upon
obtaining the manufacturer’s commitment to consult with countries
concerned and secure their endorsement of texts and images illustrating
properties situated in their territory, at no cost to the Secretariat, together
with the proof that this has been done. The text to be approved should be
provided in either one of the official languages of the Committee or in
the language of the country concerned. A draft model to be used by
States Parties to authorize the use of the Emblem to third parties appears
below.
Agreement requiring quality control of content
Simple agreement of the national authorities
decision should be guided by the Guidelines and Principles and by the Table of
Uses.
国家当局可准许国家实体使用徽章，条件是该项目，无论是国家的还是国
际的，只涉及位于同一国家领土上的世界遗产财产。国家当局的决
定应该遵循指导方针和原则以及用途表。
277. States Parties are invited to provide the Secretariat with the names and
addresses of the authorities in charge of managing the use of the Emblem.
请缔约国向秘书处提供负责管理徽章使用的当局的名称和地址。

VIII.G Right of States Parties to exert quality control
八. g 缔约国实行质量控制的权利
279. Authorization to use the Emblem is inextricably linked to the requirement that the national
authorities may exert quality control over the products with which it is associated.
使用徽章的授权与国家主管部门对其相关产品实施质量控制的要求有着千
丝万缕的联系。
a) The States Parties to the Convention are the only parties authorized to approve the content
(images and text) of any distributed product appearing under the World Heritage Emblem with regard
to the properties located in their territories.
《公约》缔约国是唯一有权批准在其领土内的财产方面出现在世界
遗产徽章下的任何分发产品的内容(图像和文字)的缔约国。
b) States Parties that protect the Emblem legally must review these uses.
合法保护徽章的缔约国必须审查这些用途。
c) Other States Parties may elect to review proposed uses or refer such proposals to the
Secretariat. States Parties are responsible for identifying an appropriate national authority and for
informing the Secretariat whether they wish to review proposed uses or to identify uses that are
inappropriate. The Secretariat maintains a list of responsible national authorities.
其他缔约国可选择审查拟议用途或将此类建议提交秘书处。缔约国
有责任确定适当的国家主管部门，并通知秘书处他们是否希望
审查建议的用途或确定不适当的用途。秘书处有一份负责任的
国家主管部门的名单。

IX.A Information archived by the Secretariat
九. 秘书处存档的资料
280. The Secretariat maintains a database of all documents of the World Heritage
Committee and the General Assembly of States Parties to the World Heritage
秘书处维持一个世界遗产委员会和世界遗产缔约国大会所有文件的数据库
Convention. This database is available at:
https://whc.unesco.org/en/documents.
这个数据库可以在: https://whc.unesco. org/en/documents。
281. The Secretariat ensures that copies of Tentative Lists submissions,
Preliminary Assessment requests, World Heritage nominations, including copies
of maps and relevant information received from States Parties are archived in
hard copy and in electronic format where possible. The Secretariat also arranges
for the archiving of relevant information relating to inscribed properties,
including evaluations and other documents developed by the Advisory Bodies,
any correspondence and reports received from States Parties (including Reactive
Monitoring and Periodic Reports) and correspondence and material from the
Secretariat and World Heritage Committee.
秘书处确保将提交的暂定名单副本、初步评估请求、世界遗产提名，包括
从缔约国收到的地图副本和有关资料，尽可能以硬拷贝和电子格式
存档。秘书处还安排将有关已登记财产的相关信息存档，包括咨询
机构编写的评价和其他文件、从缔约国收到的任何信函和报告(包
括被动监测和定期报告)以及秘书处和世界遗产委员会的信函和材
料。
282. Archived material will be kept in a form appropriate to long-term
storage. Provisions will be made for the storage of paper copies and electronic
copies, as relevant. Provision will be made for copies to be provided to States
Parties as requested.
已存档的资料将以适合长期保存的形式保存。根据相关情况，将对纸质副
本和电子副本的存储作出规定。将根据要求向缔约国提供副本。
283. Nomination dossiers of those properties inscribed on the World Heritage
List by the Committee will be made available for consultation. States Parties are
urged to upload a copy of the nomination on their own websites and inform the
Secretariat of this action. States Parties preparing nominations may wish to use such
information as guides for identifying and elaborating nomination of properties
within their own territories.
委员会将提供那些列入世界遗产名录的物业的提名档案，以供咨询。敦促缔
约国在其自己的网站上传提名副本，并将此行动通知秘书处。准备提
名的缔约国可能希望使用这些信息作为指导，以确定和详细提名的财
产在他们自己的领土。
284. Advisory Body evaluations and Committee decisions concerning each
inscribed property are available on the World Heritage Centre’s website on the
page dedicated to each property of the World Heritage List. For the sites not
inscribed on the List, the Advisory Body evaluation is available on the World
Heritage Centre’s website on the page dedicated to the Committee session when
the nomination was examined.

Authenticity in relation to the World Heritage Convention Annex 4
《世界遗产公约》附件 4 的真实性
AUTHENTICITY IN RELATION
关系的真实性
TO THE WORLD HERITAGE CONVENTION
世界遗产公约
INTRODUCTION
引言
This Annex reproduces the Nara Document on Authenticity, drafted by the 45 participants to the
Nara Conference on Authenticity in Relation to the World Heritage Convention, held at Nara,
Japan, from 1-6 November 1994. The Nara Conference was organized in cooperation with
UNESCO, ICCROM and ICOMOS.
本附件转载了 1994 年 11 月 1 日至 6 日在日本纳拉河举行的世界遗产公约真实性问题奈良会
议 45 名与会者起草的奈良文件。奈良会议是与联合国教科文组织，ICCROM 和 ICOMOS 合
作组织的。
The World Heritage Committee examined the report of the Nara meeting on Authenticity at its 18th
session (Phuket, Thailand, 1994) (see document WHC-94/CONF.003/16).
世界遗产委员会第十八届会议审查了纳拉河真伪问题会议的报告(1994 年，泰国普吉)(见
WHC-94/CONF. 003/16 号文件)。
Subsequent expert meetings have enriched the concept of authenticity in relation to the World
Heritage Convention (see Bibliography of the Operational Guidelines).
随后的专家会议丰富了与《世界遗产公约》有关的真实性概念(见业务准则目录)。
I. THE NARA DOCUMENT ON AUTHENTICITY
奈良文件的真实性
Preamble
序言
1. We, the experts assembled in Nara (Japan), wish to acknowledge the generous spirit and intellectual
courage of the Japanese authorities in providing a timely forum in which we could challenge conventional
thinking in the conservation field, and debate ways and means of broadening our horizons to bring greater
respect for cultural and heritage diversity to conservation practice.
我们，聚集在纳拉河(日本)的专家们，希望感谢日本当局的慷慨精神和智慧勇气，提供了一个及时的
论坛，让我们能够挑战保护领域的传统思维，并讨论如何扩大我们的视野，使保护做法更加尊
重文化和遗产多样性。
2. We also wish to acknowledge the value of the framework for discussion provided by the World Heritage
Committee's desire to apply the test of authenticity in ways which accord full respect to the social and cultural
values of all societies, in examining the outstanding universal value of cultural properties proposed for the
World Heritage List.
我们还要承认，世界遗产委员会希望以充分尊重所有社会的社会和文化价值的方式，在审查提议列入
世界遗产名录的文化财产的突出普遍价值时，应用真实性检验办法，这一愿望提供了讨论框架。
3. The Nara Document on Authenticity is conceived in the spirit of the Charter of Venice, 1964, and
builds on it and extends it in response to the expanding scope of cultural heritage concerns and interests
in our contemporary world.
关于真实性的奈良文件是根据 1964 年《威尼斯宪章》的精神构思的，并以此为基础，针对我们当
代世界对文化遗产的关注和兴趣范围不断扩大而加以扩展。
4. In a world that is increasingly subject to the forces of globalization and homogenization, and in a world
in which the search for cultural identity is sometimes pursued through aggressive nationalism and the
suppression of the cultures of minorities, the essential contribution made by the consideration of authenticity
in conservation practice is to clarify and illuminate the collective memory of humanity.
在一个日益受到全球化和同质化力量影响的世界中，在一个有时通过侵略性民族主义和压制少数群体
文化来寻求文化特性的世界中，在保护实践中考虑真实性的重要贡献是澄清和阐明人类的集体
记忆。
Cultural Diversity and Heritage Diversity
文化多样性和遗产多样性
5. The diversity of cultures and heritage in our world is an irreplaceable source of spiritual and
intellectual richness for all humankind. The protection and enhancement of cultural and heritage
diversity in our world should be actively promoted as an essential aspect of human development.
我们世界文化和遗产的多样性是全人类精神和智力丰富性的不可替代的来源。保护和加强我们世
界的文化和遗产多样性应该作为人类发展的一个重要方面得到积极推动。
6. Cultural heritage diversity exists in time and space, and demands respect for other cultures and all
aspects of their belief systems. In cases where cultural values appear to be in conflict, respect for cultural
diversity demands acknowledgment of the legitimacy of the cultural values of all parties.
文化遗产的多样性存在于时间和空间中，需要尊重其他文化及其信仰体系的各个方面。在文化价
值观发生冲突的情况下，对文化多样性的尊重要求承认各方文化价值观的合法性。
7. All cultures and societies are rooted in the particular forms and means of tangible and intangible
expression which constitute their heritage, and these should be respected.
所有文化和社会都植根于构成其遗产的有形和无形表达的特定形式和手段，这些都应得到尊重。
8. It is important to underline a fundamental principle of UNESCO, to the effect that the cultural heritage
of each is the cultural heritage of all. Responsibility for cultural heritage and the management of it
强调联合国教科文组织的一个基本原则很重要，即每个人的文化遗产都是所有人的文化遗产。文化遗
产的责任及其管理
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 96
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 96
Authenticity in relation to the World Heritage Convention Annex 4
《世界遗产公约》附件 4 的真实性
belongs, in the first place, to the cultural community that has generated it, and subsequently to that
which cares for it. However, in addition to these responsibilities, adherence to the international
charters and conventions developed for conservation of cultural heritage also obliges
consideration of the principles and responsibilities flowing from them. Balancing their own
requirements with those of other cultural communities is, for each community, highly desirable,
provided achieving this balance does not undermine their fundamental cultural values.
首先，它属于产生它的文化群体，然后才属于那些关心它的人。然而，除了这些责任之外，
遵守为保护文化遗产而制定的国际宪章和公约也要求考虑这些宪章和公约所产生的原则和责
任。对于每个社区来说，平衡他们自己的需求和其他文化群体的需求是非常可取的，只要实
现这种平衡不损害他们的基本文化价值观。
Values and authenticity
价值观和真实性
9. Conservation of cultural heritage in all its forms and historical periods is rooted in the values attributed
to the heritage. Our ability to understand these values depends, in part, on the degree to which information
sources about these values may be understood as credible or truthful. Knowledge and understanding of these
sources of information, in relation to original and subsequent characteristics of the cultural heritage, and their
meaning, is a requisite basis for assessing all aspects of authenticity.
一切形式和历史时期的文化遗产保护植根于遗产的价值观。我们理解这些价值观的能力部分取决于这
些价值观的信息来源可以被理解为可信或真实的程度。了解和理解这些信息来源与文化遗产的
原始和后续特征及其含义有关的情况，是评估真实性的所有方面的必要基础。
10. Authenticity, considered in this way and affirmed in the Charter of Venice, appears as the essential
qualifying factor concerning values. The understanding of authenticity plays a fundamental role in all
scientific studies of the cultural heritage, in conservation and restoration planning, as well as within the
inscription procedures used for the World Heritage Convention and other cultural heritage inventories.
以这种方式考虑并在《威尼斯宪章》中确认的真实性，似乎是关于价值观的基本限定因素。对真实性
的理解在文化遗产的所有科学研究、保护和修复规划以及《世界遗产公约》和其他文化遗产目
录所使用的登记程序中发挥着根本作用。
11. All judgements about values attributed to cultural properties as well as the credibility of related
information sources may differ from culture to culture, and even within the same culture. It is thus not
possible to base judgements of values and authenticity within fixed criteria. On the contrary, the respect
due to all cultures requires that heritage properties must be considered and judged within the cultural
contexts to which they belong.
对于归因于文化特性的价值观以及相关信息来源的可信度的所有判断可能因文化而异，甚至在同
一文化中也是如此。因此，根据固定的标准来判断价值和真实性是不可能的。相反，对所有
文化的尊重要求遗产属性必须在它们所属的文化背景下被考虑和判断。
12. Therefore, it is of the highest importance and urgency that, within each culture, recognition be
accorded to the specific nature of its heritage values and the credibility and truthfulness of related
information sources.
因此，在每一种文化中，承认其遗产价值的具体性质以及相关信息来源的可信性和真实性，具有
最高的重要性和紧迫性。
13. Depending on the nature of the cultural heritage, its cultural context, and its evolution through
time, authenticity judgements may be linked to the worth of a great variety of sources of information.
Aspects of the sources may include form and design, materials and substance, use and function, traditions
and techniques, location and setting, and spirit and feeling, and other internal and external factors. The
use of these sources permits elaboration of the specific artistic, historic, social, and scientific dimensions
of the cultural heritage being examined.
根据文化遗产的性质、其文化背景及其随时间的演变，真实性判断可能与各种信息来源的价值有
关。来源的方面可能包括形式和设计，材料和物质，使用和功能，传统和技术，位置和设置，
精神和感觉，以及其他内部和外部因素。这些来源的使用允许详细阐述特定的艺术，历史，
社会和科学方面的文化遗产被检查。
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 97
实施世界遗产公约的操作指南
Authenticity in relation to the World Heritage Convention Annex 4
《世界遗产公约》附件 4 的真实性
Appendix 1: Suggestions for follow-up
附录一: 跟进建议
1. Respect for cultural and heritage diversity requires conscious efforts to avoid imposing mechanistic
formulae or standardized procedures in attempting to define or determine authenticity of particular
monuments and sites.
尊重文化和遗产多样性需要有意识地努力避免在试图界定或确定特定古迹和遗址的真实性时强加机械
公式或标准化程序。
2. Efforts to determine authenticity in a manner respectful of cultures and heritage diversity requires
approaches which encourage cultures to develop analytical processes and tools specific to their nature and
needs. Such approaches may have several aspects in common:
努力以尊重文化和遗产多样性的方式确定真实性，需要采取鼓励各种文化发展适合其性质和需要的分
析程序和工具的办法。这些方法可能有几个共同点:
- efforts to ensure assessment of authenticity involve multidisciplinary collaboration and the
appropriate utilisation of all available expertise and knowledge;
确保真实性评估的努力涉及多学科合作和适当利用所有现有的专门知识和知识;
- efforts to ensure attributed values are truly representative of a culture and the diversity of its
interests, in particular monuments and sites;
努力确保赋予的价值真正代表一种文化及其利益的多样性，特别是古迹和遗址;
- efforts to document clearly the particular nature of authenticity for monuments and sites as a
practical guide to future treatment and monitoring;
努力清楚地记录古迹和遗址真实性的特殊性质，作为今后处理和监测的实用指南;
- efforts to update authenticity assessments in light of changing values and circumstances.
努力根据不断变化的价值观和情况更新真实性评估。
3. Particularly important are efforts to ensure that attributed values are respected, and that their
determination included efforts to build, as far as possible, a multidisciplinary and community consensus
concerning these values.
特别重要的是努力确保所赋予的价值得到尊重，其决心包括努力尽可能就这些价值建立多学科和
社区共识。
4. Approaches should also build on and facilitate international co-operation among all those with an
interest in conservation of cultural heritage, in order to improve global respect and understanding for the
diverse expressions and values of each culture.
各种办法还应以所有关心保护文化遗产的各方之间的国际合作为基础并促进这种合作，以便在全
球范围内更好地尊重和理解每种文化的不同表现形式和价值观。
5. Continuation and extension of this dialogue to the various regions and cultures of the world is a
prerequisite to increasing the practical value of consideration of authenticity in the conservation of the
common heritage of humankind.
继续并将这种对话扩大到世界各个区域和文化，是提高在保护人类共同遗产方面考虑真实性的实
际价值的先决条件。
6. Increasing awareness within the public of this fundamental dimension of heritage is an absolute
necessity in order to arrive at concrete measures for safeguarding the vestiges of the past. This means
developing greater understanding of the values represented by the cultural properties themselves, as well
as respecting the role such monuments and sites play in contemporary society.
提高公众对遗产这一基本维度的认识是绝对必要的，以便达成具体措施来保护过去的遗迹。这意
味着要更好地理解文化财产本身所代表的价值，以及尊重这些纪念碑和遗址在当代社会中所
扮演的角色。
Appendix 2: Definitions
附录 2: 定义
Conservation: all efforts designed to understand cultural heritage, know its history and meaning, ensure
its material safeguard and, as required, its presentation, restoration and enhancement. (Cultural heritage
is understood to include monuments, groups of buildings and sites of cultural value as defined in Article 1
of the World Heritage Convention).
保护: 所有旨在了解文化遗产、了解其历史和意义、确保其物质保障以及根据需要展示、修复和
加强的努力。(文化遗产包括《世界遗产公约》第 1 条所界定的古迹、建筑群和具有文化价值的地
点)。
Information sources: all material, written, oral and figurative sources which make it possible to know the
nature, specifications, meaning and history of the cultural heritage.
资料来源: 所有可以了解文化遗产的性质、规格、意义和历史的材料、书面、口头和比喻资料。

The Nara meeting brought together 45 experts from 26 countries and international organizations from
around the world. Their papers are contained in the volume cited above, as is the Nara document prepared
in a working group of 12 meeting participants and edited by Raymond Lemaire and Herb Stovel. This

Significant post-Nara regional meetings (as of January 2005):
Nara 之后的重要区域会议 ( 截至 2005 年 1 月 ) :
Authenticity and Monitoring, October 17-22, 1995, Cesky Krumlov, Czech Republic, ICOMOS European
Conference, 1995.
真实性和监控，1995 年 10 月 17-22 日，捷克共和国 Cesky Krumlov，ICOMOS 欧洲会议，1995 年。
The European ICOMOS Conference of 17-22 October, 1995 which took place in Cesky Krumlov, Czech
Republic brought together 18 European members of ICOMOS to present national views of the application of
authenticity concepts from 14 countries. A synthesis of presentations affirmed the importance of authenticity
within the analytical processes we apply to conservation problems as a means of assuring truthful, sincere and
honest approaches to conservation problems, and gave emphasis to strengthening the notion of dynamic
conservation in order to apply authenticity analysis appropriately to cultural landscapes and urban settings.
1995 年 10 月 17 日至 22 日在捷克共和国 Cesky Krumlov 举行的 ICOMOS 欧洲会议汇集了 ICOMOS 的
18 个欧洲成员国，就 14 个国家应用真实性概念提出了各国的看法。综合介绍肯定了在我们应用于保
护问题的分析过程中真实性的重要性，以此作为确保以真实、真诚和诚实的方式处理保护问题的一种
手段，并强调加强动态保护的概念，以便将真实性分析适当应用于文化景观和城市环境。
Interamerican symposium on authenticity in the conservation and management of the cultural heritage,
US/ICOMOS, The Getty Conservation Institute, San Antonio, Texas 1996.
美洲文化遗产保护和管理的真实性研讨会，美国/ICOMOS，盖蒂保护研究所，圣安东尼奥，德克
萨斯州，1996 年。
This Authenticity meeting which took place in San Antonio, Texas, USA in March 1996, brought
together participants from ICOMOS national committees of North, Central and South America to debate
the application of the concepts of Nara. The meeting adopted the Declaration of San Antonio, which
discussed the relationship between authenticity and identity, history, materials, social value, dynamic and
static sites, stewardship and economics, and contained recommendations extending “proofs” of
authenticity to include reflection of its true value, integrity, context, identity, use and function, as well as
recommendations pertinent to different typologies of sites.
这次真实性会议于 1996 年 3 月在美国德克萨斯州圣安东尼奥举行，来自国际科学文化组织北美、
中美和南美洲国家委员会的与会者参加了会议，讨论纳拉河概念的适用问题。会议通过了《圣安
东尼奥宣言》 ，其中讨论了真实性与身份、历史、材料、社会价值、动态和静态场址、管理和经
济之间的关系，并载有扩大真实性”证明”的建议，以反映其真实价值、完整性、背景、身份、
使用和功能，以及与不同类型场址有关的建议。
Saouma-Forero, Galia, (edited by), Authenticity and integrity in an African context: expert meeting, Great
Zimbabwe, Zimbabwe, 26-29 May 2000, UNESCO - World Heritage Centre, Paris 2001.
Saouma-Forero，Galia，(编辑) ，非洲背景下的真实性和完整性: 专家会议，大津巴布韦，津巴布
韦，2000 年 5 月 26 日至 29 日，教科文组织-世界遗产中心，巴黎，2001 年。
The Great Zimbabwe meeting organised by the World Heritage Centre (26-29 May 2000) focused attention on

世界遗产中心组织的大津巴布韦会议(2000 年 5 月 26 日至 29 日)集中注意非洲背景下的真实性和完整性。

A. THE JOINT ICOMOS/IUCN PROCEDURE FOR PRELIMINARY ASSESSMENT OF
POTENTIAL NOMINATED PROPERTIES
ICOMOS/世界自然保护联盟关于对可能提名的物业进行初步评估的联合程序
The below paragraphs outline agreed procedures of ICOMOS and IUCN to undertake Preliminary
Assessments of potential nominated properties (Preliminary Assessments), based on requests
(Preliminary Assessment requests) made by the relevant State(s) Party(ies).
以下各段概述了 ICOMOS 和自然保护联盟商定的程序，以便根据有关缔约国提出的请求(初
步评估请求) ，对可能提名的物业进行初步评估(初步评估)。
In undertaking Preliminary Assessments, ICOMOS (the International Council of Monuments and
Sites) and IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature) are guided by the Operational
Guidelines (see Paragraph 122).
在进行初步评估时，ICOMOS (国际古迹和遗址理事会)和 IUCN (国际自然保护联盟)遵循业
务准则(见第 122 段)。
Preliminary Assessments will be undertaken by ICOMOS and IUCN on a joint basis whenever relevant,
and will be an independent desk review, which will include consultation with expert reviewers.
初步评估将在适当时由国际化学品观测组织和自然保护联盟联合进行，并将是一次独立的案头
审查，其中包括与专家审查员协商。
Once Preliminary Assessment requests from States Parties have been checked for completeness by
the UNESCO World Heritage Centre, the requests that are deemed as complete are delivered to
ICOMOS and IUCN. From this point, dialogue and consultation with the relevant States Parties
may begin and will continue throughout the assessment process.
一旦教科文组织世界遗产中心对缔约国提出的初步评估请求的完整性进行了检查，被视为完
整的请求将送交国际化学品卫生组织理事会和自然保护联盟。从这一点开始，与相关缔约国
的对话和磋商可能开始，并将在整个评估过程中继续。
Preliminary Assessments aim to both support efficient work to develop successful nominations, and
to avoid situations where nominations that are unlikely to be successful proceed further.
初步评估旨在支持开发成功提名的有效工作，并避免不太可能成功的提名进一步进行的情况。
The ICOMOS/IUCN assessment process involves the following stages:
ICOMOS/自然保护联盟的评估过程包括以下阶段:
1. Data Assembly
数据汇编
Following receipt of the Preliminary Assessment requests from the World Heritage Centre, a
standardised analysis is compiled on the potential nominated property using ICOMOS and IUCN
thematic studies, ICOMOS Filling the gaps study, the World Database on Protected Areas and other
IUCN global databases as relevant. This may include additional literature and advice provided
concerning the potential nominated property, or concerning Tentative Lists, through the
International Assistance and Upstream process mechanisms.
在收到世界遗产中心提出的初步评估要求之后，利用国际保护自然资源组织和自然保护联盟
的专题研究、国际保护自然资源组织填补空白研究、世界保护区数据库和自然保护联盟其他
相关全球数据库，对可能提名的财产进行了标准化分析。这可能包括通过国际援助和上游过
程机制提供的关于潜在提名财产或关于暂定清单的额外文献和建议。
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 116
实施世界遗产公约的操作指南 116
Procedures of the Advisory Bodies for Preliminary Assessments and the Evaluation of Nominations Annex 6
初步评审及提名评审咨询组织的程序附件 6
2. Exchange with States Parties
与缔约国交流
The Advisory Bodies will review the requests received, check the information provided and wherever
necessary, will request additional information from the State(s) Party(ies), which should be submitted to
the Secretariat. This may involve letters, face-to face meetings, teleconferences or other forms of
communication as agreed between the Advisory Body(ies) and the State(s) Party(ies) concerned. In all
assessments there will be dialogue between the Advisory Bodies and the concerned State(s) Party(ies) to
agree on the process of exchange, and to ensure full and effective feedback of conclusions.
咨询机构将审查收到的请求，核对所提供的资料，并在必要时要求缔约国提供补充资料，这些
资料应提交秘书处。这可能涉及信件、面对面会议、电话会议或咨询机构与有关缔约国之间商
定的其他形式的沟通。在所有评估中，咨询机构和有关缔约国之间将进行对话，商定交流进程，
并确保对结论作出充分和有效的反馈。
3. Desk Reviews
桌面评论
Preliminary Assessments are conducted exclusively on a desk review basis, focused in particular on
the potential justification of Outstanding Universal Value, and related questions of authenticity and
integrity. They do not focus in depth on protection and management issues of the potential
nominated properties unless major issues have become evident at this early stage of analysis. There
is no possibility for any field mission to take place in the framework of a Preliminary Assessment.
初步评估完全是在案头审查的基础上进行的，特别侧重于突出普遍价值的潜在理由以及真实
性和完整性的相关问题。他们没有深入关注潜在提名物业的保护和管理问题，除非主要问题
在分析的早期阶段已经变得明显。任何实地考察都不可能在初步评估的框架内进行。
Each Preliminary Assessment involves the input of a range of experts who are knowledgeable
about the site in its geo-cultural and ecological context and who advise on the potential of the site
to justify Outstanding Universal Value and to achieve the development of a robust World Heritage
nomination dossier.
每次初步评估都需要一系列专家的投入，这些专家了解该遗址的地理文化和生态背景，并就
该遗址的潜力提出建议，以证明其具有突出的普遍价值，并建立一个强有力的世界遗产提名
档案。
The experts are specialists identified within the membership of ICOMOS, its National and
International Scientific Committees, and within IUCN Commissions and Members and IUCN
Regional Offices. Experts may also be identified by ICOMOS and IUCN within other specialist
networks or institutions, universities and research institutes.
这些专家是国际化学品卫生组织及其国家和国际科学委员会成员以及自然保护联盟委员会和
成员及自然保护联盟区域办事处内确定的专家。ICOMOS 和 IUCN 也可以在其他专家网络
或机构、大学和研究机构中识别专家。
The assessment may include consultation with local NGOs, communities, indigenous peoples and
other interested parties in the potential nominated property and/or coordination with other
international conservation instruments.
评估可包括与当地非政府组织、社区、原住民和其他有关各方就可能提名的财产进行协商和
/或与其他国际养护文书进行协调。
4. Review by the ICOMOS/IUCN Panel for Preliminary Assessment of Potential Nominated
Properties
ICOMOS/IUCN 小组对潜在提名物业进行初步评估的审查
The joint ICOMOS/IUCN Panel comprises individuals appointed by ICOMOS and IUCN from
their networks who collectively possess a wide range of relevant cultural and natural heritage skills
and experience, having regard to gender and regional balance. Some of these members serve on the
Panel for a fixed term while others are appointed for one year only according to the characteristics
of the potential nominated properties to be examined in a particular year.
国际文化遗产组织/自然保护联盟联合小组由国际文化遗产组织和自然保护联盟从其网络中
任命的个人组成，他们集体拥有广泛的相关文化和自然遗产技能和经验，同时考虑到性别和
区域平衡。其中一些成员的任期是固定的，而另一些成员的任期则是一年，只是根据某一年
可能被提名的物业的特点而任命。
The Panel meets once annually in May and considers each Preliminary Assessment. The Panel aims
to reach its conclusions by consensus. If there is a need for further clarification in relation to
detailed questions from the Panel, further exchange with relevant State(s) Party(ies) is organized
following the Panel meeting. Any questions from the Panel can only be on points of details
necessary and agreed by the Panel to complete the evaluation of the Preliminary Assessment.
小组每年 5 月举行一次会议，审议每项初步评估。专家小组旨在以协商一致方式达成结论。
如果需要进一步澄清专家组提出的详细问题，则在专家组会议之后安排与有关缔约国进行进
一步交流。专家组提出的任何问题只能涉及必要的细节问题，并经专家组同意，以完成初步
评估的评估。
The Preliminary Assessment Report provides an assessment, to a standard format, on whether the
site has the potential to justify Outstanding Universal Value, including an assessment of the
proposed nomination strategy, considerations on authenticity (for cultural sites) and integrity, the
framework for comparative analysis and protection and management issues. Conclusions of the
report will inform whether or not the site might have the potential to justify Outstanding Universal
Value and to achieve the development of a robust World Heritage nomination, and if so, under
what conditions; or whether further exploratory work is needed before it can be determined whether
or not the site may have potential to justify Outstanding Universal Value, or to achieve the
development of a robust World Heritage nomination. The formats for Preliminary Assessment
Reports, together with any other relevant information on review formats and working methods are
made publicly available by ICOMOS and IUCN via their websites.
初步评估报告以标准格式评估该网站是否有潜力证明杰出的普遍价值，包括评估拟议的提名
战略、对真实性(文化遗址)和完整性的考虑、比较分析框架以及保护和管理问题。报告的结
论将说明该遗址是否有潜力证明杰出的普遍价值是合理的，是否有可能制定一项强有力的世
界遗产提名，如果有，在什么条件下; 或者在确定该遗址是否有潜力证明杰出的普遍价值是
合理的，或者是否有可能制定一项强有力的世界遗产提名之前，是否需要进一步的探索性工
作。初步评估报告的格式，以及关于审查格式和工作方法的任何其他相关信息，由国际化学
品卫生组织理事会和自然保护联盟通过其网站公布。
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 117
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 117
Procedures of the Advisory Bodies for Preliminary Assessments and the Evaluation of Nominations Annex 6
初步评审及提名评审咨询组织的程序附件 6
5. Delivery of the Preliminary Assessment Reports
提交初步评估报告
Following the Panel meeting, the Preliminary Assessment Reports are finalised and sent to the
World Heritage Centre for distribution to State(s) Party(ies) that has requested the Preliminary
Assessment. The Preliminary Assessment Report shall be provided in one of the two working
languages of the Convention. The names and qualifications of the members of the ICOMOS/IUCN
Preliminary Assessment Panel are then published on the ICOMOS and IUCN web sites.
小组会议结束后，初步评估报告定稿，送交世界文化遗产中心分发给要求进行初步评估的缔
约国。初步评估报告须以公约的两种工作语文之一提供。ICOMOS/IUCN 初步评估小组成员
的姓名和资格将在 ICOMOS 和 IUCN 网站上公布。
As a desk exercise, all advice provided is subject to consideration through a full evaluation,
including an evaluation mission, should a nomination be submitted.
作为案头工作，所有提供的咨询意见均须通过全面评价加以考虑，包括在提名时派出评价团。
The relevant final Preliminary Assessment Reports will be made available to the ICOMOS and
IUCN World Heritage Panels should a potential nominated property that has been assessed become
the subject of a full Advisory Body evaluation in future nomination processes.
如果经过评估的可能被提名的财产在今后的提名进程中成为咨询机构全面评估的主题，将向
国际化学品管理组织和世界自然保护联盟世界遗产小组提供相关的初步评估最后报告。
B. THE ICOMOS PROCEDURE FOR THE EVALUATION OF CULTURAL PROPERTIES
ICOMOS 文化财产评估程序
In carrying out its evaluation of nominations of cultural properties ICOMOS (the International
Council of Monuments and Sites) is guided by the Operational Guidelines; (see Paragraph 148).
国际古迹和遗址理事会(国际古迹和遗址理事会)在评价文化财产提名时遵循业务准则(见第
148 段)。
Once new nominations have been checked for completeness by the UNESCO World Heritage
Centre, the nomination dossiers that are deemed as complete are delivered to ICOMOS, where they
are handled by the ICOMOS World Heritage Unit. From this point, dialogue and consultation with
the nominating States Parties may begin and will continue throughout the evaluation process.
ICOMOS will use its best endeavours to allocate its available resources equitably, efficiently and
effectively to maximise the opportunity for dialogue with all nominating States Parties.
一旦教科文组织世界遗产中心检查新的提名是否完整，被视为完整的提名档案将送交国际遗
产保护协会，由国际遗产保护协会世界遗产股处理。从这一点开始，与提名缔约国的对话和
磋商可能开始，并将在整个评估过程中继续。ICOMOS 将尽最大努力公平、高效和有效地
分配其可用资源，以最大限度地提高与所有提名缔约国对话的机会。
The ICOMOS evaluation process involves the following stages as illustrated in figure 1:
ICOMOS 评估过程包括以下阶段，如图 1 所示:
1. Requests for further information
索取进一步资料
When it has identified that further information or clarification of existing information is needed,
ICOMOS starts a dialogue with States Parties in order to explore ways to meet the needs. This may
involve letters, face-to face meetings, teleconferences or other forms of communication as agreed
between ICOMOS and the State Party concerned.
在确定需要进一步提供资料或澄清现有资料时，科学理事会开始与缔约国进行对话，以探讨
满足需要的方式。这可能包括信件，面对面会议，电话会议或其他形式的沟通，如
ICOMOS 和有关缔约国之间达成的协议。
2. Desk Reviews
桌面评论
Each nomination is assessed by up to ten experts who are knowledgeable about the property in its
geo-cultural context and who advise on the proposed “Outstanding Universal Value” of the
nominated property. This is essentially a “library” exercise undertaken by specialist academics
within the membership of ICOMOS, its National and International Committees, or by individuals
within many other specialist networks or institutions with which it is linked.
每项提名最多由 10 名专家进行评估，这些专家了解该物业的地理文化背景，并就提名物业
的拟议”突出普遍价值”提出建议。这基本上是一项”图书馆”工作，由 ICOMOS 及其国
家和国际委员会成员中的专家学者或与 ICOMOS 有联系的许多其他专家网络或机构中的个
人进行。
3. On site missions
实地考察任务
These are carried out by experts who have practical experience of the management, conservation, and
authenticity aspects of individual properties. The process of selecting these experts makes full use of the
ICOMOS network. The advice of International Scientific Committees and individual members is
sought, as is that of specialist bodies with whom ICOMOS has partnership agreements, such as The
International Committee for the Conservation of the Industrial Heritage (TICCIH), the International
Federation of Landscape Architects (IFLA), and the International Committee for the Documentation and
Conservation of Monuments and Sites of the Modern Movement (DoCoMoMo).
这些项目由具有管理、保护和个人财产真实性方面实际经验的专家进行。选择这些专家的过程
充分利用了 ICOMOS 网络。征求国际科学委员会和个人成员的意见，以及国际风景园林师联合
会与之有伙伴关系协议的专门机构的意见，如国际工业遗产保护委员会、国际风景园林师联合
会和现代运动古迹和遗址文献记录和保护国际委员会。
In selecting experts to carry out on-site missions, the policy of ICOMOS is wherever possible to choose
someone from the region in which the nominated property is located. Such experts are required to be
experienced in heritage management and conservation of the type of property concerned: they are not
在挑选专家进行实地考察时，海洋生物保护组织的政策是在任何可能的情况下从提名的财产所
在地区挑选人员。这些专家必须在遗产管理和相关财产类型的保护方面有经验: 他们不是
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 118
实施世界遗产公约的操作指南 118
Procedures of the Advisory Bodies for Preliminary Assessments and the Evaluation of Nominations Annex 6
初步评审及提名评审咨询组织的程序附件 6
necessarily high academic experts. They are expected to be able to talk to site managers on a basis of
professional equality and to make informed assessments of management plans, conservation practices,
visitor handling, etc. They are provided with detailed briefings, which include copies of the relevant
information from the dossiers. The dates and programmes of their visits are agreed in consultation with
States Parties, who are requested to ensure that ICOMOS evaluation missions are given a low profile so
far as the media are concerned. ICOMOS experts submit their reports in confidence on practical aspects
of the properties concerned, and may also comment in their reports on other aspects of the nomination.
必须是高学术水平的专家。他们应能在专业平等的基础上与场地管理人员交谈，并对管理计划、
保育措施、访客处理等作出知情的评估。他们会得到详细的简报，其中包括档案中相关信息的
副本。它们的访问日期和方案是与缔约国协商商定的，要求缔约国确保就媒体而言，科学、文
化组织理事会的评价特派团保持低调。ICOMOS 专家秘密提交他们关于相关财产的实际方面的
报告，也可以在他们的报告中对提名的其他方面进行评论。
3bis. Other sources of information
3 之二. 其他资料来源
Other relevant institutions, such as UNESCO Chairs, universities and research institutes may also
be consulted during the evaluation process, and listed, as appropriate, in the evaluation report.
其他有关机构，如教科文组织讲座、大学和研究机构，也可在评价过程中征求意见，并酌情
列入评价报告。
4. Review by the ICOMOS Panel
ICOMOS 小组的审查
The ICOMOS World Heritage Panel comprises individual ICOMOS members who collectively
represent all regions of the world and possess a wide range of relevant cultural heritage skills and
experience. Some of these members serve on the Panel for a fixed term while others are appointed
for one year only according to the characteristics of the nominated properties to be examined.
ICOMOS will include within its Panel membership some experts who have past experience as
members of States Parties delegations, but who are no longer serving as members of the World
Heritage Committee. These experts will serve in a personal and professional capacity.
ICOMOS 世界遗产小组由 ICOMOS 成员组成，他们集体代表世界所有地区，拥有广泛的相
关文化遗产技能和经验。其中一些成员的任期为定期，而另一些成员的任期仅为一年，他们
是根据拟审查的提名物业的特点而获委任。ICOMOS 将在其小组成员中包括一些专家，这
些专家过去曾担任缔约国代表团成员，但现已不再担任世界遗产委员会成员。这些专家将以
个人和专业身份服务。
The Panel meets twice, first in December and then in March. At the first meeting, the Panel
evaluates each nomination, based on the reports of Desk experts and of the site missions.
该小组举行了两次会议，第一次在 12 月，然后在 3 月。在第一次会议上，小组根据 Desk 专
家的报告和现场任务评估每个提名。
The Panel aims to reach its recommendations on nominations by consensus.
专家小组的目标是通过协商一致达成提名的建议。
The first Panel may come to final collective recommendations on some nominations while for others
further dialogue with States Parties may be agreed related to the need for more information or the need
for adjustments to the approach of the nomination. In cases where the Panel has concluded that the
nomination has no potential to justify Outstanding Universal Value, ICOMOS will contact States Parties
at this stage. A short interim report for each nomination, in one of the two working languages of the
Convention, outlining the status and any issues relevant to the evaluation process, and any further
requests for supplementary information, will be provided in January to the nominating States Parties and
copied to the World Heritage Centre for distribution to the Chair of the World Heritage Committee.
第一个小组可就某些提名提出最后的集体建议，而对于其他提名，可商定与缔约国就是否需要
更多信息或是否需要调整提名办法进行进一步对话。如果专家小组认为提名没有潜力证明突出
的普遍价值，ICOMOS 将在这个阶段与缔约国联系。将于 1 月份以《公约》两种工作语文之一
向提名缔约国提供每项提名的简短临时报告，概述评价进程的现状和任何有关问题，以及任何
进一步要求提供补充资料的请求，并将复印件送交世界遗产中心，以便分发给世界遗产委员会
主席。
The second Panel undertakes further evaluation of nominations for which a recommendation has
not yet been reached based on the receipt of further information or the outcome of dialogue with
States Parties. The Panel then agrees the remaining collective recommendations. Following the
second Panel meeting, the text of all evaluations is finalised and sent to the World Heritage Centre
for distribution to States Parties. The names and qualifications of the members of the Panel are then
provided to the World Heritage Centre and published on the ICOMOS web site.
第二小组根据收到的进一步资料或与缔约国对话的结果，对尚未提出建议的提名进行进一步
评价。小组然后同意其余的集体建议。在第二次专家小组会议之后，所有评估的文本最终定
稿并送往世界遗产中心分发给缔约国。小组成员的姓名和资历随后提供给世界遗产中心，并
在 ICOMOS 网站上公布。
The ICOMOS evaluations provide an assessment of Outstanding Universal Value, including the
applicability of the criteria and the requirements of integrity and authenticity, assessment of the
adequacy of legislative protection, management, and the state of conservation, and finally draft
recommendations to the World Heritage Committee with respect to inscription.
ICOMOS 的评价对突出的普遍价值进行了评估，包括标准的适用性以及完整性和真实性的
要求，对立法保护、管理和保护状况的充分性进行了评估，最后向世界遗产委员会提出了有
关登记的建议草案。

C. THE IUCN PROCEDURE FOR THE EVALUATION OF NATURAL PROPERTIES
自然保护联盟自然资源评估程序
1. In carrying out its evaluation of nominations of natural properties, IUCN (the International Union
for Conservation of Nature) is guided by the Operational Guidelines (see Paragraph 148). The evaluation
process (see Figure 2) involves five elements:
世界自然保护联盟(国际自然保护联盟)在对自然财产提名进行评估时，遵循业务准则(见第 148 段)。
评估过程(见图 2)包括五个要素:
(i) Data Assembly. Following receipt of the nomination dossier from the World Heritage Centre, a
standardised analysis is compiled on the property using the World Database on Protected Areas and other
IUCN global databases and thematic studies. This may include comparative analyses on biodiversity values
undertaken in partnership with the UNEP World Conservation Monitoring Centre (UNEP-WCMC). Key
findings of data analysis are the subject of dialogue with the State Party during the evaluation mission, and at
other stages of the process.
数据汇编。在收到世界遗产中心的提名档案后，利用世界保护区数据库和世界自然保护联盟其
他全球数据库和专题研究对该财产进行了标准化分析。这可能包括与环境署世界保护监测
中心(UNEP-wcmc)合作进行的生物多样性价值的比较分析。数据分析的主要结果是在评
估任务期间和过程的其他阶段与缔约国进行对话的主题。
(ii) External Review. The nomination is sent for desk review to independent experts
knowledgeable about the property and/or the values that are the subject of the nomination, who are
primarily members of IUCN's specialist Commissions and networks, or expert members of partner
organisations of IUCN. The documents used to guide IUCN desk reviews are publicly available on the
IUCN website: www.iucn.org/worldheritage.
外部检讨。提名将送交了解提名所涉财产和/或价值的独立专家进行案头审查，这些专家主
要是自然保护联盟专家委员会和网络的成员，或自然保护联盟伙伴组织的专家成员。
用 于 指 导 IUCN 桌 面 审 查 的 文 件 可 在 IUCN 网 站 上 公 开 获 取 :
www.IUCN.org/worldheritage。
(iii) Evaluation mission to the property. One or two appropriately qualified IUCN experts visit
each nominated property to clarify details about the area, to evaluate site management and to discuss the
nomination with relevant authorities and stakeholders. IUCN experts, selected for their global perspective
on conservation and natural history as well as their knowledge of the Convention, are usually experienced
members of the IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas. (This field inspection is undertaken jointly
with ICOMOS in certain situations - see Part C below). The format of IUCN field evaluation mission
reports is publicly available on the IUCN website: www.iucn.org/worldheritage.
评估任务的财产。一至两名具有适当资格的自然保护联盟专家访问每个被提名的物业，以
澄清该地区的细节，评价场地管理，并与有关当局和利益攸关方讨论提名事宜。自然
保护联盟的专家通常是自然保护联盟世界保护区委员会的经验丰富的成员，他们是根
据自己对保护和自然历史的全球观点以及对《公约》的了解而选出的。(在某些情况下，
这种实地考察是与 ICOMOS 联合进行的——见下文 c 部分)。IUCN 实地评估任务报
告的格式在 IUCN 网站上公开提供: www.IUCN.org/worldheritage。
(iv) Other sources of information. IUCN also consults additional literature and may receive
comments from local NGOs, communities, indigenous peoples and other interested parties in the nomination.
Where relevant IUCN will also coordinate with other international conservation instruments such as the
Ramsar Convention, the Man and Biosphere Programme and the Global Geoparks Network, and will consult
with universities and research institutes as appropriate.
其他资料来源。世界自然保护联盟还参考了其他文献，并可能收到来自当地非政府组织、社区、
原住民和其他对提名感兴趣的团体的意见。自然保护联盟还将在哪些方面与其他国际保护
文书协调，如《拉姆萨尔公约》、人与生物圈方案和全球地质公园网络，并酌情与大学和
研究机构协商。
(v) IUCN World Heritage Panel Review. The IUCN World Heritage Panel is established by the
Director General of IUCN to provide high quality and independent technical and scientific advice to IUCN on
its work as an Advisory Body to the World Heritage Committee and strategic advice to IUCN’s work on World
Heritage throughout the IUCN Programme. Specific Tasks of the World Heritage Panel are to conduct a
rigorous evaluation of all nominations of natural and mixed properties to the World Heritage List, leading to a
panel recommendation on the IUCN position in relation to each new nomination, in line with the requirements
established in the Operational Guidelines of the World Heritage Convention. The Panel also provides comment
where relevant to ICOMOS in relation to nominations of cultural landscapes to the World Heritage List. The
Panel normally meets at least twice in the evaluation process, once in December (year 1) and a second meeting
in March/April (year 2).
世界自然保护联盟世界遗产小组审查。世界自然保护联盟世界遗产小组由自然保护联盟总干事
设立，目的是就自然保护联盟作为世界遗产委员会咨询机构的工作向其提供高质量和独立
的技术和科学咨询意见，并就自然保护联盟在整个世界自然保护联盟方案中关于世界遗产
的工作提供战略咨询意见。世界遗产小组的具体任务是根据《世界遗产公约业务准则》规
定的要求，对列入世界遗产名录的所有自然和混合财产提名进行严格评价，从而就自然保
护联盟在每个新提名方面的立场提出小组建议。小组亦就世界文化遗产名录内的文化景观
提名，就与 ICOMOS 有关的事宜提供意见。评审小组通常在评审过程中至少举行两次会
议，一次在 12 月(第一年) ，第二次在 3 月/4 月(第二年)。
The members of the Panel comprise senior IUCN staff, IUCN Commission members and
external experts selected for their high level of experience and recognised leading expertise and
knowledge relevant to IUCN’s work on World Heritage, including a balance of particular
thematic and/or regional perspectives. It includes some experts who have past experience as
members of State Party delegations, but are not current serving members of the World Heritage
Committee. These experts will serve in a personal and professional capacity. The IUCN World
Heritage Panel reviews all field evaluation reports (and normally hears direct feedback from the
mission team), reviewers' comments, the UNEP-WCMC and other analyses and all other
background material before finalising the text of the IUCN evaluation report for each nominated
property. The membership, terms of reference and working methods of the IUCN World
专家小组成员包括自然保护联盟的高级工作人员、自然保护联盟委员会成员和外部专家，
这些专家是根据自然保护联盟在世界遗产方面的工作，包括某些专题和/或区域观点的平
衡而挑选的，他们的经验和知识都得到了认可。它包括一些专家，他们过去作为缔约国代
表团成员具有经验，但不是目前世界遗产委员会的现任成员。这些专家将以个人和专业的
身份服务。世界自然保护联盟世界遗产小组审查所有实地评价报告(通常听取特派团小组
的直接反馈意见)、审查员的意见、环境署-世界遗产监测中心和其他分析以及所有其他背
景材料，然后最后确定世界自然保护联盟对每个提名财产的评价报告案文。IUCN 世界的
成员，职权范围和工作方法
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 121
实施世界遗产公约的操作指南 121
Procedures of the Advisory Bodies for Preliminary Assessments and the Evaluation of Nominations Annex 6
初步评审及提名评审咨询组织的程序附件 6
Heritage Panel are publicly available on the IUCN website, and are provided to the World
Heritage Committee.
文物小组已上载于世界自然保护联盟网站，供公众查阅，并提供予世界遗产委员会。
Each evaluation report presents a concise summary of the proposed Outstanding Universal
Value of the property nominated, a global comparative analysis with other similar sites
(including both World Heritage properties and other protected areas) and a review of
integrity and management issues. It concludes with the assessment of the applicability of the
criteria, and a clear recommendation to the World Heritage Committee. The names of all
experts involved in the evaluation process are included in the final evaluation report, except
in the case of reviewers who have provided confidential reviews.
每份评价报告简要概述提名财产的拟议未决普遍价值，与其他类似地点(包括世界遗产
财产和其他保护区)进行全球比较分析，并审查完整性和管理问题。报告最后评估了标
准的适用性，并向世界遗产委员会提出了明确的建议。参与评估过程的所有专家的姓
名都包括在最终评估报告中，除了提供保密审查的审查人员。
IUCN undertakes dialogue with the nominating States Party/ies at all stages of the
nomination process. IUCN will use its best endeavours to allocate its available resources
equitably, efficiently and effectively, to maximise the opportunities for dialogue with all
nominating States Parties. Dialogue starts early in the evaluation process and intensifies after
the meeting of the IUCN World Heritage Panel in December, and includes the following:
自然保护联盟在提名过程的所有阶段与提名缔约国进行对话。世界自然保护联盟将尽
最大努力公平、高效和有效地分配其可用资源，以最大限度地提高与所有提名缔约国
对话的机会。对话在评估过程的早期开始，并在 12 月的世界自然保护联盟世界遗产
小组会议之后加强，包括以下内容:
i) Prior to the evaluation mission, IUCN may request additional information on
questions in the nomination document that require clarification, and will always contact the State Party to
prepare for the evaluation mission.
在进行评估之前，自然保护联盟可要求就提名文件中需要澄清的问题提供补充资料，
并将始终与缔约国联系，为评估工作做准备。
ii) During the evaluation mission the IUCN mission team is able to undertake in-depth
discussions on site with representatives of the State Party and with stakeholders.
在评估任务期间，世界自然保护联盟使命团队能够在现场与缔约国代表和利益相关者
进行深入讨论。
iii) After the evaluation mission, IUCN may discuss issues that have been identified by
the mission team, and request further information from the State Party as required.
在评估团之后，自然保护联盟可以讨论评估团小组确定的问题，并视需要要求缔约国
提供进一步资料。
iv) After IUCN’s first World Heritage Panel meeting, normally held in December, IUCN
will discuss issues raised by the Panel, and request further information from the State Party as required. A
short interim report outlining the status, and any issues relevant to
在自然保护联盟通常于 12 月举行的第一次世界遗产专家小组会议之后，自然保护联盟
将讨论专家小组提出的问题，并根据需要要求缔约国提供进一步资料。一份简
短的中期报告概述了现状，以及任何与
the evaluation, and detailing any requests for supplementary information, in one of the
two working languages of the Convention, is sent to the nominating State Party/ies, a
n d copied t o t h e World Heritage Centre, for transmission to the Chairperson of the
World Heritage Committee. Dialogue and consultation takes place either through
teleconference and/or face-to-face meetings, as mutually agreed.
以《公约》两种工作语文之一提出的评价和详细要求提供补充资料的请求，将
送交提名缔约国和世界遗产中心，以便转交世界遗产委员会主席。对话和磋商
通过电话会议和/或面对面会议进行，双方同意。
IUCN takes into account in its evaluation all information that is officially submitted by the State
Party in writing to the World Heritage Centre by the specified deadline (see paragraph 148 of the
Operational Guidelines). However, at all of the above stages any stakeholder in the nomination
is also at liberty to contact IUCN to provide information if they wish.
自然保护联盟在其评价中考虑到缔约国在规定期限之前正式书面提交世界遗产中心的所有
资料(见业务准则第 148 段)。然而，在上述所有阶段，提名中的任何利益相关者也可以自
由地联系自然保护联盟提供信息，如果他们愿意的话。
IUCN also always considers fully all past decisions of the World Heritage Committee relevant to
the nomination, such as in cases of nominations that have been previously referred or deferred by
the Committee, or where the Committee has taken any position in relation to issues of policy.
自然保护联盟还始终充分考虑世界遗产委员会过去与提名有关的所有决定，例如委员会以
前提交或推迟的提名，或委员会对政策问题采取任何立场的情况。
In the case of renominations, extensions and boundary modifications to an existing World
Heritage property, IUCN also considers all matters regarding the state of conservation of that
property that have been previously reported to the World Heritage Committee. IUCN may also
consider bringing to the attention of the Committee, through the state of conservation reporting
process, any significant matters regarding the state of conservation of that property, when such
are identified for the first time during the evaluation process.
在重新提名、扩建和修改现有世界遗产财产的情况下，自然保护联盟还审议以前向世界
遗产委员会报告的有关该财产保护状况的所有事项。自然保护联盟还可考虑通过养护状
况报告程序，提请委员会注意在评价过程中首次查明的与该财产的养护状况有关的任何
重大事项。
Biogeographic classification systems as a basis for comparison
作为比较基础的生物地理分类系统
2. In the evaluations, IUCN uses biogeographic classification systems such as Udvardy’s “Biogeographical
Provinces of the World” (1975) and the more recent terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecoregions of the world
as a central element of its approach to the global comparative analysis. These systems provide an
在评价中，自然保护联盟使用生物地理分类系统，例如 Udvardy 的”世界生物地理省份”(1975 年)和
世界上最近的陆地、淡水和海洋生态区，作为其全球比较分析方法的一个核心要素。这些系统
提供了
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 122
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 122
Procedures of the Advisory Bodies for Preliminary Assessments and the Evaluation of Nominations Annex 6
初步评审及提名评审咨询组织的程序附件 6
objective means of comparing nominated properties with sites of similar climatic and ecological
conditions.
客观的方法比较指定的特性与类似的气候和生态条件的地点。
3. It is stressed, however, that these biogeographical classification systems are used as a measure for
comparison only and do not imply that World Heritage properties are to be selected solely on this basis, nor
that the representation of all such classification systems is the basis for the selection process. The guiding
principle is that World Heritage properties must be of Outstanding Universal Value.
然而，有人强调，这些生物地理分类系统只是用来作为比较的一种手段，并不意味着世界遗产的财产
只能在这个基础上选择，也不意味着所有这些分类系统的代表性是选择过程的基础。指导原则
是世界遗产必须具有突出的普遍价值。
Systems to identify priority areas for conservation
确定优先保护区的系统
4. IUCN also uses systems which identify priority areas for conservation such as the World Wide
Fund for Nature's (WWF) Global 200 Ecoregions, WWF/IUCN's Centres of Plant Diversity,
Conservation International's Biodiversity Hotspots and High-Biodiversity Wilderness Areas, Birdlife
International's Endemic Bird Areas and Important Bird Areas, and other Key Biodiversity Areas such as
Alliance for Zero Extinction sites. These systems provide additional information on the significance of
the nominated properties for biodiversity conservation; however it is not assumed that all such sites
should be included on the World Heritage List. The guiding principle is that World Heritage properties
must be of Outstanding Universal Value.
自然保护联盟还使用确定优先保护区的系统，例如世界自然基金会全球 200 个生态区、世界自然
基金会/自然保护联盟的植物多样性中心、国际保护组织的生物多样性热点和高生物多样性
荒野地区、国际鸟类保护组织的地方鸟类保护区和重要鸟类保护区，以及其他关键的生物多
样性保护区，例如零灭绝保护区联盟。这些系统提供了关于指定地点对保护生物多样性的重
要性的补充信息; 然而，并不假定所有这些地点都应列入世界遗产名录。指导原则是世界遗
产必须具有突出的普遍价值。
Systems to evaluate properties for earth science value
评估地球科学价值特性的系统
5. In evaluating properties which have been nominated for their geological value, IUCN consults with
a range of specialised organisations such as the UNESCO Earth Sciences Division, International
Association of Geomorphologists, the International Union of Speleology and the International Union of
Geological Sciences (IUGS).
在评估被提名的地质价值时，世界自然保护联盟咨询了一系列专门组织，如教科文组织地球科学
部、国际地貌学家协会、国际洞穴学联合会和国际地质科学联盟。
Additional reference publications used in the evaluation process
评价过程中使用的其他参考出版物
6. The evaluation process also includes consideration of key reference publications on the world's
protected areas published by IUCN and a range of international conservation organisations. These
documents together provide system-wide overviews which allow comparison of the conservation
importance of protected areas throughout the world. IUCN has also undertaken a range of thematic
studies to identify gaps in natural World Heritage coverage and properties of World Heritage potential.
These can be viewed on the IUCN website at www.iucn.org/worldheritage.
评估过程还包括考虑世界自然保护联盟和一系列国际自然保护组织出版的关于世界保护区的主要
参考出版物。这些文件一起提供了全系统的概述，允许比较世界各地保护区的保护重要性。
世界自然保护联盟还进行了一系列的主题研究，以确定自然世界遗产覆盖面和世界遗产潜力
属性的差距。这些可以在 IUCN 网站上查看 www.IUCN. org/worldheritage。
IUCN also draws upon references specific to the nominated properties in order to gain insights into
site values and conservation issues.
自然保护联盟还利用提名物业的具体参考资料，以便深入了解场地价值和保护问题。
Evaluation of Cultural Landscapes (see also paragraphs 47-47ter)
文化景观的评估(另见第 47-47 段之三)
7. IUCN has an interest in many cultural properties, especially those nominated as cultural
landscapes. For that reason, it will on occasion participate in joint field inspections to nominated cultural
landscapes with ICOMOS (see Part D below).
世界自然保护联盟对许多文化财产感兴趣，特别是那些被提名为文化景观的财产。由于这个原因，
它有时会参与 ICOMOS 对提名的文化景观的联合实地考察(见下文 d 部分)。
8. In accordance with the natural qualities of certain cultural landscapes, IUCN's evaluation is
concerned with the following factors:
根据某些文化景观的自然特质，世界自然保护联盟的评估涉及以下因素:
(i) Conservation of natural and semi-natural systems, and of wild species of fauna and flora
自然和半自然系统以及野生动植物物种的保护
(ii) Conservation of biodiversity within sustainable use systems (farming, traditional fisheries,
forestry);
保护可持续利用系统内的生物多样性(农业，传统渔业，林业) ;
(iii) Sustainable land and water use;
可持续的土地和水资源利用;
(iv) Enhancement of scenic beauty;
增强景观美感;
(v) Ex-situ collections, such as botanic gardens or arboreta;
异地采集，如植物园或植物园;
(vi) Outstanding examples of humanity's inter-relationship with nature;
人类与自然相互关系的杰出例子;
(vii) Historically significant discoveries
具有重大历史意义的发现
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 123
实施世界遗产公约的操作指南 123

D. ADVISORY BODY COLLABORATION Nominations of mixed properties
混合物业的提名
1. Properties that are nominated under both natural and cultural criteria entail a joint IUCN and
ICOMOS mission to the nominated property. Following the mission, IUCN and ICOMOS prepare
separate evaluation reports of the property under the relevant criteria (see above), and harmonise and
coordinate their evaluations to the extent possible.
在自然和文化标准下被提名的物业需要一个 IUCN 和 ICOMOS 的联合使命来提名物业。执行任务
后，自然保护联盟和国际保护监测组织根据有关标准分别编写财产评价报告(见上文) ，并尽
可能协调和协调它们的评价。
Cultural Landscapes
文化景观
2. Properties nominated as Cultural Landscapes are evaluated by ICOMOS under criteria (i) - (vi) (see
Paragraph 77 of the Operational Guidelines). IUCN may provide advice when relevant on the natural
values and the conservation and management of the nominated property, and addresses any questions that
are raised by ICOMOS. In some cases, a joint mission is required.
被提名为文化景观的物业由 ICOMOS 根据标准(i)-(vi)进行评估(见运营指南第 77 段)。世界自然保
护联盟(IUCN)可以就提名物业的自然价值、保护和管理提供相关建议，并解决 ICOMOS 提
出的任何问题。在某些情况下，需要一个联合使命。
Linkages between nature and culture
自然与文化的联系
3.
As most properties nominated to the World Heritage List include aspects of management related to
the
由于大多数被列入世界遗产名录的物业都包括与管理相关的方面
interaction of nature and culture, IUCN and ICOMOS, to the extent possible, discuss any such
自然和文化的相互作用，世界自然保护联盟和 ICOMOS，尽可能讨论任何这样的
interactions during their evaluation processes.
评估过程中的相互作用。

This Annex presents an outline of the Periodic Reporting questionnaire. The full questionnaire can
