C. THE IUCN PROCEDURE FOR THE EVALUATION OF NATURAL PROPERTIES
自然保护联盟自然资源评估程序
1. In carrying out its evaluation of nominations of natural properties, IUCN (the International Union
for Conservation of Nature) is guided by the Operational Guidelines (see Paragraph 148). The evaluation
process (see Figure 2) involves five elements:
世界自然保护联盟(国际自然保护联盟)在对自然财产提名进行评估时，遵循业务准则(见第 148 段)。
评估过程(见图 2)包括五个要素:
(i) Data Assembly. Following receipt of the nomination dossier from the World Heritage Centre, a
standardised analysis is compiled on the property using the World Database on Protected Areas and other
IUCN global databases and thematic studies. This may include comparative analyses on biodiversity values
undertaken in partnership with the UNEP World Conservation Monitoring Centre (UNEP-WCMC). Key
findings of data analysis are the subject of dialogue with the State Party during the evaluation mission, and at
other stages of the process.
数据汇编。在收到世界遗产中心的提名档案后，利用世界保护区数据库和世界自然保护联盟其
他全球数据库和专题研究对该财产进行了标准化分析。这可能包括与环境署世界保护监测
中心(UNEP-wcmc)合作进行的生物多样性价值的比较分析。数据分析的主要结果是在评
估任务期间和过程的其他阶段与缔约国进行对话的主题。
(ii) External Review. The nomination is sent for desk review to independent experts
knowledgeable about the property and/or the values that are the subject of the nomination, who are
primarily members of IUCN's specialist Commissions and networks, or expert members of partner
organisations of IUCN. The documents used to guide IUCN desk reviews are publicly available on the
IUCN website: www.iucn.org/worldheritage.
外部检讨。提名将送交了解提名所涉财产和/或价值的独立专家进行案头审查，这些专家主
要是自然保护联盟专家委员会和网络的成员，或自然保护联盟伙伴组织的专家成员。
用 于 指 导 IUCN 桌 面 审 查 的 文 件 可 在 IUCN 网 站 上 公 开 获 取 :
www.IUCN.org/worldheritage。
(iii) Evaluation mission to the property. One or two appropriately qualified IUCN experts visit
each nominated property to clarify details about the area, to evaluate site management and to discuss the
nomination with relevant authorities and stakeholders. IUCN experts, selected for their global perspective
on conservation and natural history as well as their knowledge of the Convention, are usually experienced
members of the IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas. (This field inspection is undertaken jointly
with ICOMOS in certain situations - see Part C below). The format of IUCN field evaluation mission
reports is publicly available on the IUCN website: www.iucn.org/worldheritage.
评估任务的财产。一至两名具有适当资格的自然保护联盟专家访问每个被提名的物业，以
澄清该地区的细节，评价场地管理，并与有关当局和利益攸关方讨论提名事宜。自然
保护联盟的专家通常是自然保护联盟世界保护区委员会的经验丰富的成员，他们是根
据自己对保护和自然历史的全球观点以及对《公约》的了解而选出的。(在某些情况下，
这种实地考察是与 ICOMOS 联合进行的——见下文 c 部分)。IUCN 实地评估任务报
告的格式在 IUCN 网站上公开提供: www.IUCN.org/worldheritage。
(iv) Other sources of information. IUCN also consults additional literature and may receive
comments from local NGOs, communities, indigenous peoples and other interested parties in the nomination.
Where relevant IUCN will also coordinate with other international conservation instruments such as the
Ramsar Convention, the Man and Biosphere Programme and the Global Geoparks Network, and will consult
with universities and research institutes as appropriate.
其他资料来源。世界自然保护联盟还参考了其他文献，并可能收到来自当地非政府组织、社区、
原住民和其他对提名感兴趣的团体的意见。自然保护联盟还将在哪些方面与其他国际保护
文书协调，如《拉姆萨尔公约》、人与生物圈方案和全球地质公园网络，并酌情与大学和
研究机构协商。
(v) IUCN World Heritage Panel Review. The IUCN World Heritage Panel is established by the
Director General of IUCN to provide high quality and independent technical and scientific advice to IUCN on
its work as an Advisory Body to the World Heritage Committee and strategic advice to IUCN’s work on World
Heritage throughout the IUCN Programme. Specific Tasks of the World Heritage Panel are to conduct a
rigorous evaluation of all nominations of natural and mixed properties to the World Heritage List, leading to a
panel recommendation on the IUCN position in relation to each new nomination, in line with the requirements
established in the Operational Guidelines of the World Heritage Convention. The Panel also provides comment
where relevant to ICOMOS in relation to nominations of cultural landscapes to the World Heritage List. The
Panel normally meets at least twice in the evaluation process, once in December (year 1) and a second meeting
in March/April (year 2).
世界自然保护联盟世界遗产小组审查。世界自然保护联盟世界遗产小组由自然保护联盟总干事
设立，目的是就自然保护联盟作为世界遗产委员会咨询机构的工作向其提供高质量和独立
的技术和科学咨询意见，并就自然保护联盟在整个世界自然保护联盟方案中关于世界遗产
的工作提供战略咨询意见。世界遗产小组的具体任务是根据《世界遗产公约业务准则》规
定的要求，对列入世界遗产名录的所有自然和混合财产提名进行严格评价，从而就自然保
护联盟在每个新提名方面的立场提出小组建议。小组亦就世界文化遗产名录内的文化景观
提名，就与 ICOMOS 有关的事宜提供意见。评审小组通常在评审过程中至少举行两次会
议，一次在 12 月(第一年) ，第二次在 3 月/4 月(第二年)。
The members of the Panel comprise senior IUCN staff, IUCN Commission members and
external experts selected for their high level of experience and recognised leading expertise and
knowledge relevant to IUCN’s work on World Heritage, including a balance of particular
thematic and/or regional perspectives. It includes some experts who have past experience as
members of State Party delegations, but are not current serving members of the World Heritage
Committee. These experts will serve in a personal and professional capacity. The IUCN World
Heritage Panel reviews all field evaluation reports (and normally hears direct feedback from the
mission team), reviewers' comments, the UNEP-WCMC and other analyses and all other
background material before finalising the text of the IUCN evaluation report for each nominated
property. The membership, terms of reference and working methods of the IUCN World
专家小组成员包括自然保护联盟的高级工作人员、自然保护联盟委员会成员和外部专家，

的直接反馈意见)、审查员的意见、环境署-世界遗产监测中心和其他分析以及所有其他背
景材料，然后最后确定世界自然保护联盟对每个提名财产的评价报告案文。IUCN 世界的

Heritage Panel are publicly available on the IUCN website, and are provided to the World

文物小组已上载于世界自然保护联盟网站，供公众查阅，并提供予世界遗产委员会。
Each evaluation report presents a concise summary of the proposed Outstanding Universal
Value of the property nominated, a global comparative analysis with other similar sites
(including both World Heritage properties and other protected areas) and a review of
integrity and management issues. It concludes with the assessment of the applicability of the
criteria, and a clear recommendation to the World Heritage Committee. The names of all
experts involved in the evaluation process are included in the final evaluation report, except
in the case of reviewers who have provided confidential reviews.
每份评价报告简要概述提名财产的拟议未决普遍价值，与其他类似地点(包括世界遗产
财产和其他保护区)进行全球比较分析，并审查完整性和管理问题。报告最后评估了标
准的适用性，并向世界遗产委员会提出了明确的建议。参与评估过程的所有专家的姓
名都包括在最终评估报告中，除了提供保密审查的审查人员。
IUCN undertakes dialogue with the nominating States Party/ies at all stages of the
nomination process. IUCN will use its best endeavours to allocate its available resources
equitably, efficiently and effectively, to maximise the opportunities for dialogue with all
nominating States Parties. Dialogue starts early in the evaluation process and intensifies after
the meeting of the IUCN World Heritage Panel in December, and includes the following:
自然保护联盟在提名过程的所有阶段与提名缔约国进行对话。世界自然保护联盟将尽
最大努力公平、高效和有效地分配其可用资源，以最大限度地提高与所有提名缔约国
对话的机会。对话在评估过程的早期开始，并在 12 月的世界自然保护联盟世界遗产
小组会议之后加强，包括以下内容:
i) Prior to the evaluation mission, IUCN may request additional information on
questions in the nomination document that require clarification, and will always contact the State Party to
prepare for the evaluation mission.
在进行评估之前，自然保护联盟可要求就提名文件中需要澄清的问题提供补充资料，
并将始终与缔约国联系，为评估工作做准备。
ii) During the evaluation mission the IUCN mission team is able to undertake in-depth
discussions on site with representatives of the State Party and with stakeholders.
在评估任务期间，世界自然保护联盟使命团队能够在现场与缔约国代表和利益相关者
进行深入讨论。
iii) After the evaluation mission, IUCN may discuss issues that have been identified by
the mission team, and request further information from the State Party as required.
在评估团之后，自然保护联盟可以讨论评估团小组确定的问题，并视需要要求缔约国
提供进一步资料。
iv) After IUCN’s first World Heritage Panel meeting, normally held in December, IUCN
will discuss issues raised by the Panel, and request further information from the State Party as required. A
short interim report outlining the status, and any issues relevant to
在自然保护联盟通常于 12 月举行的第一次世界遗产专家小组会议之后，自然保护联盟
将讨论专家小组提出的问题，并根据需要要求缔约国提供进一步资料。一份简
短的中期报告概述了现状，以及任何与
the evaluation, and detailing any requests for supplementary information, in one of the
two working languages of the Convention, is sent to the nominating State Party/ies, a
n d copied t o t h e World Heritage Centre, for transmission to the Chairperson of the
World Heritage Committee. Dialogue and consultation takes place either through
teleconference and/or face-to-face meetings, as mutually agreed.
以《公约》两种工作语文之一提出的评价和详细要求提供补充资料的请求，将
送交提名缔约国和世界遗产中心，以便转交世界遗产委员会主席。对话和磋商
通过电话会议和/或面对面会议进行，双方同意。
IUCN takes into account in its evaluation all information that is officially submitted by the State
Party in writing to the World Heritage Centre by the specified deadline (see paragraph 148 of the
Operational Guidelines). However, at all of the above stages any stakeholder in the nomination
is also at liberty to contact IUCN to provide information if they wish.
自然保护联盟在其评价中考虑到缔约国在规定期限之前正式书面提交世界遗产中心的所有
资料(见业务准则第 148 段)。然而，在上述所有阶段，提名中的任何利益相关者也可以自
由地联系自然保护联盟提供信息，如果他们愿意的话。
IUCN also always considers fully all past decisions of the World Heritage Committee relevant to
the nomination, such as in cases of nominations that have been previously referred or deferred by
the Committee, or where the Committee has taken any position in relation to issues of policy.
自然保护联盟还始终充分考虑世界遗产委员会过去与提名有关的所有决定，例如委员会以
前提交或推迟的提名，或委员会对政策问题采取任何立场的情况。
In the case of renominations, extensions and boundary modifications to an existing World
Heritage property, IUCN also considers all matters regarding the state of conservation of that
property that have been previously reported to the World Heritage Committee. IUCN may also
consider bringing to the attention of the Committee, through the state of conservation reporting
process, any significant matters regarding the state of conservation of that property, when such
are identified for the first time during the evaluation process.
在重新提名、扩建和修改现有世界遗产财产的情况下，自然保护联盟还审议以前向世界
遗产委员会报告的有关该财产保护状况的所有事项。自然保护联盟还可考虑通过养护状
况报告程序，提请委员会注意在评价过程中首次查明的与该财产的养护状况有关的任何
重大事项。
Biogeographic classification systems as a basis for comparison
作为比较基础的生物地理分类系统
2. In the evaluations, IUCN uses biogeographic classification systems such as Udvardy’s “Biogeographical
Provinces of the World” (1975) and the more recent terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecoregions of the world
as a central element of its approach to the global comparative analysis. These systems provide an
在评价中，自然保护联盟使用生物地理分类系统，例如 Udvardy 的”世界生物地理省份”(1975 年)和
世界上最近的陆地、淡水和海洋生态区，作为其全球比较分析方法的一个核心要素。这些系统
提供了
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 122
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 122
Procedures of the Advisory Bodies for Preliminary Assessments and the Evaluation of Nominations Annex 6
初步评审及提名评审咨询组织的程序附件 6
objective means of comparing nominated properties with sites of similar climatic and ecological
conditions.
客观的方法比较指定的特性与类似的气候和生态条件的地点。
3. It is stressed, however, that these biogeographical classification systems are used as a measure for
comparison only and do not imply that World Heritage properties are to be selected solely on this basis, nor
that the representation of all such classification systems is the basis for the selection process. The guiding
principle is that World Heritage properties must be of Outstanding Universal Value.
然而，有人强调，这些生物地理分类系统只是用来作为比较的一种手段，并不意味着世界遗产的财产
只能在这个基础上选择，也不意味着所有这些分类系统的代表性是选择过程的基础。指导原则
是世界遗产必须具有突出的普遍价值。
Systems to identify priority areas for conservation
确定优先保护区的系统
4. IUCN also uses systems which identify priority areas for conservation such as the World Wide
Fund for Nature's (WWF) Global 200 Ecoregions, WWF/IUCN's Centres of Plant Diversity,
Conservation International's Biodiversity Hotspots and High-Biodiversity Wilderness Areas, Birdlife
International's Endemic Bird Areas and Important Bird Areas, and other Key Biodiversity Areas such as
Alliance for Zero Extinction sites. These systems provide additional information on the significance of
the nominated properties for biodiversity conservation; however it is not assumed that all such sites
should be included on the World Heritage List. The guiding principle is that World Heritage properties
must be of Outstanding Universal Value.
自然保护联盟还使用确定优先保护区的系统，例如世界自然基金会全球 200 个生态区、世界自然
基金会/自然保护联盟的植物多样性中心、国际保护组织的生物多样性热点和高生物多样性
荒野地区、国际鸟类保护组织的地方鸟类保护区和重要鸟类保护区，以及其他关键的生物多
样性保护区，例如零灭绝保护区联盟。这些系统提供了关于指定地点对保护生物多样性的重
要性的补充信息; 然而，并不假定所有这些地点都应列入世界遗产名录。指导原则是世界遗
产必须具有突出的普遍价值。
Systems to evaluate properties for earth science value
评估地球科学价值特性的系统
5. In evaluating properties which have been nominated for their geological value, IUCN consults with
a range of specialised organisations such as the UNESCO Earth Sciences Division, International
Association of Geomorphologists, the International Union of Speleology and the International Union of
Geological Sciences (IUGS).
在评估被提名的地质价值时，世界自然保护联盟咨询了一系列专门组织，如教科文组织地球科学
部、国际地貌学家协会、国际洞穴学联合会和国际地质科学联盟。
Additional reference publications used in the evaluation process
评价过程中使用的其他参考出版物
6. The evaluation process also includes consideration of key reference publications on the world's
protected areas published by IUCN and a range of international conservation organisations. These
documents together provide system-wide overviews which allow comparison of the conservation
importance of protected areas throughout the world. IUCN has also undertaken a range of thematic
studies to identify gaps in natural World Heritage coverage and properties of World Heritage potential.
These can be viewed on the IUCN website at www.iucn.org/worldheritage.
评估过程还包括考虑世界自然保护联盟和一系列国际自然保护组织出版的关于世界保护区的主要
参考出版物。这些文件一起提供了全系统的概述，允许比较世界各地保护区的保护重要性。
世界自然保护联盟还进行了一系列的主题研究，以确定自然世界遗产覆盖面和世界遗产潜力
属性的差距。这些可以在 IUCN 网站上查看 www.IUCN. org/worldheritage。
IUCN also draws upon references specific to the nominated properties in order to gain insights into
site values and conservation issues.
自然保护联盟还利用提名物业的具体参考资料，以便深入了解场地价值和保护问题。
Evaluation of Cultural Landscapes (see also paragraphs 47-47ter)
文化景观的评估(另见第 47-47 段之三)
7. IUCN has an interest in many cultural properties, especially those nominated as cultural
landscapes. For that reason, it will on occasion participate in joint field inspections to nominated cultural
landscapes with ICOMOS (see Part D below).
世界自然保护联盟对许多文化财产感兴趣，特别是那些被提名为文化景观的财产。由于这个原因，
它有时会参与 ICOMOS 对提名的文化景观的联合实地考察(见下文 d 部分)。
8. In accordance with the natural qualities of certain cultural landscapes, IUCN's evaluation is
concerned with the following factors:
根据某些文化景观的自然特质，世界自然保护联盟的评估涉及以下因素:
(i) Conservation of natural and semi-natural systems, and of wild species of fauna and flora
自然和半自然系统以及野生动植物物种的保护
(ii) Conservation of biodiversity within sustainable use systems (farming, traditional fisheries,
forestry);
保护可持续利用系统内的生物多样性(农业，传统渔业，林业) ;
(iii) Sustainable land and water use;
可持续的土地和水资源利用;
(iv) Enhancement of scenic beauty;
增强景观美感;
(v) Ex-situ collections, such as botanic gardens or arboreta;
异地采集，如植物园或植物园;
(vi) Outstanding examples of humanity's inter-relationship with nature;
人类与自然相互关系的杰出例子;
(vii) Historically significant discoveries
具有重大历史意义的发现

D. ADVISORY BODY COLLABORATION Nominations of mixed properties
混合物业的提名
1. Properties that are nominated under both natural and cultural criteria entail a joint IUCN and
ICOMOS mission to the nominated property. Following the mission, IUCN and ICOMOS prepare
separate evaluation reports of the property under the relevant criteria (see above), and harmonise and
coordinate their evaluations to the extent possible.
在自然和文化标准下被提名的物业需要一个 IUCN 和 ICOMOS 的联合使命来提名物业。执行任务
后，自然保护联盟和国际保护监测组织根据有关标准分别编写财产评价报告(见上文) ，并尽
可能协调和协调它们的评价。
Cultural Landscapes
文化景观
2. Properties nominated as Cultural Landscapes are evaluated by ICOMOS under criteria (i) - (vi) (see
Paragraph 77 of the Operational Guidelines). IUCN may provide advice when relevant on the natural
values and the conservation and management of the nominated property, and addresses any questions that
are raised by ICOMOS. In some cases, a joint mission is required.
被提名为文化景观的物业由 ICOMOS 根据标准(i)-(vi)进行评估(见运营指南第 77 段)。世界自然保
护联盟(IUCN)可以就提名物业的自然价值、保护和管理提供相关建议，并解决 ICOMOS 提
出的任何问题。在某些情况下，需要一个联合使命。
Linkages between nature and culture
自然与文化的联系
3.
As most properties nominated to the World Heritage List include aspects of management related to
the
由于大多数被列入世界遗产名录的物业都包括与管理相关的方面
interaction of nature and culture, IUCN and ICOMOS, to the extent possible, discuss any such
自然和文化的相互作用，世界自然保护联盟和 ICOMOS，尽可能讨论任何这样的
interactions during their evaluation processes.
评估过程中的相互作用。

THE WORLD HERITAGE CONVENTION
世界遗产公约
This Annex presents an outline of the Periodic Reporting questionnaire. The full questionnaire can
be accessed at https://whc.unesco.org/en/periodicreporting/.
本附件概述了定期报告调查表。
General Requirements
一般要求
 Information should be as precise, specific and concise as possible. It should be quantified where
possible and fully referenced. Opportunities for comment are provided in each chapter.
信息应该尽可能准确、具体和简明。信息应尽可能量化，并充分参考。每一章都提供了评论的机
会。
 Expressions of opinion should be supported by reference to the authority on which they are made
and the verifiable facts which support them.
意见的表达应该参照权威和可证实的事实来支持。
SECTION I:APPLICATION OF THE WORLD HERITAGE CONVENTION BY THE STATE
PARTY
第一节: 缔约国适用《世界遗产公约》
Section I requests that the State Party provide information or validate existing information on the
legislative and administrative provisions which they have adopted and other actions which they have
taken for the application of this Convention, together with details of the experience acquired in this field
(Article 29.1 of the World Heritage Convention).
第一节请缔约国提供资料或核实现有资料，说明它们为适用本公约而通过的立法和行政规定以及
为适用本公约而采取的其他行动，并详细说明在这一领域取得的经验(《世界遗产公约》第 29.1
条)。
1. INTRODUCTION
1. 导言
Chapter 1 lists the name of the State Party and the year of ratification or acceptance of the Convention and
seeks information on the groups and institutions involved in the preparation of Section I of the report.
第 1 章列出了缔约国的名称以及批准或接受《公约》的年份，并要求提供关于参与编写报告第一节
的团体和机构的资料。
2. SYNERGIES WITH OTHER CONVENTIONS, PROGRAMMES AND RECOMMENDATIONS
FOR THE CONSERVATION OF THE NATURAL AND CULTURAL HERITAGE
与保护自然和文化遗产的其他公约、方案和建议的协同作用
Chapter 2 aims to gather information on existing and potential synergies between Multilateral
Environmental Agreements, as well as other UNESCO conventions, programmes, and
recommendations. The State Party is also invited to provide information on the extent to which it has
implemented relevant policies adopted by the World Heritage Committee.
第二章旨在收集关于多边环境协定以及其他联合国教科文组织公约、计划和建议之间现有和潜
在协同作用的信息。缔约国也被邀请提供其执行世界遗产委员会相关政策的程度的信息。
3. TENTATIVE LIST
3. 暂定名单
Chapter 3 aims to gather information on the process of preparing the tentative list, the tools and guidance
used, potential synergies with other conventions of properties on the tentative list as well as the
sustainability of the process in line with the World Heritage and Sustainable Development Policy (2015).
第三章旨在收集关于编制暂定名单的进程、所使用的工具和指南、与暂定名单上的其他财产公约的
潜在协同作用以及按照《世界遗产和可持续发展政策》(2015 年)这一进程的可持续性的信息。
4. NOMINATIONS
4. 提名
Chapter 4 aims to gather information on the process of nominating properties for inscription on the
World Heritage List, the tools and guidance used, as well as the sustainability of the process in line with
the World Heritage and Sustainable Development Policy (2015).
第四章旨在收集关于提名财产列入世界遗产名录的进程、所使用的工具和指南以及根据《世界遗
产和可持续发展政策》(2015 年)这一进程的可持续性的信息。
5. GENERAL POLICY DEVELOPMENT
5. 一般政策发展
Chapter 5 aims to gather information on the legal framework for the protection, conservation
and presentation of the cultural and/or natural heritage and its effectiveness.
第五章旨在收集关于保护、保存和展示文化和/或自然遗产的法律框架及其有效性的信
息。
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 128
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 128
Format for Periodic Reporting on the application of the World Heritage Convention Annex 7
关于《世界遗产公约》适用情况的定期报告格式
6. INVENTORIES/LISTS/REGISTERS OF CULTURAL AND NATURAL HERITAGE
6. 文化和自然遗产目录/清单/登记册
Chapter 6 aims to gather information on the status of inventories/lists/registers of cultural and
natural heritage of national significance and the processes used to compile them.
第六章旨在收集关于具有国家重要性的文化和自然遗产清单/清单/登记册的状况以及汇编
这些清单/清单/登记册的过程的资料。
7. STATUS OF SERVICES FOR PROTECTION, CONSERVATION AND PRESENTATION
7. 保护、养护和展示服务的状况
Chapter 7 aims to gather information on services within the territories of the State Party for the
identification, protection, conservation and presentation of the cultural and natural heritage and
on cooperation between the stakeholders involved.
第七章旨在收集关于缔约国境内为确定、保护、养护和展示文化和自然遗产提供的服务
以及有关利益攸关方之间合作的信息。
8. FINANCIAL STATUS AND HUMAN RESOURCES
8. 财务状况和人力资源
Chapter 8 aims to gather information on the availability and adequacy of financial resources for
the conservation and protection of cultural and natural heritage.
第八章旨在收集关于保护和保护文化和自然遗产的财政资源的可用性和充足性的信息。
9. CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT
9. 能力发展
Chapter 9 aims to gather information on capacity building in heritage conservation, protection,
presentation and management, in line with World Heritage Capacity Building Strategy (2011).
第九章旨在按照《世界遗产能力建设战略》(2011 年) ，收集有关文物保护、保护、介绍和管理
方面的能力建设资料。
10. POLICY AND RESOURCING OF WORLD HERITAGE PROPERTIES
10. 世界遗产财产的政策和资源
Chapter 10 aims to gather information on specific legislation, policies and measures for the
protection, conservation, presentation and management of World Heritage.
第十章旨在收集关于保护、保护、呈现和管理世界遗产的具体立法、政策和措施的信息。
11. INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION AND FUNDRAISING
11. 国际合作和筹资
Chapter 11 aims to gather information on the cooperation with other States Parties in the field of
cultural and natural heritage.
第十一章旨在收集与其他缔约国在文化和自然遗产领域合作的信息。
12. EDUCATION, INFORMATION AND AWARENESS BUILDING
12. 教育、信息和提高认识
Chapter 12 aims to gather information on steps taken to raise the awareness of decision-makers, property
owners and the general public, and in particular the youth, about the protection and conservation of
cultural and natural heritage.
第 12 章旨在收集资料，说明为提高决策者、财产所有人和一般公众，特别是青年对保护和保存
文化和自然遗产的认识而采取的步骤。
13. CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDED ACTIONS
13. 结论和建议的行动
Chapter 13 automatically generates the main conclusions under each of the items of Section I based on
the answers provided in the questionnaire. States Parties should also provide information about the
actions they have taken regarding their implementation of the World Heritage Convention.
第十三章根据调查问卷中提供的答案，自动生成第一部分每个项目下的主要结论。缔约国也应该
提供关于他们在执行世界遗产公约方面所采取的行动的信息。
14. GOOD PRACTICES IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE WORLD HERITAGE
CONVENTION
实施世界遗产公约的良好做法
Chapter 14 offers the opportunity to provide an example of a good practice in World Heritage
protection, identification, conservation or management implemented at national level.
第 14 章提供了一个在国家一级实施的世界遗产保护、鉴定、保护或管理的良好实践的例子。
15. ASSESSMENT OF THE PERIODIC REPORTING EXERCISE
15、定期报告评估
Chapter 15 assesses the format, content and process of the Periodic Reporting exercise, including the
degree to which it meets the objectives of Periodic Reporting, how the data generated is used and the
training and guidance available to respondents.
第 15 章评估了定期报告工作的形式、内容和过程，包括它在多大程度上达到了定期报告的目标，
所产生的数据如何使用，以及答复者可以得到的培训和指导。
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 129
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 129
Format for Periodic Reporting on the application of the World Heritage Convention Annex 7
关于《世界遗产公约》适用情况的定期报告格式
SECTION II:
第二部分:
STATE OF CONSERVATION OF SPECIFIC WORLD HERITAGE PROPERTIES
特定世界遗产保护状况
Section II gathers information on the implementation of the Convention at site-level and must be
completed for each individual World Heritage property. The preparation of this report should involve
those who are responsible for the day-to-day management of the property. For transboundary properties,
it is recommended that reports be prepared jointly by or with close collaboration between the agencies
concerned.
第二节收集关于在场地一级执行《公约》的资料，必须为每个世界遗产财产完成。这份报告的编
写应该包括那些负责物业日常管理的人员。对于跨界物业，建议由有关机构联合或紧密合作编制
报告。
1. WORLD HERITAGE PROPERTY DATA
1. 世界遗产数据
Chapter 1 requires that information be provided or existing information validated with regards to the
basic data of the property (name, year of inscription, geographic coordinates, maps, social media
presence), and also gathers information on the organizations or entities involved in the preparation of
Section I of the report.
第 1 章要求提供关于财产的基本数据(名称、登记年份、地理坐标、地图、社交媒体存在)的信
息或现有信息，并收集参与编写报告第一节的组织或实体的信息。
2. OTHER CONVENTIONS/PROGRAMMES UNDER WHICH THE WORLD HERITAGE
PROPERTY IS PROTECTED
保护世界遗产财产的其他公约/方案
Chapter 2 gathers information relating to synergies with other conventions and programmes (UNESCO
and others) relevant to the property and on the extent of cooperation and integration existing between
these conventions and programmes (where applicable).
第 2 章收集有关与与财产有关的其他公约和方案(教科文组织和其他方案)的协同作用以及这些公
约和方案之间现有合作和一体化程度(如适用)的资料。
3. STATEMENT OF OUTSTANDING UNIVERSAL VALUE AND DEFINING OF ATTRIBUTES
三、关于突出普遍价值和属性定义的陈述
Chapter 3 gathers information on the attributes of Outstanding Universal Value (OUV), their
current condition and the trend in that condition since the last cycle of Periodic Reporting.
第 3 章收集了关于杰出普遍价值(OUV)的属性、它们目前的状况以及自上一个定期报告周
期以来这种状况的趋势的信息。
4. FACTORS AFFECTING THE PROPERTY
影响财产的因素
Chapter 4 gathers information on the range of factors that are currently affecting or have strong potential
to affect the property, both positively and negatively.
第 4 章收集了关于目前正在影响或极有可能影响财产的各种因素的信息，包括正面和负面因素。
5. PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT OF THE PROPERTY
财产的保护和管理
Chapter 5 gathers information on practical issues of management, and the effectiveness of
protection, management and monitoring of the property and its Outstanding Universal Value.
第 5 章收集关于管理的实际问题，以及保护、管理和监测财产及其突出的普遍价值的有效
性的信息。
6. FINANCIAL AND HUMAN RESOURCES
6、财务和人力资源
Chapter 6 gathers information on the sources of funding available, the adequacy of budget for management
needs, as well as the availability of human resources and levels of capacity building at the property.
第 6 章收集关于可用资金来源、预算是否足以满足管理需要以及可用人力资源和房地产能力建设水平
的信息。
7. SCIENTIFIC STUDIES AND RESEARCH PROJECTS
科学研究和研究项目
Chapter 7 gathers information on the adequacy of available knowledge (both scientific and
traditional) regarding the values and attributes of the World Heritage property and the existence of
research programmes directed towards management needs and/or the improvement of the
understanding of the Outstanding Universal Value.
第 7 章收集关于世界遗产财产的价值和属性的现有知识(包括科学和传统知识)是否充分的信
息，以及是否存在针对管理需要的研究方案和(或)提高对突出的普遍价值的理解的信息。
8. EDUCATION, INFORMATION AND AWARENESS BUILDING
8. 教育、信息和意识建设
Chapter 8 gathers information on the existence and effectiveness of heritage education and awareness
programmes at the property as well as general services dedicated to education, information,
interpretation and awareness building.
第八章收集有关该物业的文物教育和提高认识方案的存在和成效的资料，以及专门用于教育、
信息、口译和提高认识的一般服务的资料。
9. VISITOR MANAGEMENT
9. 游客管理
Chapter 9 gathers information on tourism activities and visitor management at the property.
第九章收集有关旅游活动和旅客管理的资料。
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 130
实施《世界遗产公约》的运作指引 130
Format for Periodic Reporting on the application of the World Heritage Convention Annex 7
关于《世界遗产公约》适用情况的定期报告格式
10. MONITORING
10. 监察
Chapter 10 gathers information on the existence of monitoring programmes and indicators for the
property as well as on the implementation of property-related Committee Decisions (where applicable).
第 10 章收集有关财产的现有监测方案和指标以及有关财产的委员会决定(如适用)的执行情况的
资料。
11. IDENTIFICATION OF PRIORITY MANAGEMENT NEEDS
11. 确定优先管理需要
Chapter 11 automatically lists all the management needs requiring further action which have
been highlighted in this Section of the Periodic Report.
第 11 章自动列出了需要采取进一步行动的所有管理需要，定期报告本节强调了这些需
要。
12. SUMMARY AND CONCLUSIONS
总结和结论
Chapter 12 highlights the most important positive and negative factors (up to ten of each) which have
been highlighted in this Section of the Periodic Report.
第 12 章着重介绍了定期报告本节所强调的最重要的积极和消极因素(每个因素多达 10 个)。
13. IMPACT OF WORLD HERITAGE STATUS
世界遗产地位的影响
Chapter 13 gathers information regarding the impact of World Heritage status in relation to various
topics, with a particular focus on the World Heritage and Sustainable Development Policy (2015).
第十三章收集关于世界遗产地位对各种议题的影响的信息，特别侧重于世界遗产和可持续发展
政策(2015 年)。
14. GOOD PRACTICES IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE WORLD HERITAGE
CONVENTION
实施世界遗产公约的良好做法
Chapter 14 offers the opportunity to provide an example of a good practice in World Heritage
protection, identification, conservation and preservation implemented at the property level.
第 14 章提供了一个在财产一级实施世界遗产保护、识别、保护和保存的良好做法的例子。
15. ASSESSMENT OF THE PERIODIC REPORTING EXERCISE
15、定期报告评估
Chapter 15 assesses the format, content and process of the Periodic Reporting exercise, including how
the data generated is used and the training and guidance available to respondents.
第 15 章评估了定期报告工作的形式、内容和过程，包括如何使用所产生的数据以及答复者可
获得的培训和指导。

Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 149
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 149
Evaluation criteria for International Assistance requests Annex 9
国际援助请求评估标准附件 9
EVALUATION CRITERIA
评估准则
FOR INTERNATIONAL ASSISTANCE REQUESTS
国际援助请求
The following considerations are to be taken into account by the Advisory Bodies, World Heritage Centre, and
the relevant Decision-maker (the Chairperson of the World Heritage Committee, the World Heritage
Committee or the Director of the World Heritage Centre) when assessing International Assistance requests.
咨询机构、世界遗产中心和有关决策者(世界遗产委员会主席、世界遗产委员会主席或世界遗产中心主
任)在评估国际援助请求时，应考虑以下因素。
These items do not constitute a checklist, and not every item will be applicable to every International
Assistance Request. Rather the appropriate items are to be considered together in an integrated manner in
making balanced judgments concerning the appropriateness of allocating the limited financial support
available through the World Heritage Fund.
这些项目并不构成核对清单，亦不是每个项目都适用于每个国际援助要求。相反，应当综合考虑
适当的项目，对通过世界遗产基金分配有限的财政支助是否适当作出平衡的判断。
A. Eligibility
资格
1. Is the State Party in arrears for payment of its contribution to the World Heritage Fund?
缔约国是否拖欠其对世界遗产基金会的捐款？
2. Is the request coming from an authorized organization/institution of the State Party?
请求是否来自缔约国的授权组织/机构？
B. Priority considerations
优先考虑
3. Is the request from a State Party on the list of the Least Developed Countries (LDCs), Low Income
Economies (LIEs), Small Island Developing States (SIDS) or post-conflict countries?
最不发达国家、低收入经济体、小岛屿发展中国家或冲突后国家名单上的缔约国是否提出请求？
4. Is the property on the List of World Heritage in Danger?
世界遗产名录上的财产是否处于危险之中？
5. Does the request further one or more of the Strategic Objectives of the World Heritage Committee
(Credibility, Conservation, Capacity building, and Communication)?
是否进一步要求世界遗产委员会的一个或多个战略目标(公信力、保护、能力建设和传播) ？
6. Does the request respond to needs identified through the Periodic Reporting process at the property
and/or regional levels?
请求是否回应了在财产和/或区域层面通过定期报告过程确定的需求？
7. Is the request linked to a regional or sub-regional capacity building programme?
请求是否与区域或次区域能力建设方案有关？
8. Is there a capacity building aspect to the activity (no matter what type of assistance sought)?
是否有能力建设方面的活动(无论什么类型的援助寻求) ？
9. Will the lessons learned from the activity provide benefits to the larger World Heritage system?
从这项活动中吸取的经验教训是否会为更大的世界遗产系统带来益处？
C. Considerations linked to the specific content of the proposed activity
与拟议活动的具体内容相关的考虑
10. Are the objectives of the request clearly stated and achievable?
请求的目标是否清楚说明并可达到？
11. Is there a clear work plan for achieving the results, including a timeline for its implementation? Is
the work plan reasonable?
是否有一个明确的工作计划来实现结果，包括实施的时间表？工作计划是否合理？
12. Does the agency/organization responsible for implementing the proposal have the capacity to do so,
and is there a responsible person identified for ongoing contacts?
负责执行该建议的机构/组织是否有能力这样做，是否已确定负责持续接触的人员？
13. Are the professionals proposed to be used (whether national or international) qualified to carry out
the work being requested? Are there clear terms of reference for them, including adequate period of their
involvement?
被提议使用的专业人员(无论是国内的还是国际的)是否有资格执行所要求的工作？他们是否有明
确的职权范围，包括他们参与的足够时间？
14. Is the involvement of all relevant parties taken into account in the proposal (for example
stakeholders, other institutions, etc.)?
建议是否考虑了所有相关各方的参与(例如持份者、其他机构等) ？
15. Are the technical requirements clearly expressed and are they reasonable?
技术要求是否清晰表达，是否合理？
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 150
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 150
Evaluation criteria for International Assistance requests Annex 9
国际援助请求评估标准附件 9
16. Is there a clear plan for reporting the results and for continued monitoring, including appropriate
indicators for success?
是否有报告结果和持续监测的明确计划，包括适当的成功指标？
17. Is there a commitment of the State Party for appropriate follow-up after the activity is completed?
缔约国是否承诺在活动完成后采取适当的后续行动？
D. Budgetary / Financial considerations
预算/财政考虑因素
18. Is the overall budget reasonable for the work that is proposed to be carried out?
总体预算对于拟进行的工作是否合理？
19. Is the budget detailed sufficiently to ensure that the unit costs are reasonable and in line with local
costs and/or UNESCO norms and rules as appropriate?
预算是否足够详细，以确保单位费用合理，并符合当地费用和(或)教科文组织的规范和细则？
20. Does the request act as a catalyst (multiplier) for other funding (are other sources of funding, either
cash or in-kind clearly specified)?
请求是否作为其他资金的催化剂(乘数)(其他资金来源，无论是现金还是实物是否明确指定) ？
E. Considerations for specific types of International Assistance
关于特定类型国际援助的考虑
a) Emergency Assistance Requests
紧急援助请求
21. Does the threat or disaster covered by the request conform to the definition of an emergency within
the Operational Guidelines (unexpected phenomena)?
请求所涵盖的威胁或灾难是否符合业务指南中的紧急情况定义(意外现象) ？
22. Can the proposed intervention be carried out with reasonable safety for those involved with its
implementation?
对于那些参与实施的人来说，所提议的干预措施是否能够在合理的安全条件下实施？
23. Does the intervention respond to the most critical issues related to the protection/conservation of
the property?
干预措施是否针对与保护/养护财产有关的最关键问题作出回应？
b) Preparatory Assistance Requests
预备援助请求
For requests for preparation of nomination files
申请拟备提名档案
24. Is the property on the State Party’s Tentative List?
该财产是否在缔约国的暂定清单上？
25. Does the State Party already have properties inscribed on the World Heritage List? If yes, how many?
缔约国是否已有财产被列入世界遗产名录? 如果是，有多少？
26. Is the type of property proposed for World Heritage listing un-represented or under-represented in
the World Heritage List?
提议列入世界遗产名录的财产类型是否在世界遗产名录中没有代表性或者代表性不足？
27. Is sufficient attention paid to necessary elements, such as the preparation of the management plan,
comparative analysis, Statement of Outstanding Universal Value, mapping, etc.?
是否充分注意必要的因素，如管理计划的编制、比较分析、突出普遍价值的陈述、测绘等。？
28. Is sufficient attention given to community involvement? For requests for preparation of Tentative Lists
是否对社区参与给予了足够的关注? 准备暂定清单的请求
29. Is the process designed to include all the necessary stakeholders and points of view?
这一过程是否旨在包括所有必要的利益相关者和观点？
30. Are both natural and cultural heritage professionals proposed to be involved?
自然和文化遗产专业人士是否都被提议参与？
31. Is the State Party new to the World Heritage Convention?
缔约国是《世界遗产公约》的新缔约国吗？
32. If the request is for harmonization of Tentative Lists, are representatives from all the necessary
States Parties in the region or sub-region involved?
如果要求协调暂定名单，是否涉及区域或次区域所有必要缔约国的代表？
For requests for preparation of other types of assistance
请求准备其他类型的援助
33. If the request is for the preparation of a request for other assistance, is the need for the eventual
request well documented?
如果请求是为了准备其他援助请求，那么最终请求的必要性是否有详细的文件记录？
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 151
执行《世界遗产公约》的业务准则 151
Evaluation criteria for International Assistance requests Annex 9
国际援助请求评估标准附件 9
c) Conservation and Management Assistance Requests
养护和管理援助请求
For requests for conservation work or the preparation of a management plan
要求进行保育工作或准备管理计划
34. Is the property on the World Heritage List?
这处房产在世界遗产名录上吗？
35. Is the work being proposed a priority for protecting or safeguarding the property?
这项工作是否被提议作为保护或保护财产的优先事项？
36. Does the work being proposed conform to best practice? For requests for training activities
所提议的工作是否符合最佳做法
37. Is it clearly related to the implementation of the World Heritage Convention?
它是否与世界遗产公约的实施明确相关？
38. Does it take place on a World Heritage property or involve a visit/case study of a World Heritage
property?
是否在世界遗产财产内进行，或涉及世界遗产财产的参观/个案研究？
39. Does it involve those responsible for conservation at a World Heritage property as trainees or
resource persons?
它是否涉及到那些作为学员或者顾问负责世界遗产保护的人员？
40. Does it respond to well-defined training needs?
它是否符合明确定义的培训需求？
41. Are the training methods appropriate to ensure that the learning objectives will be met?
培训方法是否恰当，以确保学习目标将得到满足？
42. Does it strengthen a local and/or regional training institution?
它是否加强了地方和/或区域培训机构？
43. Is it linked with practical applications in the field?
它是否与该领域的实际应用相关联？
44. Is there a provision for disseminating results and related training materials to other organizations in
the World Heritage system?
是否有向世界遗产系统其他组织传播成果和相关培训材料的规定？
For requests related to scientific research
对于与科学研究相关的请求
45. Can it be demonstrated that the subject matter is of a priority nature for better protection and
safeguarding of World Heritage properties?
是否可以证明，为了更好地保护和保护世界遗产财产，这一主题具有优先性？
46. Can it be demonstrated that the results will be concrete and applicable widely within the World
Heritage system?
能否证明其结果将是具体的，并广泛适用于世界遗产系统？
For requests for educational or awareness activities
要求进行教育或宣传活动
47. Will it help make the World Heritage Convention better known or create a stronger interest in it
amongst the target audience?
它是否有助于使世界遗产公约更加广为人知，或者在目标受众中产生更大的兴趣？
48. Will it create a greater awareness of the different issues related to the implementation of the World
Heritage Convention?
它是否会提高人们对与执行《世界遗产公约》有关的不同问题的认识？
49. Will it promote more involvement in World Heritage Convention related activities?
它会促进更多人参与世界遗产公约相关活动吗？
50. Will it be a means of exchanging experiences or stimulate joint educational and information
programmes, especially amongst school children?
它是否将成为交流经验或促进联合教育和信息方案的一种手段，特别是在学龄儿童中间？
51. Will it produce appropriate awareness materials for the promotion of the World Heritage
Convention for use by the target audience?
它会为宣传世界遗产公约提供适当的宣传材料供目标受众使用吗？

Format of a Statement of Outstanding Universal Value, and of a retrospective Statement of Outstanding

突出普遍价值声明和突出普遍价值回顾性声明的格式。
The retrospective Statement of Outstanding Universal Value should be submitted either in English or in
French. An electronic version (Word or .pdf format) should also be submitted.
杰出普世价值的追溯性声明应该以英文或法文提交。电子版本(Word 或。Pdf 格式)。
A Statement of Outstanding Universal Value should respect the following format (2 A4 pages max):
优异通用值声明应遵循以下格式(最多 2 a4 页) :

Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 153
实施世界遗产公约的操作指南 153
Modifications to World Heritage Properties Annex 11
修改世界遗产附件 11
MODIFICATIONS
修改
TO WORLD HERITAGE PROPERTIES
世界文化遗产
MINOR MODIFICATIONS TO THE BOUNDARIES OF WORLD HERITAGE PROPERTIES
世界遗产地产边界的小修改
Boundary modifications should serve better identification of World Heritage properties and enhance
protection of their Outstanding Universal Value.
修改边界应有助于更好地识别世界遗产财产，并加强对其突出的普遍价值的保护。
A proposal for a minor boundary modification, submitted by the State Party concerned, is subject to the
review of the relevant Advisory Body(ies) and to the approval of the World Heritage Committee.
有关缔约国提出的小规模边界修改提案须经有关咨询机构审查，并须经世界遗产委员会批准。
A proposal for a minor boundary modification can be approved, not approved, or referred by the World
Heritage Committee.
世界遗产委员会可以批准、不批准或转交对边界进行轻微修改的提案。
Documentation requested
所需文件
1) Area of the property (in hectares): please indicate a) the area of the property as inscribed and b) the
area of the property as proposed to be modified (or the area of the proposed buffer zone). (Note that
reductions can be considered as minor modifications only under exceptional circumstances).
物业面积(以公顷为单位) : 请注明: a)物业的登记面积; b)拟议修改的物业面积(或拟议缓冲区的面
积)。(请注意，只有在特殊情况下，减少建筑面积才可视为轻微修改)。
2) Description of the modification: please provide a written description of the proposed change to the
boundary of the property (or a written description of the proposed buffer zone).
修改说明: 请提供对属性边界的拟议更改的书面说明(或拟议的缓冲区的书面说明)。
3) Justification for the modification: please provide a brief summary of the reasons why the
boundaries of the property should be modified (or why a buffer zone is needed), with particular emphasis
on how such modification will improve the conservation and/or protection of the property.
修改的理由: 请简要说明为什么要修改财产的边界(或为什么需要一个缓冲区) ，特别强调这种修改
将如何改进财产的保护和(或)保护。
4) Contribution to the maintenance of the Outstanding Universal Value: please indicate how the
proposed change (or the proposed buffer zone) will contribute to the maintenance of the Outstanding
Universal Value of the property.
对维持尚未实现的普遍价值的贡献: 请说明拟议的变更(或拟议的缓冲区)将如何有助于维持该财产
的尚未实现的普遍价值。
5) Implications for legal protection: please indicate the implications of the proposed change for the
legal protection of the property. In the case of a proposed addition, or of the creation of a buffer zone,
please provide information on the legal protection in place for the area to be added and a copy of relevant
laws and regulations.
对法律保护的影响: 请说明拟议修改对财产法律保护的影响。如果拟议增加或建立缓冲区，请提
供资料，说明为增加区域提供的法律保护情况，并提供有关法律和条例的副本。
6) Implications for management arrangements: please indicate the implications of the proposed
change for the management arrangements of the property. In the case of a proposed addition, or of the
creation of a buffer zone, please provide information on the management arrangements in place for the
area to be added.
对管理安排的影响: 请说明拟议的改变对物业管理安排的影响。如果拟议增加或建立缓冲区，请
提供资料，说明为增加区域而作出的管理安排。
7) Maps: please submit two maps, one clearly showing both delimitations of the property (original and
proposed revision) and the other showing only the proposed revision. In the case of the creation of a
buffer zone, please submit a map showing both the inscribed property and the proposed buffer zone.
地图: 请提交两份地图，一份清楚显示财产的分界线(原始和拟议修订) ，另一份只显示拟议修订。
在创建缓冲区的情况下，请提交一份地图，显示已登记的属性和拟议的缓冲区。
Please make sure that the maps:
请确保地图:
- are either topographic or cadastral;
是地形或地籍;
- are presented at a scale which is appropriate to the size in hectares of the property and sufficient to
clearly show the detail of the current boundary and the proposed changes (and, in any case, the largest
available and practical scale);
以适当的比例(以公顷为单位)展示物业，并足以清楚显示现时界线的详情和拟议的改动(以及
在任何情况下，最大的可用和实用的比例) ;
- have the title and the legend/key in English or French (if this is not possible, please attach a translation);
有英文或法文的标题和图例/钥匙(如果不可能，请附上译文) ;
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 154
实施世界遗产公约的操作指南 154
Modifications to World Heritage Properties Annex 11
修改世界遗产附件 11
- mark the boundaries of the property (current and proposed revision) through a clearly visible line
that can be distinguished from other features on the maps;
以清晰可见的界线标示物业(现时及拟议修订)的界线，以区别于地图上的其他地貌;
- bear a clearly labeled coordinate grid (or coordinate ticks);
有一个明确标记的坐标网格(或坐标刻度) ;
- clearly refer (in the title and in the legend) to the boundary of the World Heritage property (and to
the buffer zone of the World Heritage property, if applicable). Please clearly distinguish the boundary of
the World Heritage property from any other protected area boundaries.
清楚地指出(在标题和图例中)世界遗产财产的边界(以及世界遗产财产的缓冲区，如果适用)。
请清楚区分世界遗产的界线与其他保护区的界线。
8) Additional information: In the case of a proposed addition, please submit some photographs of the
area to be added that provide information on its key values and conditions of authenticity/integrity.
附加信息: 如果建议增建，请提交一些拟增建区域的照片，提供关于其主要价值观和真实性/完整
性条件的信息。
Any other relevant document can be submitted such as thematic maps (e.g. vegetation maps), summaries
of scientific information concerning the values of the area to be added (e.g. species lists), and supporting
bibliographies.
任何其他相关文件均可提交，例如专题地图(例如植被图)、有关拟增加地区价值的科学资料摘要
(例如物种清单) ，以及辅助参考书目。
The above-mentioned documentation should be submitted in English or French in two identical copies
(three for mixed properties). An electronic version (the maps in formats such as .jpg, .tif, .pdf) should also
be submitted.
上述文件应以英文或法文提交两份相同的副本(三份为混合性质)。电子版本(地图格式如。图片。
蒂夫。Pdf).

OF THE WORLD HERITAGE EMBLEM
世界遗产徽章
This table was prepared on the basis of Chapter VIII of the Operational Guidelines of the World
Heritage Convention and the Directives Concerning the Use of the Name, Acronym, Logo and Internet
Domain Names of UNESCO (Resolution 34C/86).
本表是根据《世界遗产公约业务准则》第八章和教科文组织关于使用名称、首字母缩略词、徽
标和互联网域名的指示(第 34c/86 号决议)编制的。
Reminder concerning the authority and delegation of authority for the use of the World Heritage
Emblem according to Chapter VIII of the Operational Guidelines:
关于根据《业务准则》第八章使用世界遗产徽章的授权和授权的提醒:
Para. 262:
第 262 段:
"The World Heritage Committee is responsible for determining the use of the World Heritage Emblem
and for making policy prescriptions regarding how it may be used."
世界遗产委员会负责决定世界遗产徽章的使用，并就如何使用世界遗产徽章制定政策规定
Para. 276:
第 276 段:
"National authorities may grant the use of the Emblem to a national entity, provided that the project,
whether national or international, involves only World Heritage properties located on the same
national territory. National authorities’ decision should be guided by the Guidelines and Principles."
”国家当局可准许国家实体使用徽章，条件是该项目，无论是国家的还是国际的，只涉及位于
同一国家领土上的世界遗产财产。国家当局的决定应该遵循指南和原则。”
Para. 278:
第 278 段:
Any other request must be addressed to the Director of the World Heritage Centre, who has the authority
to grant the use of the Emblem in accordance with the Guidelines and Principles.
任何其他请求必须向世界文化遗产中心主任提出，他有权根据准则和原则批准使用会徽。
For cases not covered, or not sufficiently covered, by the Guidelines and Principles and by the Table of
Uses, the Director refers the matter to the Chairperson who, in the most difficult cases, might wish to
refer the matter to the Committee for final decision.
对于准则和原则以及用途表没有涵盖或没有充分涵盖的情况，主任将此事项提交主席，在最困
难的情况下，主席可能希望将此事项提交委员会作出最后决定。
Reminder concerning the use of the linked logo and of the stand alone Emblem:
关于使用链接标志和独立标志的提醒:
Para. 262:
第 262 段:
Since the adoption by the UNESCO General Conference in October 2007 of the Directives concerning
the Use of the Name, Acronym, Logo and Internet Domain Names of UNESCO, it is strongly encouraged
to use the World Heritage Emblem as part of a linked logo block accompanied by UNESCO’s logo,
whenever feasible. When the emblem is used in a linked logo block with the UNESCO logo, the graphical
standards of the UNESCO Secretariat must be strictly followed. The use of the World Heritage Emblem
alone remains however possible, in line with the present Guidelines and with the Table of Uses (Annex
14 of the Guidelines).
自 2007 年 10 月教科文组织大会通过关于使用教科文组织名称、首字母缩略词、徽标和因特网域
名的指示以来，大力鼓励在可行的情况下使用世界遗产徽标作为与教科文组织徽标相连接的徽标
块的一部分。当徽章与联合国教科文组织的标志连接在一起时，必须严格遵守联合国教科文组织
秘书处的图形标准。然而，根据本准则和用途表(准则附件 14) ，仅使用世界遗产徽章仍然是可能
的。

Reminder concerning the use of the UNESCO logo:
有关使用联合国教科文组织标志的提示:

有关使用教科文组织标志的资料可在此查阅:
http://en.unesco.org/logopatronage
Http://en.unesco. org/logopatronage
According to the Preamble of Chapter VIII of the Operational Guidelines, the stand alone World Heritage
Emblem can be used in any colour or size. However, when the emblem is used in a linked logo block with
the UNESCO logo, the graphical standards of the UNESCO Secretariat must be strictly followed.
根据业务准则第八章序言，独立的世界遗产徽章可以使用任何颜色或大小。然而，当徽章与联合国
教科文组织的标志连接在一起时，必须严格遵守联合国教科文组织秘书处的图形标准。
The logos are provided by the authorizing entities (as detailed in the following table) in digital format
which cannot be modified by the users in any way.
标志由授权实体(详见下表)以数字格式提供，用户不得以任何方式修改。
It is obligatory to submit the draft layout of the intended use to the authorizing entity for validation
before production.
在生产之前，必须向授权实体提交预期用途的布局草案，以供审定。
Definition of commercial use:
商业用途的定义:
The sale of goods or services bearing the name, acronym, logo and/or Internet domain name of
UNESCO combined with the World Heritage Emblem chiefly for profit shall be regarded as
“commercial use” for the purpose of the Operational Guidelines. Such use must be expressly authorized
by the Director-General, under a specific contractual arrangement (definition adapted from UNESCO
Logo Directives 2007. Art III.2.1.3)
出售带有教科文组织名称、首字母缩略词、标志和(或)因特网域名与世界遗产徽章相结合的货物
或服务，主要是为了牟利，应被视为《业务准则》所指的”商业用途”。这种使用必须明确授权
总干事，在一个具体的合同安排(定义改编自教科文组织标志指令 2007 年。第三部分 2.1.3)

Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 11
I INTRODUCTION
I.A The Operational Guidelines
1. The Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage
Convention (hereinafter referred to as the Operational Guidelines) aim to
facilitate the implementation of the Convention concerning the Protection of
the World Cultural and Natural Heritage (hereinafter referred to as “the
World Heritage Convention” or “the Convention”), by setting forth the
procedures for:
a) the inscription of properties on the World Heritage List and the List
of World Heritage in Danger;
b) the protection and conservation of World Heritage properties;
c) the granting of International Assistance under the World Heritage
Fund; and
d) the mobilization of national and international support in favor of the
Convention.
2. The Operational Guidelines are periodically revised to reflect the decisions
of the World Heritage Committee.
3. The key users of the Operational Guidelines are:
a) the States Parties to the World Heritage Convention;
b) the Intergovernmental Committee for the Protection of the Cultural
and Natural Heritage of Outstanding Universal Value, hereinafter
referred to as “the World Heritage Committee” or “the Committee”;
c) the UNESCO World Heritage Centre as Secretariat to the World
Heritage Committee, hereinafter referred to as “the Secretariat”;
d) the Advisory Bodies to the World Heritage Committee;
e) site managers, stakeholders and partners in the protection of World
Heritage properties.
I.B The World Heritage Convention
4. The cultural and natural heritage is among the priceless and irreplaceable
assets, not only of each nation, but of humanity as a whole. The loss, through
deterioration or disappearance, of any of these most prized assets constitutes
an impoverishment of the heritage of all the peoples of the world. Parts of
this heritage, because of their exceptional qualities, can be considered to be
of “Outstanding Universal Value” and as such worthy of special protection
against the dangers which increasingly threaten them.
The historical development of
the Operational Guidelines is
available at:
https://whc.unesco.org/en/guidelines/
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 12
5. To ensure, as far as possible, the proper identification, protection,
conservation and presentation of the world's heritage, the Member States of
UNESCO adopted the World Heritage Convention in 1972. The Convention
foresees the establishment of a “World Heritage Committee” and a “World
Heritage Fund”. Both the Committee and the Fund have been in operation
since 1976.
6. Since the adoption of the Convention in 1972, the international community
has embraced the concept of “sustainable development”. The protection and
conservation of the natural and cultural heritage constitute a significant
contribution to sustainable development.
7. The Convention aims at the identification, protection, conservation,
presentation and transmission to future generations of cultural and natural
heritage of Outstanding Universal Value.
8. The criteria and conditions for the inscription of properties on the World
Heritage List have been developed to evaluate the Outstanding Universal
Value of properties and to guide States Parties in the protection and
management of World Heritage properties.
9. When a property inscribed on the World Heritage List is threatened by
serious and specific dangers, the Committee considers placing it on the List
of World Heritage in Danger. When the Outstanding Universal Value of the
property which justified its inscription on the World Heritage List is lost, the
Committee considers deleting the property from the World Heritage List.
I.C The States Parties to the World Heritage Convention
10. States are encouraged to become party to the Convention. Model instruments
for ratification/acceptance and accession are included as Annex 1. The
original signed version should be sent to the Director-General of UNESCO.
11. The list of States Parties to the Convention is available at:
https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties
12. States Parties to the Convention are encouraged to adopt a human-rights
based approach, and ensure gender-balanced participation of a wide variety
of stakeholders and rights-holders, including site managers, local and
regional governments, local communities, indigenous peoples, non-
governmental organizations (NGOs) and other interested parties and partners
in the identification, nomination, management and protection processes of
World Heritage properties.
13. States Parties to the Convention should provide the Secretariat with the
names and contact details of the governmental organization(s) primarily
responsible as national focal point(s) for the implementation of the
Convention, so that copies of all official correspondence and documents can
be sent by the Secretariat to these national focal points as appropriate.
14. States Parties are encouraged to bring together their cultural and natural
heritage experts at regular intervals to discuss the implementation of the
Convention. States Parties may wish to involve representatives of the
Advisory Bodies and other experts and partners as appropriate.
Decision 43 COM 11A
Decision 43 COM 11A
Decision 43 COM 11A
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 13
14bis. States Parties are encouraged to mainstream into their programmes and
activities related to the World Heritage Convention the principles of the
relevant policies adopted by the World Heritage Committee, the General
Assembly of States Parties to the Convention and the UNESCO Governing
Bodies, such as the Policy Document for the Integration of a Sustainable
Development Perspective into the Processes of the World Heritage
Convention and the UNESCO policy on engaging with indigenous peoples,
as well as other related policies and documents, including the 2030 Agenda
for Sustainable Development and international human rights standards.
15. While fully respecting the sovereignty of the States on whose territory the
cultural and natural heritage is situated, States Parties to the Convention
recognize the collective interest of the international community to cooperate
in the protection of this heritage. States Parties to the World Heritage
Convention, have the responsibility to:
a) ensure the identification, nomination, protection, conservation,
presentation, and transmission to future generations of the cultural
and natural heritage found within their territory, and give help in
these tasks to other States Parties that request it;
b) adopt general policies to give the heritage a function in the life of
the community;
c) integrate heritage protection into comprehensive planning
programmes and coordination mechanisms, giving consideration in
particular to the resilience of socio-ecological systems of properties;
d) establish services for the protection, conservation and presentation
of the heritage;
e) develop scientific and technical studies to identify actions that
would counteract the dangers that threaten the heritage;
f) take appropriate legal, scientific, technical, administrative and
financial measures to protect the heritage;
g) foster the establishment or development of national or regional
centres for training in the protection, conservation and presentation

protection of World Heritage;
l) give assistance to international fundraising campaigns organized for
the World Heritage Fund;

I.E The World Heritage Committee
19. The World Heritage Committee is composed of 21 members and meets at
least once a year (June/July). It establishes its Bureau, which meets during
the sessions of the Committee as frequently as deemed necessary. The
composition of the Committee and its Bureau is available at:
https://whc.unesco.org/en/committee
20. The Committee manages its meetings according to its Rules of Procedure,
available at: https://whc.unesco.org/en/committee
21. The term of office of Committee members is six years but, in order to ensure
equitable representation and rotation, States Parties are invited by the General
Assembly to consider voluntarily reducing their term of office from six to
four years and are discouraged from seeking consecutive terms of office.
22. At each election, due consideration shall be given to the election of at least
one State Party which has never served as a Member of the World Heritage
Committee.

carried out. The Committee recognizes that such decisions depend upon:

1 Reactive Monitoring missions are part of the statutory reporting by the Secretariat and the Advisory Bodies to the World
Heritage Committee on the state of conservation of specific properties that are under threat (see Paragraph 169). They are
requested by the World Heritage Committee to ascertain, in consultation with the State Party concerned, the condition of the
property, the dangers to the property and the feasibility of adequately restoring the property or to assess progress made in
implementing such corrective measures, and include a reporting back to the Committee on the findings of the mission (see
Paragraph 176.e). The terms of reference of Reactive Monitoring missions are proposed by the World Heritage Centre, in
line with the decision adopted by the World Heritage Committee, and consolidated in consultation with the State Party and
the relevant Advisory Body(ies). Experts for such missions shall not be nationals of the country where the property is located.
It is however encouraged that, where possible, they be from the same region as the property. The costs of the Reactive
Monitoring missions are borne by the World Heritage Fund.
2 Advisory missions are not part stricto sensu of the statutory and mandatory processes, as they are voluntarily initiated by
States Parties and depend on the considerations and judgement of the States Parties requesting them. Advisory missions are
to be understood as missions providing expert advice to a State Party on specific matters. They can concern provision of
“upstream” support and advice on identification of sites, Tentative Lists or nomination of sites for inscription on the World
Heritage List or alternatively, they can relate to the state of conservation of properties and provide advice in evaluating
possible impact of a major development project on the Outstanding Universal Value of the property, advice in the
preparation/revision of a management plan, or in the progress achieved in the implementation of specific mitigation measures,
etc. The terms of reference of Advisory missions are proposed by the State Party itself, and consolidated in consultation with
the World Heritage Centre and the relevant Advisory Bod(ies), other organization(s) or experts. Experts for such missions
shall not be nationals of the country where the property is located. It is however encouraged that, where possible, they be
from the same region as the property. The entire costs of Advisory missions are borne by the State Party inviting the mission,
except where the State Party is eligible for relevant International Assistance or funding from the new budget line for Advisory
missions approved by Decision 38 COM 12.

ICCROM
32. ICCROM (the International Centre for the Study of the Preservation and

organization with headquarters in Rome, Italy. Established by UNESCO in
1956, ICCROM's statutory functions are to carry out research,
documentation, technical assistance, training and public awareness
programmes to strengthen conservation of immovable and moveable cultural
heritage.
33. The specific role of ICCROM in relation to the Convention includes: being
the priority partner in training for cultural heritage, monitoring the state of
conservation of World Heritage cultural properties, reviewing requests for
International Assistance submitted by States Parties, and providing input and
support for capacity building activities.
ICOMOS
34. ICOMOS (the International Council on Monuments and Sites) is a non-
governmental organization with headquarters in Charenton-le-Pont, France.
Founded in 1965, its role is to promote the application of theory,
methodology and scientific techniques to the conservation of the
architectural and archaeological heritage. Its work is based on the principles
of the 1964 International Charter on the Conservation and Restoration of
Monuments and Sites (the Venice Charter).
35. The specific role of ICOMOS in relation to the Convention includes:
evaluation of properties nominated for inscription on the World Heritage List,
monitoring the state of conservation of World Heritage cultural properties,
reviewing requests for International Assistance submitted by States Parties,
and providing input and support for capacity building activities.

I.I Partners in the protection of World Heritage
39. A partnership approach, underpinned by inclusive, transparent and

provides a significant contribution to the protection of World Heritage
properties and the implementation of the Convention.
40. Partners in the protection and conservation of World Heritage can be those
individuals and other stakeholders, especially local communities, indigenous
peoples, governmental, non-governmental and private organizations and
owners who have an interest and involvement in the conservation and
management of a World Heritage property.

II THE WORLD HERITAGE LIST
II.A Definition of World Heritage
Cultural and Natural Heritage
45. Cultural and natural heritage are defined in Articles 1 and 2 of the World
Heritage Convention.
Article 1
For the purposes of this Convention, the following shall be considered as
“cultural heritage”;
- monuments: architectural works, works of monumental sculpture and
painting, elements or structures of an archaeological nature, inscriptions,
cave dwellings and combinations of features, which are of Outstanding
Universal Value from the point of view of history, art or science;
- groups of buildings: groups of separate or connected buildings which,
because of their architecture, their homogeneity or their place in the
landscape, are of Outstanding Universal Value from the point of view of
history, art or science;
- sites: works of man or the combined works of nature and of man, and areas
including archaeological sites which are of Outstanding Universal Value
from the historical, aesthetic, ethnological or anthropological points of view.
Article 2
For the purposes of this Convention, the following shall be considered as
“natural heritage”:
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 22
- natural features consisting of physical and biological formations or groups
of such formations, which are of Outstanding Universal Value from the
aesthetic or scientific point of view;
geological and physiographical formations and precisely delineated areas
which constitute the habitat of threatened species of animals and plants of
Outstanding Universal Value from the point of view of science or
conservation;
- natural sites or precisely delineated natural areas of Outstanding Universal
Value from the point of view of science, conservation or natural beauty.
Mixed Cultural and Natural Heritage
46. Properties shall be considered as “mixed cultural and natural heritage” if they
satisfy a part or whole of the definitions of both cultural and natural heritage
laid out in Articles 1 and 2 of the Convention.
Cultural landscapes
Definition
47. Cultural landscapes inscribed on the World Heritage List are cultural
properties and represent the “combined works of nature and of man”
designated in Article 1 of the Convention. They are illustrative of the
evolution of human society and settlement over time, under the influence of
the physical constraints and/or opportunities presented by their natural
environment and of successive social, economic and cultural forces, both
external and internal.
They should be selected on the basis both of their Outstanding Universal
Value and of their representativity in terms of a clearly defined geo-cultural
region. They should be selected also for their capacity to illustrate the
essential and distinct cultural elements of such regions.
The term “cultural landscape” embraces a diversity of manifestations of the
interaction between humankind and the natural environment.
Cultural landscapes often reflect specific techniques of sustainable land use,
considering the characteristics and limits of the natural environment they are
established in, and may reflect a specific spiritual relationship to nature.
Protection of cultural landscapes can contribute to current techniques of
sustainable land use and can maintain or enhance natural values in the
landscape. The continued existence of traditional forms of land use supports
biological diversity in many regions of the world. The protection of
traditional cultural landscapes is therefore helpful in maintaining biological
diversity.
Types
47bis. Cultural landscapes fall into three main types, namely:
(i) The most easily identifiable is the clearly defined landscape designed
and created intentionally by people. This embraces garden and
parkland landscapes constructed for aesthetic reasons which are often
(but not always) associated with religious or other monumental
buildings and ensembles.
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 23
(ii) The second type is the organically evolved landscape. This results
from an initial social, economic, administrative, and/or religious
imperative and has developed its present form by association with and
in response to its natural environment. Such landscapes reflect that
process of evolution in their form and component features. They fall
into two sub-types:
a) a relict (or fossil) landscape is one in which an evolutionary
process came to an end at some time in the past, either abruptly
or over a period. Its significant distinguishing features are,
however, still visible in material form;
b) a continuing landscape is one which retains an active social role
in contemporary society closely associated with the traditional
way of life, and in which the evolutionary process is still in
progress. At the same time it exhibits significant material
evidence of its evolution over time;
(iii) The final type is the associative cultural landscape. The inscription of
such landscapes on the World Heritage List is justifiable by virtue of
the powerful religious, artistic or cultural associations of the natural
element rather than material cultural evidence, which may be
insignificant or even absent.
Inscription of Cultural Landscapes on the World Heritage List
47ter. The extent of a cultural landscape for inscription on the World Heritage List
is relative to its functionality and intelligibility. In any case, the sample
selected must be substantial enough to represent adequately the totality of
the cultural landscape that it illustrates. The possibility of designating long
linear areas which represent culturally significant transport and
communication networks should not be excluded.
General criteria for protection and management are equally applicable to
cultural landscapes. It is important that due attention be paid to the full range
of values represented in the landscape, both cultural and natural. The
nominations should be prepared in collaboration with and the full approval
of local communities.
The existence of a category of “cultural landscape”, included on the World
Heritage List on the basis of the criteria set out in Paragraph 77 of the
Operational Guidelines, does not exclude the possibility of properties of
exceptional importance in relation to both cultural and natural criteria
continuing to be inscribed (see definition of mixed properties as set out in
Paragraph 46). In such cases, their Outstanding Universal Value must be
justified under both cultural and natural criteria (see Paragraph 77).
Movable Heritage
48. Nominations of immovable heritage which are likely to become movable
will not be considered.
Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the World Heritage Convention 24
Outstanding Universal Value
49. Outstanding Universal Value means cultural and/or natural significance
which is so exceptional as to transcend national boundaries and to be of
common importance for present and future generations of all humanity. As
such, the permanent protection of this heritage is of the highest importance
to the international community as a whole. The Committee defines the
criteria for the inscription of properties on the World Heritage List.
50. States Parties are invited to submit nominations of properties of cultural
and/or natural value considered to be of “Outstanding Universal Value” for
inscription on the World Heritage List.
51. At the time of inscription of a property on the World Heritage List, the
Committee adopts a Statement of Outstanding Universal Value (see
paragraph 154) which will be the key reference for the future effective
protection and management of the property.
52. The Convention is not intended to ensure the protection of all properties of
great interest, importance or value, but only for a select list of the most
outstanding of these from an international viewpoint. It is not to be assumed
that a property of national and/or regional importance will automatically be
inscribed on the World Heritage List.
53. Nominations presented to the Committee shall demonstrate the full
commitment of the State Party to preserve the heritage concerned, within its
means. Such commitment shall take the form of appropriate policy, legal,
scientific, technical, administrative and financial measures adopted and
proposed to protect the property and its Outstanding Universal Value.
II.B A Representative, Balanced and Credible World Heritage List
54. The Committee seeks to establish a representative, balanced and credible
World Heritage List in conformity with the four Strategic Objectives it
adopted at its 26th session (Budapest, 2002).
The Global Strategy for a Representative, Balanced and Credible World
Heritage List
55. The Global Strategy for a Representative, Balanced and Credible World
Heritage List is designed to identify and fill the major gaps in the World
Heritage List. It does this by encouraging more countries to become States
Parties to the Convention and to develop Tentative Lists as defined in
paragraph 62 and nominations of properties for inscription on the World

59. To promote the establishment of a representative, balanced and credible

a) spacing voluntarily their nominations according to conditions that
they will define, and/or;
b) proposing only properties falling into categories still under-
represented, and/or;
c) linking each of their nominations with a nomination presented by a
State Party whose heritage is under-represented; or
d) deciding, on a voluntary basis, to suspend the presentation of new
nominations.

II.C Tentative Lists
Procedure and Format
62. A Tentative List is an inventory of those sites situated on its territory which
each State Party considers suitable for nomination to the World Heritage List.
States Parties should therefore include, in their Tentative Lists, details of
those sites which they consider to be of potential Outstanding Universal
Value and which they intend to nominate during the following years.
63. A nomination dossier will not be considered complete unless the nominated
property has already been included on the State Party's Tentative List and has
undergone a Preliminary Assessment.
64. States Parties are encouraged to prepare their Tentative Lists with the full,
effective and gender-balanced participation of a wide variety of stakeholders
and rights-holders, including site managers, local and regional governments,
local communities, indigenous peoples, NGOs and other interested parties
and partners. In the case of sites affecting the lands, territories or resources
of indigenous peoples, States Parties shall consult and cooperate in good faith
with the indigenous peoples concerned through their own representative
institutions in order to obtain their free, prior and informed consent before
including the sites on their Tentative List.
65. States Parties shall submit Tentative Lists to the Secretariat, at least one year
prior to the submission of a Preliminary Assessment request to the Secretariat
for review by the Advisory Bodies. States Parties are encouraged to re-
examine and re-submit their Tentative List at least every ten years.
66. States Parties are requested to submit their Tentative Lists in English or
French using the standard formats in Annex 2A and Annex 2B (for
transnational and transboundary future nominations), containing the name of
the sites, their geographical location, a brief description of the sites, and
justification of their potential Outstanding Universal Value.
67. The original duly signed version of the completed Tentative List shall be
submitted by the State Party, to:

Tentative Lists as a planning and evaluation tool

provide an indication of future nominations.
71. Tentative Lists should be established selectively and on the basis of evidence

IUCN to identify the gaps in the World Heritage List. These analyses could

bio-geographic provinces for prospective World Heritage properties. States
Parties are encouraged to seek as early as possible upstream advice from the
Advisory Bodies during the development of their Tentative Lists as

as well as by other technical studies performed by the Advisory Bodies and
qualified organizations and individuals. A list of studies already completed
is available at: https://whc.unesco.org/en/globalstrategy

73. States Parties are encouraged to harmonize their Tentative Lists at regional
and thematic levels. Harmonization of Tentative Lists is the process whereby
States Parties, with the assistance of the Advisory Bodies, collectively assess
their respective Tentative List to review gaps and identify common themes.
The harmonization has considerable potential to generate fruitful dialogue
between States Parties and different cultural communities, promoting respect
for common heritage and cultural diversity and can result in improved
Tentative Lists, new nominations from States Parties and cooperation
amongst groups of States Parties in the preparation of nominations.

II.D Criteria for the assessment of Outstanding Universal Value
77. The Committee considers a property as having Outstanding Universal Value
(see paragraphs 49-53) if the property meets one or more of the following
criteria. Nominated properties shall therefore:
(i) represent a masterpiece of human creative genius;
(ii) exhibit an important interchange of human values, over a span of time
or within a cultural area of the world, on developments in architecture
or technology, monumental arts, town-planning or landscape design;
(iii) bear a unique or at least exceptional testimony to a cultural tradition or
to a civilization which is living or which has disappeared;
(iv) be an outstanding example of a type of building, architectural or
technological ensemble or landscape which illustrates (a) significant
stage(s) in human history;
(v) be an outstanding example of a traditional human settlement, land-use,
or sea-use which is representative of a culture (or cultures), or human
interaction with the environment especially when it has become
vulnerable under the impact of irreversible change;
(vi) be directly or tangibly associated with events or living traditions, with
ideas, or with beliefs, with artistic and literary works of outstanding
universal significance. (The Committee considers that this criterion
should preferably be used in conjunction with other criteria);
Decision 24 COM VI.2.3.5(ii)
These criteria were formerly
presented as two separate sets of
criteria - criteria (i) - (vi) for
cultural heritage and (i) - (iv) for

The 6th extraordinary session of

decided to merge the ten criteria
(Decision 6 EXT.COM 5.1)
